orig.explanation: E Recurrent small pulmonary embolisms Pulmonary HTN from capillary bed loss; recurrent PEs cause precapillary arteriolar remodeling.

stem: A 26-year-old woman with idiopathic (primary) pulmonary arterial hypertension is evaluated for therapy. Which of the following therapies may be indicated?
explanation: Bosentan (endothelin receptor antagonist) treats PAH; others are PDE-5 inhibitors, riociguat and prostacyclin agents. Monitor LFTs.

orig.stem: A 26 year old woman with a diagnosis of primary pulmonary hypertension is evaluated for therapy. Which of the following therapies may be indicated?
orig.explanation: Bosentan Bosentan, an endothelin receptor antagonist, is used in primary pulmonary hypertension.

stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with worsening breathlessness and palpitations. Examination shows an elevated JVP, and the chest X-ray shows prominent proximal pulmonary arteries with a paucity of peripheral vascular markings. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
options: Dysfunctional breathing studies and Nijmegen questionnaire
explanation: Raised JVP with pruned peripheral vessels suggests pulmonary hypertension; transthoracic echo is the first test, then RHC.

orig.stem: A 24 year old woman presents with worsening breathlessness and palpitations. Examination shows elevated JVP and a paucity of peripheral vasculature on CXR. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
options: Dysfunctional breathing studies and Nijmegen questionnaire
orig.explanation: Transthoracic echocardiography Echocardiography is indicated to evaluate for pulmonary hypertension or cardiac causes.

stem: A 23 year old woman diagnosed with primary pulmonary hypertension is evaluated for therapy. Which of the following therapies may be indicated?

orig.stem: A 23 year old woman diagnosed with primary pulmonary hypertension is evaluated for therapy. Which of the following therapies may be indicated?
orig.explanation: CT chest, abdomen, pelvis The mediastinal widening and pleural effusion suggest a lympho matous process; CT is required for further evaluation and tissue sampling.

stem: Which of the following sets of pulmonary function test results is most consistent with heritable (familial) pulmonary arterial hypertension?
options: Increased TLC, decreased vital capacity, decreased FEV1/FVC ratio
Decreased TLC, decreased VC, decreased RV, increased FEV1/FVC ratio, normal MIP
Decreased TLC, increased RV, normal FEV1/FVC ratio, decreased MIP
Normal TLC, normal RV, normal FEV1/FVC ratio, normal MIP
explanation: PAH is vascular, so volumes, spirometry and muscle strength are normal; the typical abnormality is an isolated low DLCO.

orig.stem: Which of the following pulmonary function test results is consistent with Familial pulmonary hypertension?
options: Increased TLC, decreased vital capacity, de creased FEV1/FVC ratio
Decreased TLC, decreased VC, decreased RV, increased FEV1/FVC ratio, normal MIP
Decreased TLC, increased RV, normal FEV1/ FVC ratio, decreased MIP
Normal TLC, normal RV, normal FEV1/FVC ratio, normal MIP
orig.explanation: PET scan In a nodule >8 mm in an at-risk patient, PET scan is indicated to assess metabolic activity.

stem: A 47-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and right heart failure despite maximal medical therapy is referred for transplantation. Which of the following statements is true?
options: Patients with idiopathic PAH have worse 5-year survival after transplantation than all other recipient groups
Single-lung transplantation is the preferred procedure
Her right ventricular function will recover after lung transplantation
She is at high risk of recurrent PAH in the transplanted lungs
explanation: RV dysfunction in PAH recovers after bilateral lung transplantation as afterload falls; heart–lung only for complex disease.

orig.stem: A 47-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and right heart failure is referred for transplant. Which is true?
options: iPAH patients have worse 5-year survival than all others.
Her own RV function will recover after lung transplant.
She is at high risk of recurrent PAH post-transplant.
orig.explanation: Her own right ventricular function will recover after lung transplantation Lung transplantation can result in significant recovery of RV function by reducing pulmonary vascular resistance.

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with SOB and chest pain. She comments that she has recently travelled to Australia. An electrocardiogram demonstrates evidence of right heart strain. You suspect a pulmonary embolus. Which investigation is most likely to lead to a diagnosis?

orig.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with SOB and chest pain. She comments that she has recently travelled to Australia. An electrocardiogram demonstrates evidence of right heart strain. You suspect a pulmonary embolus. Which investigation is most likely to lead to a diagnosis?
orig.explanation: CT pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) CTPA has the best diagnostic accuracy for pulmonary embolism; if contraindicated, a V/Q scan may be considered.

stem: A 40-year-old woman has had increasing fatigue and breathlessness for several years. Chest X-ray shows right ventricular enlargement and enlarged central pulmonary arteries. Pulmonary embolism has been excluded by CT pulmonary angiography, and other causes of pulmonary hypertension have been ruled out. Right heart catheterisation shows a pulmonary artery pressure of 75/30 mmHg. What is the best next step in management?
options: Acute drug testing with short-acting pulmonary vasodilators
explanation: In idiopathic PAH, perform acute vasoreactivity testing at RHC; the ~10% responders get high-dose CCBs, others combination PAH therapy.

orig.stem: A 40-year-old woman has had increasing fatigue and shortness of breath for years. Chest x-ray shows right ventricular hypertrophy and enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries. Pulmonary embolus is ruled out by spiral CT scan. Other causes of pulmonary hypertension have also been ruled out. Right heart catheterization reveals a pulmonary artery pressure of 75/30 mm Hg. Which of the following is the best next step in the management of the patient?
options: Acute drug testing with short-acting pulmonary vasodilators
orig.explanation: Acute drug testing with short-acting pulmonary vasodilators Confirmed PAH → acute vasoreactivity testing; CCBs if responsive; otherwise prostacyclin, PDE-5i, ERA; transplant for refractory advanced disease.

stem: A 35-year-old woman complains of slowly progressive breathlessness. She has no cough, sputum, pleuritic chest pain or history of thrombophlebitis, but has taken appetite suppressants at various times. Examination reveals a raised JVP, a palpable right ventricular heave and a loud P2. The chest X-ray shows clear lung fields, oxygen saturation is 94% and the ECG shows right axis deviation. A perfusion lung scan is normal, with no segmental defects. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Pulmonary hypertension with clear lungs, normal perfusion scan and prior appetite suppressants is drug-induced PAH; confirm by RHC.

orig.stem: A 35-year-old female complains of slowly progressive dyspnea. Her past history is nega tive, and there is no cough, sputum production, pleuritic chest pain, or thrombophlebitis. She has taken appetite suppressants at different times. Physical examination reveals jugular venous distention, a palpable right ventricular lift, and a loud P2 heart sound. Chest x-ray shows clear lung fields. Oxygen saturation is 94%. ECG shows right axis deviation. A perfusion lung scan is normal, with no segmental deficits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Primary pulmonary hypertension Young woman with appetite suppressant use, dyspnea, normal perfusion scan → primary PAH; exclude CTEPH; echo shows RV pressure overload; O₂ noncorrective shunt unlikely.

stem: 19-A 30-year-old woman presents with shortness of breath. This began insidiously over several months. She has no cough and no chest pain. Spirometry shows a restrictive pattern. Arterial blood gases reveal hypoxia and hypercapnia; a lung perfusion scan is normal. Right heart catheterisation reveals that right-sided pressures are markedly raised. Which diagnosis best fits with this clinical picture?

orig.stem: 19-A 30-year-old woman presents with shortness of breath. This began insidiously over several months. She has no cough and no chest pain. Spirometry shows a restrictive pattern. Arterial blood gases reveal hypoxia and hypercapnia; a lung perfusion scan is normal. Right heart catheterisation reveals that right-sided pressures are markedly raised. Which diagnosis best fits with this clinical picture?
orig.explanation: E Whispering pectoriloguy Whispering pectoriloquy → consolidation from tumor and retained secretions; likely bronchial carcinoma → get endobronchial biopsy.

stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with breathlessness that has increased over several months. She has peripheral oedema and clinical evidence of right-sided heart failure without signs of left ventricular failure. She is a non-smoker with no chronic cough or sputum, and her chest X-ray lung fields and spirometry are normal. What is the most likely cause of her cor pulmonale?
explanation: Cor pulmonale with normal lung fields and spirometry suggests CTEPH from recurrent small emboli; V/Q scan, endarterectomy may cure.

orig.stem: 21-A 50-year-old woman patient presents with increasing dyspnoea. She has peripheral oedema and clinical evidence of right-sided heart failure without signs of left ventricular failure. What is the most likely cause for the cor pulmonale?
orig.explanation: Recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis Recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis causes hoarseness rather than dyspnea.

stem: A 73-year-old heavy smoker man with bronchial carcinoma developed nausea, vomiting, irritability and confusion. Investigations revealed Hb 9.8 g/dl, serum Na+ 104 mEq/L (normal 135–145 mEq/L). Which of the following is the most probable cause?

orig.stem: A 73-year-old heavy smoker man with bronchial carcinoma developed nausea, vomiting, irritability and confusion. Investigations revealed Hb 9.8 g/dl, serum Na+ 104 mEq/L (normal 135–145 mEq/L). Which of the following is the most probable cause?
orig.explanation: SIADH Small cell lung cancer commonly causes paraneoplastic SIADH leading to severe hyponatremia.

stem: A 73-year-old heavy smoker man with bronchial carcinoma consults a physician because of progressive confusion and lethargy. Blood tests reveal serum Na+ 104 mEq/L, and chest imaging shows a central lung mass. Which paraneoplastic syndrome is most likely responsible?

orig.stem: A 73-year-old heavy smoker man with bronchial carcinoma consults a physician because of progressive confusion and lethargy. Blood tests reveal serum Na+ 104 mEq/L, and chest imaging shows a central lung mass. Which paraneoplastic syndrome is most likely responsible?
orig.explanation: SIADH Severe hyponatremia in a heavy smoker with a central tumor is typically caused by SIADH from small cell lung cancer.

stem: Which of the following is the strongest determinant of prognosis in lung cancer?
explanation: TNM stage at diagnosis is the strongest prognostic factor (stage IA ~70–90% vs stage IV < 10% 5-year survival).

orig.stem: the following affect prognosis of CA lung except
options: Type of cell (small cell worse than non small cell)
orig.explanation: Nebulised tobramycin is an effective treatment in chronic colonisation Chronic colonisation with Pseudomonas is best managed with nebulised tobramycin.

stem: Causes of dyspnoea in bronchial carcinoma may be the following EXCEPT:
explanation: Recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy causes hoarseness and bovine cough, not breathlessness.

orig.stem: Causes of dyspnoea in bronchial carcinoma may be the following EXCEPT:
orig.explanation: E Whispering pectoriloguy Whispering pectoriloquy → consolidation from tumor; bronchial carcinoma likely → endobronchial biopsy.

stem: A 46-year-old woman was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the lung at bronchoscopy 1 week ago. She presents to the emergency department acutely short of breath with a non-productive cough and a central chest ache that is worse on inspiration. She is apyrexial; SpO2 91% on 40% oxygen, respiratory rate 30/min, BP 100/65 mmHg, pulse 110/min. Expansion is reduced on the right, with dullness to percussion throughout the right side and reduced breath sounds; the trachea is deviated to the right and the apex beat is not palpable. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Whole-hemithorax dullness with the trachea pulled towards it is lung collapse from an obstructing tumour; an effusion pushes it away.

orig.stem: A 46 year old woman has a recent diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the lung made at bronchoscopy 1 week ago. She presents to the emergency department acutely short of breath with a non-productive cough. She has an ache in the centre of her chest that is made worse by breathing in. She is apyrexial. Oxygen saturations are 91% on 40% oxygen. Respiratory rate is 30 breaths/min. Blood pressure (BP) is 100/65 mmHg and pulse is 110 beats/min. Examination reveals decreased expansion of the right side with dullness to percussion throughout the right side. Her trachea is deviated to the right and the apex beat is not palpable. Breath sounds are reduced on the right. What is the most likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Collapse of the right lung Examination findings indicate lung collapse with mediastinal shift due to a central obstructing lesion (likely a tumour).

stem: A 52-year-old man presents with 4 days of haemoptysis. He has lost weight over the last 2 months without night sweats. He has smoked 30 cigarettes per day for 40 years and worked in construction, where he may have been exposed to asbestos. He returned from a holiday in Guyana 1 week ago. His chest X-ray is shown. What is the most likely cause of the X-ray findings?
explanation: A thick-walled cavitating mass in a smoker with haemoptysis and weight loss is most likely cavitating squamous carcinoma.

orig.stem: A 52 year old man presents with 4 days of haemoptysis. Over the last 2 months he has lost weight without experiencing night sweats. He has smoked 30 cigarettes per day for 40 years and worked in construction. He thinks it is likely that he encountered asbestos at work but cannot recall any specific exposure. He returned home from holiday in Guyana 1 week ago. What is most likely to cause the CXR findings shown below.
orig.explanation: Bronchial carcinoma A central cavitating mass with associated nodules in a heavy smoker is most consistent with bronchial carcinoma.

stem: A 26-year-old woman presents with 24 hours of central chest pain and a month of progressive shortness of breath. Pulse 105/min, BP 105/65 mmHg, SpO2 96% on air, respiratory rate 16/min; she is apyrexial. The chest is clear and the heart sounds are normal without murmurs. ECG shows sinus tachycardia only. Haemoglobin 110 g/L, WCC 9 × 10⁹/L, platelets 340 × 10⁹/L, urea and electrolytes normal, CRP 67 mg/L. Her chest X-ray (shown) shows a widened superior mediastinum. What should the next investigation be?
explanation: A widened mediastinum with inflammation in a young woman suggests lymphoma; contrast CT chest, abdomen, pelvis to stage and find biopsy sites.

orig.stem: A 26 year old woman presents with 24 hours of central chest pain and progressive shortness of breath over a month. Examination reveals pulse 105 beats/min, BP 105/65 mmHg, oxygen saturations 96% on room air, apyrexial, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min. Chest clear; heart sounds dual, no murmurs. ECG: sinus tachycardia; no other abnormalities. Blood tests: haemoglobin 110 g/L, WCC 9 × 10^9/L, platelets 340 × 10^9/L, urea and electrolytes normal, CRP 67 mg/L. Given the CXR below, what should the next test be?
orig.explanation: Stop daptomycin and give prednisolone The clinical picture is consistent with daptomycin-induced eosinophilic pneumonia, requiring cessation of the drug and steroids.

stem: A 63-year-old woman had a CT pulmonary angiogram for left-sided pleuritic chest pain. There was no pulmonary embolism, but a 15-mm spiculated nodule at the apex of the right lung was noted (shown). Her pain resolved within 24 hours and she is otherwise asymptomatic; she has smoked 10 cigarettes per day for 40 years. What is the best next step?
explanation: A spiculated solid upper-lobe nodule ≥ 8 mm in a smoker (Brock risk > 10%) needs PET-CT next (BTS).

orig.stem: A 63 year old woman had a CT pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) when she presented with left-sided pleuritic chest pain. There was no pulmonary thromboembolism but a small pulmonary nodule at the apex of the right lung was noted. The patient recovered spontaneously over 24 hours and is otherwise asymptomatic with a smoking history of 10 cigarettes per day for 40 years. What is the best next step?
orig.explanation: Nitrofurantoin lung disease Chronic nitrofurantoin use can lead to a pneumonitis mimicking interstitial lung disease.

stem: A 63-year-old woman had a pulmonary nodule identified incidentally on a CT pulmonary angiogram. She has a 20 pack-year smoking history but no past medical history, is asymptomatic with performance status 0 and has normal pulmonary function. PET-CT (shown) shows FDG avidity in the right upper lobe nodule with no nodal or distant uptake. What should be the next step?
explanation: An FDG-avid nodule without nodal or distant uptake in a fit patient is presumed stage I: lobectomy (SABR if unfit).

orig.stem: A 63 year old woman had a pulmonary nodule identified incidentally during a CTPA examination. She has a 20 pack-year smoking history but no past medical history and is asymptomatic with performance status 0. Pulmonary function testing is normal. A PET scan is performed and shows FDG avidity in the right upper lobe nodule. What should be the next step?
orig.explanation: Right upper lobectomy An early-stage FDG-avid nodule in a fit patient should be resected surgically.

stem: A 51-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset breathlessness and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. She is a non-smoker with no significant past medical history. She needs 40% oxygen to maintain saturations of 92%; she is apyrexial, BP 101/62 mmHg, pulse 112/min, respiratory rate 30/min. What does her chest X-ray (shown) demonstrate?
explanation: Right hemithorax opacification with volume loss and the mediastinum pulled right is right lung collapse; bronchoscopy for the cause (e.g. carcinoid).

orig.stem: A 51 year old woman presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset breathlessness and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. She is a non-smoker with no significant past medical history. She requires 40% oxygen to maintain saturations at 92%, is apyrexial, BP 101/62 mmHg, pulse 112 beats/min, respiration rate 30 breaths/min. What is shown on the CXR?
orig.explanation: Right-sided lung collapse The CXR demonstrates complete right lung collapse with mediastinal shift, typical of a central obstructing lesion.

stem: A 54-year-old woman attends the rapid-access lung cancer clinic with haemoptysis and an abnormal chest X-ray. CT shows a large cavitating right upper lobe mass and bronchoscopic biopsy confirms squamous cell carcinoma. What does her PET-CT scan (shown) demonstrate?
options: Uptake confined to the right upper lobe lesion
Uptake in the right upper lobe lesion and a spinal metastasis
Uptake in the right upper lobe lesion and indeterminate uptake in pulmonary vessels
Uptake in the right upper lobe lesion and right hilar lymph node
Uptake in the right upper lobe lesion, a spinal metastasis and a sternal metastasis
explanation: PET-CT shows uptake in the right upper lobe primary and right hilar node (N1); sample PET-positive nodes (EBUS) before deciding.

orig.stem: A 54 year old woman attends the rapid-access lung cancer clinic with haemoptysis and an abnormal CXR. CT confirms a large cavitating right upper lobe mass and bronchoscopic biopsy confirms squamous lung cancer. The PET scan below was arranged. What does the CT- PET scan show?
options: Uptake confined to the right upper lobe lesion
Uptake in the right upper lobe lesion and a spinal metastasis
Uptake in the right upper lobe lesion and indeterminate uptake in pulmonary vessels
Uptake in the right upper lobe lesion and right hilar lymph node
Uptake in the right upper lobe lesion, a spinal metastasis and a sternal metastasis
orig.explanation: Uptake in the right upper lobe lesion and right hilar lymph node The PET scan demonstrates FDG uptake in the primary lesion and ipsilateral hilar node, upstaging the disease.

stem: A 59 year old smoker presents with a new cough. CT reveals a 4-cm peripheral tumour in the left lower lobe with an ipsilateral enlarged hilar lymph node. Due to emphysema, CT-guided biopsy is high risk. PET shows high FDG avidity in the tumour and indeterminate hilar uptake. What should be the next investigation?
explanation: EBUS-TBNA of PET-avid hilar nodes gives diagnosis and stage in one low-risk procedure (NICE NG122).

orig.stem: A 59 year old smoker presents with a new cough. CT reveals a 4-cm peripheral tumour in the left lower lobe with an ipsilateral enlarged hilar lymph node. Due to emphysema, CT-guided biopsy is high risk. PET shows high FDG avidity in the tumour and indeterminate hilar uptake. What should be the next investigation?
orig.explanation: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (EBUS-FNA) EBUS-FNA is preferred for sampling hilar nodes with lower pneumothorax risk in compromised lungs.

stem: An 84-year-old retired shipyard insulation worker who smokes a pipe has a 3-month history of a nagging left-sided chest ache, worst in the axilla and radiating to the spine. Examination shows dullness from the left base to the mid zone and erythema ab igne over the left chest wall. What is the most likely cause of his chest pain?
explanation: Persistent dull chest wall pain with effusion decades after asbestos exposure is mesothelioma; CT and pleural biopsy.

orig.stem: An 84 year old man with a 3-month history of nagging left chest ache, worst in the axilla with radiation to the spine, and a history of pipe-smoking presents. Examination shows dullness from left lung base to mid-zone with erythema ab igne. Which is the most likely cause of his chest pain?
orig.explanation: Mycetoma A mycetoma developing in an old tuberculous cavity is the most common cause of haemoptysis in this setting.

stem: A 67-year-old man undergoing CT colonography is found to have a 6-mm nodule in the right lower lobe. Which feature increases the risk of malignancy in a pulmonary nodule?
explanation: Upper-lobe location raises nodule malignancy risk (Brock), as do age, female sex, emphysema, size, spiculation and part-solid nature.

orig.stem: A 67 year old man undergoing CT colonogram is found to have a 6-mm nodule in the right lower lobe. Which factor increases the risk of malignancy in pulmonary nodules?
orig.explanation: Upper lobe distribution Nodules in the upper lobes are more suspicious for malignancy.

stem: A 65-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis has CT for suspected interstitial lung disease, which shows mild basal interlobular septal thickening and a 1.5-cm spiculated right upper lobe nodule. What is true regarding PET scanning for pulmonary nodules?
options: It is not useful in nodules < 1 cm in diameter
It offers no more information than a standard CT
explanation: PET-CT is unreliable for nodules < 8–10 mm, misses low-avidity tumours (carcinoid, AIS) and is falsely positive in inflammation.

orig.stem: A 65 year old woman with rheumatoid arthritis undergoes CT for ILD evaluation which shows mild basal interlobular septal thickening and a 1.5 cm speculated right upper lobe nodule. What is true regarding PET scanning for pulmonary nodules?
options: It is not useful in nodules < 1 cm in diameter
It offers no more information than a standard CT
orig.explanation: It is not useful in nodules < 1 cm in diameter PET is limited in small nodules and cannot replace histological diagnosis.

stem: A 63 year old female non-smoker with a 5-cm lesion in the right mid-zone undergoes bronchoscopy with tumour biopsy. Which is the most common histological type of lung cancer?
explanation: Adenocarcinoma is the commonest lung cancer (40–50%), especially in never-smokers and women; test for EGFR, ALK, ROS1 and PD-L1.

orig.stem: A 63 year old female non-smoker with a 5-cm lesion in the right mid-zone undergoes bronchoscopy with tumour biopsy. Which is the most common histological type of lung cancer?
orig.explanation: Adenocarcinoma Adenocarcinoma is now the most common form of lung cancer.

stem: A 73-year-old woman with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer develops increasingly painful wrists. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Painful wrists/ankles with clubbing in NSCLC is hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy (periostitis); NSAIDs, bisphosphonates, treat tumour.

orig.stem: A 73 year old woman with metastatic non- small cell lung cancer develops increasingly painful wrists. What is the most likely cause?
orig.explanation: Nifedipine High-altitude pulmonary edema → descend, give oxygen; nifedipine helpful; dexamethasone/acetazolamide/PDE-5 inhibitors are alternatives.

stem: A 56-year-old smoker with a new cough has a CT showing a 4-cm peripheral left lung mass with an enlarged ipsilateral hilar lymph node and a pleural effusion; pleural fluid cytology is positive for malignant cells. What is the correct stage?
explanation: A malignant pleural effusion is M1a, so the cancer is stage IVA regardless of T and N; treatment is systemic.

orig.stem: A 56 year old smoker with a new cough has CT showing a 4-cm left lung peripheral mass with an ipsilateral hilar lymph node and a cytology-positive pleural effusion. What is the correct staging?
orig.explanation: IV A malignant pleural effusion automatically classifies the lung cancer as stage IV.

stem: A 36-year-old non-smoker has isolated haemoptysis. CT shows collapse of the left upper lobe with a vascular tumour at the left upper lobe orifice. What is the most likely tumour type?
explanation: A vascular endobronchial tumour causing collapse in a young non-smoker is a bronchial carcinoid; resection has an excellent prognosis.

orig.stem: A 36 year old non-smoker with isolated haemoptysis and a CT showing left upper lobe collapse with a vascular tumour at the LUL orifice. What is the most likely tumour type?
orig.explanation: Carcinoid A young non-smoker with localized haemoptysis and a vascular endobronchial mass is most consistent with a bronchial carcinoid.

stem: A 64 year old woman with breast cancer metastatic to liver, lungs and bone develops increasing breathlessness despite antibiotics. CT shows diffuse interstitial thickening radiating from the hila. What is the likely diagnosis?
explanation: Beaded septal and bronchovascular thickening radiating from the hila in metastatic breast cancer is lymphangitis carcinomatosa.

orig.stem: A 64 year old woman with breast cancer metastatic to liver, lungs and bone develops increasing breathlessness despite antibiotics. CT shows diffuse interstitial thickening radiating from the hila. What is the likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Lymphangitis carcinomatosa The CT pattern in a cancer patient with progressive dyspnoea is most consistent with lymphangitic carcinomatosis.

stem: A 28-year-old man has a large anterior mediastinal mass with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Anterior mediastinal mass with cervical and axillary nodes in a young adult is lymphoma (the 4 Ts: thymoma, teratoma, thyroid, lymphoma).

orig.stem: A 28 year old man with a large anterior mediastinal mass with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy is evaluated. What is the most likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Lymphoma The clinical and imaging findings are most consistent with lymphoma.

stem: A 72 year old man with a history of benign asbestos pleurisy presents with a right-sided pleural effusion, pleural plaques and mediastinal pleural thickening. What is the most likely reason for his presentation?
explanation: A unilateral effusion with mediastinal pleural thickening after asbestos exposure is highly suspicious of mesothelioma; pleural biopsy.

orig.stem: A 72 year old man with a history of benign asbestos pleurisy presents with a right-sided pleural effusion, pleural plaques and mediastinal pleural thickening. What is the most likely reason for his presentation?
orig.explanation: Mesothelioma The clinical and imaging findings in an asbestos-exposed patient with an effusion and thickening are most concerning for mesothelioma.

stem: A 72-year-old smoker has a 5-cm peripheral left lung mass, left hilar lymphadenopathy, an indeterminate liver lesion and a palpable, hard 2-cm left supraclavicular lymph node. What should be the next diagnostic test?
explanation: Biopsy the palpable supraclavicular node (N3): it gives histology, molecular markers and the highest stage with least risk (NICE NG122).

orig.stem: A 72 year old man with a smoking history and occupational exposure (‘monkey dung’) has a 5-cm peripheral left lung mass, left hilar lymphadenopathy, and an indeterminate liver lesion. What should be the next diagnostic test?
orig.explanation: Supraclavicular lymph node biopsy Peripheral lymph node biopsy is the least invasive method to obtain tissue in suspected lung cancer.

stem: A 55-year-old woman with a left apical lung cancer and suspected mediastinal node involvement undergoes mediastinoscopy under general anaesthesia, followed by radiotherapy. She has been hoarse since waking from the procedure, but laryngoscopy shows normal vocal cord movement. What is the most likely cause?
options: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement by the tumour
explanation: Hoarseness right after anaesthesia with normal cord movement is intubation-related laryngeal trauma; a nerve palsy would paralyse the cord.

orig.stem: A 55 year old woman with left apical lung cancer and lymph node involvement undergoes radiotherapy after mediastinoscopy. She develops hoarseness but bronchoscopy reveals no vocal cord paralysis. What is the likely cause?
options: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement by the tumour
orig.explanation: Endotracheal intubation during mediastinoscopy The hoarseness is most likely due to trauma from intubation rather than tumour involvement.

stem: A woman with systemic sclerosis is found to have a 3-cm lung lesion that is FDG-avid on PET-CT. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The findings on PET/CT make infection very likely
The findings on PET/CT make infection very unlikely
The findings on PET/CT make malignancy very likely
The findings on PET/CT make malignancy very unlikely
explanation: FDG uptake also occurs in infection and inflammation, so an avid lesion still needs tissue diagnosis.

orig.stem: Mrs. Wittstine has scleroderma and a suspicious 3 cm FDG-avid lesion on PET/CT. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The findings on PET/CT make infection very likely.
The findings on PET/CT make infection very unlikely.
The findings on PET/CT make malignancy very likely.
The findings on PET/CT make malignancy very unlikely.
orig.explanation: Additional diagnostic studies are indicated. FDG uptake can be seen in both infection and malignancy; further studies are required.

stem: A 75-year-old man with previous asbestos exposure has a pleural effusion suspicious for mesothelioma. Which statement about this condition is true?
options: Cigarette smoking increases the likelihood of developing the condition
Death is usually due to widespread distant metastases
Exposure can be brief (1–2 years) and the latency may be 40 years or more
Repeated pleural fluid cytology usually gives a definitive diagnosis
Combined surgical resection and chemotherapy significantly improves survival
explanation: Mesothelioma can follow brief asbestos exposure with a 30–40+ year latency; smoking does not raise its risk; cytology is often negative.

orig.stem: A 75-year-old man with asbestos exposure and a pleural effusion suspicious for mesothelioma. Which statement is true?
options: Cigarette smoking increases the likelihood of developing the condition.
Death in this disease is usually due to diffuse metastases.
Exposure can be brief (1-2 yrs), latency may be up to 40 yrs.
Repeated pleural fluid cytology usually leads to a definitive diagnosis.
Combination surgical resection and chemo significantly improves survival.
orig.explanation: Exposure can be as brief as 1–2 years, and latency to disease can be 40 years or more. Mesothelioma can occur after minimal exposure with a long latency period.

stem: A 64-year-old man has facial swelling and distended neck veins, and superior vena cava obstruction is suspected. Which CT finding is most likely?
options: A central mass obstructing right main bronchus
An apical mass invading the chest wall
Enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes compressing the SVC
explanation: SVC obstruction is usually malignant (lung cancer, lymphoma) from mediastinal nodes compressing the SVC; stent for rapid relief.

orig.stem: A 64-year-old man with facial swelling, distended neck veins, suspect SVC syndrome. Which CT finding is most likely?
options: A central mass obstructing right main bronchus
An apical mass invading the chest wall
Enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes compressing the SVC
orig.explanation: Enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes causing obstruction of the superior vena cava SVC syndrome is most commonly due to extrinsic compression from mediastinal lymphadenopathy, often from malignancy.

stem: A 64-year-old man has facial swelling and distended neck veins from superior vena cava obstruction caused by enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. He has no stridor or confusion, and no tissue diagnosis has yet been made. Initial management includes all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Elevation of the head of the bed
explanation: In SVC obstruction without stridor or cerebral oedema, get tissue first; emergency radiotherapy may obscure the diagnosis.

orig.stem: In the scenario of SVC syndrome, initial therapy includes all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Elevation of the head of the bed
orig.explanation: Administration of furosemide as needed to achieve diuresis Diuresis is not a standard initial treatment for SVC syndrome.

stem: A 58-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer develops acute paraplegia from suspected metastatic spinal cord compression. What is the first step in management?
explanation: Suspected MSCC with deficit: give high-dose dexamethasone immediately, then whole-spine MRI within 24 h and definitive treatment.

orig.stem: A 58-year-old with metastatic breast cancer has acute paraplegia from spinal cord compression. First step?
orig.explanation: Administration of dexamethasone 10 mg IV Immediate IV steroids are the first step in managing spinal cord compression.

stem: A 65-year-old woman presents with breathlessness and haemoptysis. She is diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the lung. She has been a smoker for as long as she can remember. She has lived in central London for almost 30 years now and she worked in a shipbuilding yard for most of her working life. Both her father and mother died of lung cancer. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her cancer?
explanation: Smoking causes ~85% of lung cancer, especially squamous and small cell; asbestos multiplies its effect.

orig.stem: A 65-year-old woman presents with breathlessness and haemoptysis. She is diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the lung. She has been a smoker for as long as she can remember. She has lived in central London for almost 30 years now and she worked in a shipbuilding yard for most of her working life. Both her father and mother died of lung cancer. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her cancer?
orig.explanation: Smoking Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung is closely correlated with a history of tobacco smoking, the most common cause of lung cancer.

stem: A middle-aged man is diagnosed with lung cancer. He worked in a shipbuilding yard for most of his life. He is distraught with the diagnosis as he says he has never smoked in his life. Which of the following types of lung cancer is he most likely to suffer from?
explanation: Adenocarcinoma is the commonest lung cancer in never-smokers; asbestos raises risk of all types.

orig.stem: A middle-aged man is diagnosed with lung cancer. He worked in a shipbuilding yard for most of his life. He is distraught with the diagnosis as he says he has never smoked in his life. Which of the following types of lung cancer is he most likely to suffer from?
orig.explanation: Adenocarcinoma Adenocarcinoma is the most common type of lung cancer in lifelong nonsmokers, accounting for 40% of all lung cancers.

stem: A 53-year-old woman is diagnosed with lung cancer. Her main symptoms on presentation included breathlessness and haemoptysis. She complained of stretch marks on her abdomen and that her skin bruised easily. On examination you note purple abdominal striae. Which of the following types of lung cancer is she most likely to suffer from?
explanation: Cushing's (striae, bruising) in lung cancer means ectopic ACTH from small cell carcinoma (or carcinoid).

orig.stem: A 53-year-old woman is diagnosed with lung cancer. Her main symptoms on presentation included breathlessness and haemoptysis. She complained of stretch marks on her abdomen and that her skin bruised easily. On examination you note purple abdominal striae. Which of the following types of lung cancer is she most likely to suffer from?
orig.explanation: Small cell Small cell carcinoma, due to its neuroendocrine nature, can produce ectopic hormones leading to Cushing syndrome features such as purple abdominal striae.

stem: A 63-year-old man is diagnosed with lung cancer. Which of the following extrapulmonary manifestations is he most likely to suffer from?
explanation: Clubbing is the commonest extrapulmonary sign of lung cancer (up to a third); new clubbing in > 40s needs an urgent CXR.

orig.stem: A 63-year-old man is diagnosed with lung cancer. Which of the following extrapulmonary manifestations is he most likely to suffer from?
orig.explanation: Clubbing Clubbing is the most common extrapulmonary feature in lung cancer, particularly in nonsmall cell lung cancer.

stem: A 66-year-old woman with history of weight loss presents to the respiratory clinic with an 8-week history of nonproductive cough and chronic clearing of throat. She has a 52-pack year smoking history and quit 25 years ago. She was subsequently diagnosed with carcinoma of the lung. Which of the following is NOT a complication of carcinoma of the lung?
explanation: Lung cancer causes hypercalcaemia (PTHrP, bone metastases), not hypocalcaemia; SIADH, HPOA, adrenal metastases and Horner's are recognised.

orig.stem: A 66-year-old woman with history of weight loss presents to the respiratory clinic with an 8-week history of nonproductive cough and chronic clearing of throat. She has a 52-pack year smoking history and quit 25 years ago. She was subsequently diagnosed with carcinoma of the lung. Which of the following is NOT a complication of carcinoma of the lung?
orig.explanation: Hypocalcaemia Squamous cell carcinomas are associated with hypercalcaemia, not hypocalcaemia. SCLC is linked to SIADH (hyponatraemia) and adenocarcinomas with hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

stem: A 65-year-old factory worker presents with a dry cough, right-sided chest pain and finger clubbing. He has lost 4 kg in weight in the last 2 weeks and has a 30-year smoking history. The right lower chest is dull to percussion with reduced expansion, and a chest X-ray shows a right peripheral lung mass with a small pleural effusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A peripheral mass with clubbing, weight loss and effusion in a smoker is non-small cell lung cancer; clubbing is uncommon in small cell.

orig.stem: A 65-year-old factory worker presents with a dry cough, right-sided chest pain and finger clubbing. He has lost 4 kg in weight in the last 2 weeks. He has a 30-year smoking history. On examination the right lung is dull to percussion with reduced chest expansion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) Small cell lung cancer, strongly associated with smoking and central lung lesions, is suggested by the presentation.

stem: A 50-year-old heavy smoker of 30 pack years presents to his GP with weight loss of 8 kg over 4 months and a chronic cough with two episodes of haemoptysis. He denies any history of fever. Chest radiograph shows a rounded lesion measuring 5 cm in diameter in the right upper lobe. What is the most likely diagnosis?

orig.stem: A 50-year-old heavy smoker of 30 pack years presents to his GP with weight loss of 8 kg over 4 months and a chronic cough with two episodes of haemoptysis. He denies any history of fever. Chest radiograph shows a rounded lesion measuring 5 cm in diameter in the right upper lobe. What is the most likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Bronchial carcinoma The presence of a large, rounded lesion in a heavy smoker is most consistent with bronchial carcinoma, likely squamous cell carcinoma.

stem: A 42-year-old man has had a grade III chondrosarcoma of the right maxilla resected. He now has breathlessness and a dry cough, and a chest X-ray suggests lung metastases. Which radiological feature of lung metastases is characteristic of this tumour?
explanation: Calcified lung metastases are characteristic of bone/cartilage sarcomas (osteo-, chondrosarcoma) and thyroid or mucinous cancers.

orig.stem: A 42-year-old male patient presented with a 5-month history of facial swelling and a tumoral mass in the right maxilla with infiltration into the skin. Recently, he had been suffering from difficulty in breathing and a dry cough. Face and sinus computerised tomography (CT) illustrated a right maxillary lesion. Maxilla surgery was performed without orbital removal and a grade III chondrosarcoma was diagnosed, with infiltration into bone, the anterior wall of the maxillary sinus and orbital floor. A subsequent chest x-ray was performed given his chest symptoms suggesting the appearance of lung metastases. What feature of lung metastases is characteristic for this tumour?
orig.explanation: Calcification Calcified lung mets suggest osteosarcoma/chondrosarcoma or papillary thyroid; cavitation common in squamous cell; adenocarcinoma may cause consolidation.

stem: A 66-year-old man with COPD is referred by his GP to the rapid-access chest clinic after several courses of antibiotics and steroids for an exacerbation that has not fully resolved. His chest X-ray shows a suspicious 3-cm mass at the right hilum with background changes of COPD. Blood tests: Hb 142 g/L, platelets 323 × 10⁹/L, WBC 9.1 × 10⁹/L, Na 128 mmol/L, K 3.9 mmol/L, urea 6.4 mmol/L, creatinine 99 µmol/L. There is no clubbing, and a fixed monophonic wheeze is heard in the right lung. What is the most likely underlying cause?
explanation: A central mass with fixed monophonic wheeze and hyponatraemia in a smoker suggests small cell lung cancer (SIADH).

orig.stem: A 66-year-old man with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is referred by his GP to the Rapid Access Chest Clinic. He was recently treated with several courses of antibiotics and steroids for an exacerbation of COPD which failed to completely resolve. A chest x-ray was reported as follows: There is a suspicious 3cm mass in the right hilum. Background changes of COPD. Urgent referral to the chest clinic is advised. Report faxed to GP. Recent blood tests are also reviewed: Hb 14.2 g/dl; Platelets 323 * 10^9/l; WBC 9.1 * 10^9/l; Na+ 128 mmol/l; K+ 3.9 mmol/l; Urea 6.4 mmol/l; Creatinine 99 μmol/l. On examination there is no evidence of clubbing. Examination of chest demonstrates a fixed monophonic wheeze in the right lung. What is the most likely underlying cause?
orig.explanation: Small cell lung cancer Hyponatremia in lung cancer suggests SIADH → most associated with small-cell carcinoma.

stem: A 74-year-old man who has smoked 40 cigarettes per day for 30 years presents with increasing shortness of breath. He takes diclofenac and paracetamol for joint pain. His chest X-ray shows a spiculated left hilar mass with dense consolidation of the left lower lobe beyond it, and air bronchograms indicate that the lobar bronchus is still patent. Which finding would be expected on examination over the left lower lobe?
explanation: Consolidation with a patent bronchus gives bronchial breathing, increased vocal resonance and whispering pectoriloquy.

orig.stem: A 74-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of increased shortness of breath. He has smoked 40 cigarettes per day for the past 30 years. Medications include diclofenac and paracetamol for joint pain. He comes to the clinic with a chest X-ray from his GP which shows a spiculated left hilar mass. What would the classical respiratory findings over the abnormal area be?
orig.explanation: Pulmonary embolism In the postoperative setting, leg swelling and acute respiratory distress with supporting ECG changes strongly suggest a pulmonary embolism.

stem: A 74-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of increased shortness of breath. He has smoked 40 cigarettes per day for the past 30 years. Medications include diclofenac and paracetamol for joint pain. He comes to the clinic with a chest X-ray from his GP which shows a spiculated left hilar mass. What would the classical respiratory findings over the abnormal area be?

orig.stem: A 74-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of increased shortness of breath. He has smoked 40 cigarettes per day for the past 30 years. Medications include diclofenac and paracetamol for joint pain. He comes to the clinic with a chest X-ray from his GP which shows a spiculated left hilar mass. What would the classical respiratory findings over the abnormal area be?
orig.explanation: Ethambutol Ethambutol toxicity can cause optic neuritis; patients should report visual changes.

stem: A 68-year-old man who smokes 40 cigarettes per day has a proven diagnosis of bronchial carcinoma, and radical radiotherapy is being considered. Which of the following is the most significant contraindication to radical radiotherapy?
explanation: A malignant pleural effusion (M1a, stage IV) cannot be included in a radical radiotherapy field, so radical treatment is inappropriate.

orig.stem: 18-You are referred a 68-year-old man who smokes 40 cigarettes per day and has a proven diagnosis of bronchial carcinoma. You are considering radical radiotherapy in this man. Which of the following is the most significant contra indication to radical radiotherapy?
orig.explanation: C Malignant pleural effusion Malignant pleural effusion predicts poor outcome with radical radiotherapy.

stem: 52-A 64-year-old mechanic and lifelong smoker noticed haemoptysis. Chest X-ray shows left upper-lobe collapse and predominantly left-sided hilar enlargement and mediastinal widening. What is the most likely diagnosis?

orig.stem: 52-A 64-year-old mechanic and lifelong smoker noticed haemoptysis. Chest X-ray shows left upper-lobe collapse and predominantly left-sided hilar enlargement and mediastinal widening. What is the most likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: A Bronchial carcinoma Central endobronchial tumor → lobar collapse with ipsilateral hilar enlargement; proceed to bronchoscopy and/or CT. Respiratory Pharmacology

stem: A woman with history of bronchial carcinoma 2 months ago developed cough and dyspnea. Which of the following is the best treatment of choice for her persistent obstructive symptoms?

orig.stem: A woman with history of bronchial carcinoma 2 months ago developed cough and dyspnea. Which of the following is the best treatment of choice for her persistent obstructive symptoms?
orig.explanation: Tiotropium Tiotropium, a long-acting anticholinergic, is often first-line for persistent COPD symptoms.

stem: A 28-year-old man of Chinese origin on treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis telephones 2 weeks into therapy complaining of painful eyes and blurred vision. What is the likely cause?
options: Drug resistance to ethambutol and pyrazinamide
explanation: Painful eyes and blurred vision on TB treatment is ethambutol optic neuritis: stop it and get urgent ophthalmology review.

orig.stem: A 28 year old man of Chinese origin on treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis calls 2 weeks into therapy with painful eyes. What is the likely cause?
options: Short-acting beta-agonists (SABA) A. Drug resistance to ethambutol and pyrazinamide B. Ethambutol C. Immune reconstitution D. Intercurrent viral infection E. Non-tuberculous Mycobacterium
orig.explanation: Ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) scan or CT pulmonary angiogram A CT pulmonary angiogram (or V/Q scan) is used to confirm the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism when chest X-ray is unrevealing.

stem: A 24-year-old man with cystic fibrosis asks about ivacaftor. Ivacaftor corrects the function of which CFTR defect?
explanation: Ivacaftor is a CFTR potentiator for gating mutations, classically G551D; F508del needs a corrector plus ivacaftor.

orig.stem: A 24 year old man with cystic fibrosis inquires about ivacaftor. Ivacaftor corrects the function of which CFTR defect?
orig.explanation: G551D Ivacaftor is effective in patients with the G551D mutation.

stem: A 56-year-old non-smoking man with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the left lung (EGFR mutation positive) is evaluated. What is the treatment of choice?
options: EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (e.g. erlotinib or osimertinib)
explanation: Metastatic EGFR-mutant adenocarcinoma is treated first line with an oral EGFR TKI (osimertinib preferred).

orig.stem: A 56 year old non-smoking man with metastatic adenocarcinoma (EGFR positive) of the left lung is evaluated. What is the treatment of choice?
orig.explanation: Erlotinib Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g. er lotinib) are indicated in EGFR mutation-positive adenocarcinoma.

stem: A 24-year-old patient with cystic fibrosis fails to recover from an exacerbation, and sputum cultures now isolate Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Which statement regarding P. aeruginosa in cystic fibrosis is true?
options: Intravenous antibiotic therapy is rarely required
It is a benign coloniser of the bronchiectatic airways
It is one of the earliest bacteria isolated in sputum from CF patients
Nebulised azithromycin 3 times a week suppresses infection
Nebulised tobramycin is an effective treatment in chronic colonisation
explanation: Chronic Pseudomonas in CF accelerates decline; long-term nebulised tobramycin (or colistin, aztreonam) reduces exacerbations.

orig.stem: A 24 year old CF patient fails to recover from an exacerbation. Sputum cultures now isolate Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Which statement is true regarding P. aeruginosa in CF? E. Radiotherapy
orig.explanation: Montelukast LTRAs can precipitate eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Churg– Strauss).

stem: A 61 year old woman on IV daptomycin for staphylococcal discitis, previously improving, spikes a fever after 2 weeks with rising WCC (including eosinophilia) and new bilateral upper zone consolidation on CXR. What should be the treatment?
explanation: Fever, eosinophilia and new infiltrates after 2 weeks of daptomycin is drug-induced eosinophilic pneumonia: stop it and give steroids.

orig.stem: A 61 year old woman on IV daptomycin for staphylococcal discitis, previously improving, spikes a fever after 2 weeks with rising WCC (including eosinophilia) and new bilateral upper zone consolidation on CXR. What should be the treatment?
orig.explanation: High-resolution CT scan of the chest High-resolution CT scanning is the investigation of choice to visualize bronchial dilatation characteristic of bronchiectasis.

stem: A 70 year old woman with a 6-week history of cough, low-grade fever, and malaise, on nitrofurantoin for UTIs, has bi-basal infiltrates on CXR. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Chronic cough, fever and bibasal infiltrates on long-term nitrofurantoin is nitrofurantoin lung; stopping the drug is diagnostic and therapeutic.

orig.stem: A 70 year old woman with a 6-week history of cough, low-grade fever, and malaise, on nitrofurantoin for UTIs, has bi-basal infiltrates on CXR. What is the most likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Recurrent respiratory infections and hemoptysis Patients with bronchiectasis are prone to recurrent infections and may also develop significant hemoptysis.

stem: A 58-year-old woman with a 28-year history of rheumatoid arthritis presents with progressive shortness of breath. All of the following are recognised pulmonary complications of rheumatoid arthritis EXCEPT:
explanation: RA causes effusions, ILD, nodules, bronchiolitis obliterans and bronchiectasis; apical fibrobullous disease belongs to ankylosing spondylitis.

orig.stem: A 58-year-old woman with a 28-year history of rheumatoid arthritis presents with progressive shortness of breath. Which pulmonary complication is most likely?
orig.explanation: All of the above Rheumatoid arthritis can cause pleural disease, ILD, nodules, and airway involvement.

stem: Dyspnea that associate with wheezing can be caused by the following EXCEPT;

orig.stem: Dyspnea that associate with wheezing can be caused by the following EXCEPT;
orig.explanation: Pneumothorax. Pneumothorax typically does not cause wheezing.

stem: A 70-year-old postoperative male (72 hours after hip replacement) presents with left leg swelling, shortness of breath, hypotension, and an oxygen saturation of 78%. The ECG shows sinus tachycardia with a partial right bundle branch block. What is the most likely cause of his symptoms?

orig.stem: A 70-year-old postoperative male (72 hours after hip replacement) presents with left leg swelling, shortness of breath, hypotension, and an oxygen saturation of 78%. The ECG shows sinus tachycardia with a partial right bundle branch block. What is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
orig.explanation: If the Gram stain reveals numerous gram-positive diplococci, numerous white blood cells, and few epithelial cells, Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most likely pathogen. CAP in >35 with rigors, pleuritic pain, lobar consolidation → pneumococcal pneumonia; diagnose via sputum GPC diplococci; empiric ceftriaxone or resp FQ (penicillin resistance common).

stem: If the chest X-ray is normal, which investigation is most appropriate to support the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism?
options: Ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) scan or CT pulmonary angiogram

orig.stem: If the chest X-ray is normal, which investigation is most appropriate to support the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism?
options: Ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) scan or CT pulmonary angiogram
orig.explanation: Nausea Varenicline most common adverse effect = nausea; vivid dreams and insomnia occur but less frequent; constipation and DILE not typical.

stem: What is the immediate treatment for a haemodynamically unstable patient with suspected pulmonary embolism?
explanation: Haemodynamically unstable (high-risk) PE: systemic thrombolysis (alteplase) after starting heparin; embolectomy if contraindicated.

orig.stem: What is the immediate treatment for a hemodynamically unstable patient with suspected pulmonary embolism?
orig.explanation: Thrombolytic therapy In unstable patients with pulmonary embolism, prompt thrombolytic therapy is indicated.

stem: A 48-year-old man presents with an 8-month history of productive cough with yellowish sputum, occasional hemoptysis, exertional dyspnea, and finger clubbing. What is the most likely diagnosis?

orig.stem: A 48-year-old man presents with an 8-month history of productive cough with yellowish sputum, occasional hemoptysis, exertional dyspnea, and finger clubbing. What is the most likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Bronchiectasis The chronic productive cough with clubbing and hemoptysis strongly suggests bronchiectasis.

stem: Which investigation is considered the gold standard for confirming a diagnosis of bronchiectasis?
options: High-resolution CT scan of the chest

orig.stem: Which investigation is considered the gold standard for confirming a diagnosis of bronchiectasis?
options: High-resolution CT scan of the chest
orig.explanation: C Prednisolone Viral-triggered asthma exacerbation → give prednisolone.

stem: Which two complications are most important to monitor for in patients with bronchiectasis?

orig.stem: Which two complications are most important to monitor for in patients with bronchiectasis?
orig.explanation: C Erythromycin Mycoplasma pneumonia → no cell wall → β-lactams ineffective.

stem: A 75-year-old woman has a 10-year history of daily non-productive cough. She has back pain from a vertebral fracture, and the chest X-ray shows a large hiatus hernia and kyphosis. What is the most likely cause of her cough?
explanation: Chronic dry cough with a large hiatus hernia and kyphosis is most likely GORD; trial a PPI.

orig.stem: A 75 year old woman with a 10-year history of daily non-productive cough, back pain from vertebral fracture, a large hiatus hernia and kyphosis on CXR. What is the most likely cause of her cough?
orig.explanation: Gastro-oesophageal reflux The hiatus hernia and kyphosis point to reflux as the likely cause.

stem: A 42-year-old non-smoking woman has a 4-month history of breathlessness occurring only in the daytime, which began after an upper respiratory tract infection with nasal blockage. Her D-dimer was positive but CTPA is normal, and spirometry is normal. What should be the next investigation?
options: Dysfunctional breathing studies and a Nijmegen questionnaire
Lung volume and gas transfer studies
explanation: Daytime-only breathlessness after a viral illness with normal imaging and spirometry suggests dysfunctional breathing; Nijmegen questionnaire.

orig.stem: A 42 year old non-smoker woman presents with a 4-month history of breathlessness occurring only in the daytime following an upper respiratory tract infection with nasal blockage. Her D-dimer is positive but CTPA is normal. Spirometry is normal. What should be the next investigation?
options: Dysfunctional breathing studies and a Nijmegen questionnaire
Lung volume and gas transfer studies
orig.explanation: Dysfunctional breathing studies and a Nijmegen questionnaire The presentation is typical of dysfunctional breathing post-infection.

stem: A 64-year-old woman with COPD presents with sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness after returning from a 3-week holiday. SpO2 is 84% on room air; there is reduced air entry and mild bilateral ankle oedema, and the D-dimer is elevated. What is the most likely cause of her chest pain?
explanation: Sudden pleuritic pain with hypoxaemia after travel and a raised D-dimer in COPD is most likely PE; CTPA (CXR to exclude pneumothorax).

orig.stem: A 64 year old woman with COPD presents with sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness after a 3-week holiday. O2 saturations are 84% on room air; exam shows decreased air entry and mild bipedal oedema; D-dimer is elevated. What is the most likely cause of her chest pain?
orig.explanation: Pulmonary thromboembolism The acute onset in a high-risk patient points to pulmonary embolism.

stem: A 45-year-old non-smoking man with finger clubbing, noted since his teens and also present in his father, presents with a sprained wrist. He has no other symptoms. What is the next step the family physician should take?
options: Check bloods (including LFTs, thyroid function tests and ESR)
Sweat test to exclude cystic fibrosis
explanation: Lifelong familial clubbing without symptoms is hereditary clubbing: reassure. New clubbing needs investigation.

orig.stem: A 45 year old non-smoking man with longstanding finger clubbing (noted since his teens, similar to his father) presents with a sprained wrist. What is the next step the family physician should take?
options: Check bloods (including LFTs, thyroid function tests and ESR)
Sweat test to exclude cystic fibrosis
orig.explanation: Reassurance The longstanding familial clubbing without other symptoms requires no further investigation.

stem: A patient with known bronchiectasis and a long-standing right apical cavity from old tuberculosis now coughs up 50 mL of fresh red blood. The chest X-ray shows a rounded mass partially filling the cavity. What is the likely cause of his haemoptysis?
explanation: A mass within an old TB cavity with an air crescent is an aspergilloma (mycetoma), which causes haemoptysis.

orig.stem: A patient with known bronchiectasis and a long-standing right apical cavity now coughs up 50 mL of fresh red blood. The CXR shows partial filling of the cavity. What is the likely cause of his haemoptysis?
orig.explanation: Klebsiella pneumoniae Cavitating upper-lobe pneumonia in elderly diabetic/alcoholic → think Klebsiella; Pseudomonas = HAP/CF; Mycoplasma/Legionella give atypical patterns.

stem: A 32-year-old patient with cystic fibrosis presents with massive haemoptysis (250 mL of fresh red blood) but is haemodynamically stable. What is the most useful investigation?
explanation: Massive haemoptysis in CF comes from bronchial arteries: bronchial artery angiography localises and embolises the bleeding.

orig.stem: A 32 year old cystic fibrosis patient presents with massive haemoptysis (250 mL of fresh red blood) but is haemodynamically stable. What is the most useful investigation?
orig.explanation: Bronchial artery angiography Angiography is most useful to localise the bleeding site in CF patients.

stem: A 57 year old woman with a 3-year history of chronic productive cough (with green sputum) and frequent brief antibiotic responses is investigated. What is the best investigation?

orig.stem: A 57 year old woman with a 3-year history of chronic productive cough (with green sputum) and frequent brief antibiotic responses is investigated. What is the best investigation?
orig.explanation: High-resolution CT chest HRCT is the investigation of choice to assess for bronchiectasis.

stem: Acute coryza is most commonly caused by which of the following?
explanation: The common cold (acute coryza) is caused mainly by rhinoviruses; symptomatic treatment only.

orig.stem: Acute coryza is most commonly caused by which of the following?
orig.explanation: Rhinovirus Rhinovirus is the most common cause of the common cold.

stem: A 45 year old man with a history of spontaneous VTE and family history presents with sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain, shortness of breath, and a swollen right calf after ACL reconstruction abroad and a recent long- haul flight. What should the next test be?

orig.stem: A 45 year old man with a history of spontaneous VTE and family history presents with sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain, shortness of breath, and a swollen right calf after ACL reconstruction abroad and a recent long- haul flight. What should the next test be?

stem: A 28-year-old woman recovering from ACL repair in an above-knee cast has near-syncope on standing, with BP 80/45 mmHg and sinus tachycardia. The chest X-ray is clear and the D-dimer is elevated, and she then has a cardiac arrest. What should the immediate management include?
explanation: Cardiac arrest from suspected massive PE: immediate thrombolysis during CPR, continuing CPR for 60–90 min.

orig.stem: A 28 year old woman recovering from ACL repair in an above-knee cast experiences near-syncope on standing, with BP 80/45 mmHg and sinus tachycardia. CXR is clear, D-dimer is elevated, and she subsequently suffers a cardiac arrest. What should the immediate management include?
orig.explanation: Thrombolysis In the setting of a massive pulmonary embolism with cardiac arrest, immediate thrombolysis is indicated.

stem: A 45-year-old woman has a cough every May that resolves by autumn, with nasal discharge and watering eyes. Examination and spirometry are normal. What is the likely diagnosis?
explanation: Seasonal cough with rhinorrhoea and watery eyes every May with normal spirometry is seasonal allergic rhinitis; antihistamine and nasal steroid.

orig.stem: A 45 year old woman presents with a seasonal cough in May that resolves by autumn, with nasal discharge and watering eyes. Examination and spirometry are normal. What is the likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Allergic rhinitis The seasonal nasal symptoms point to allergic rhinitis.

stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding breathing during sleep?
options: Abnormal ventilatory drive is present in obstructive sleep apnoea
Forty per cent of middle-aged women snore
Palatoglossus and genioglossus contract actively during expiration
explanation: Normal sleep reduces ventilatory drive and muscle tone, so mild hypoventilation (small PaCO2 rise) is normal.

orig.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding breathing during sleep?
options: Abnormal ventilatory drive is present in obstructive sleep apnoea
Forty per cent of middle-aged women snore
Palatoglossus and genioglossus contract actively during expiration
orig.explanation: Hypoventilation accompanies normal sleep During sleep, overall muscle tone decreases leading to slight hypoventilation.

stem: A 55-year-old man with excessive daytime sleepiness, an Epworth Sleepiness Scale score of 18 and a BMI of 36 kg/m² undergoes a sleep study. What is the likely result?
explanation: Epworth 18 in an obese man suggests significant OSA; AHI 20/h is moderate (mild 5–14, moderate 15–29, severe ≥ 30).

orig.stem: A 55 year old man with excessive daytime sleepiness, an Epworth score of 18, and a BMI of 36 undergoes a sleep study. What is the likely result?
orig.explanation: 20 apnoea/hypopneas per hour An AHI of 20 is diagnostic for moderate obstructive sleep apnoea.

stem: A 72-year-old man with ischaemic heart disease, hypertension and childhood poliomyelitis has increasing breathlessness and nocturnal symptoms. His chest X-ray is under-inspired, a sleep study shows significant nocturnal hypoventilation, and arterial blood gases show decompensated type 2 respiratory failure. What is the likely diagnosis?
explanation: New respiratory muscle weakness decades after polio is post-polio syndrome, causing nocturnal then daytime hypercapnia; nocturnal NIV.

orig.stem: A 72 year old man with a history of ischaemic heart disease, hypertension, and childhood polio presents with increasing breathlessness and nocturnal symptoms. His CXR is under-inspired and a sleep study shows significant hypoventilation with decompensated type II respiratory failure on ABG. What is the likely diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Post-polio syndrome His history of polio and current hypoventilation suggest post-polio respiratory muscle weakness.

stem: Which of these associations between pathophysiological features and conditions is correct?
options: Eventration of diaphragm and foramen of Bochdalek
explanation: Spinal TB (Pott disease) causes angular thoracic kyphosis/kyphoscoliosis and can lead to restrictive ventilatory failure.

orig.stem: Which of these associations between pathophysiological features and conditions is correct?
options: Eventration of diaphragm and foramen of Bochdalek
orig.explanation: Thoracic kyphoscoliosis and tuberculosis Thoracic kyphoscoliosis is classically associated with tuberculous sequelae.

stem: At what lung volume does the outward recoil of the chest wall equal the inward elastic recoil of the lung?
explanation: At FRC the inward recoil of the lung equals the outward recoil of the chest wall; FRC rises in emphysema and falls in fibrosis or obesity.

orig.stem: At what lung volume does the outward recoil of the chest wall equal the inward elastic recoil of the lung?
orig.explanation: Functional residual capacity FRC is where outward chest wall recoil balances inward lung recoil.

stem: A 65-year-old man has stridor-like, low-pitched wheeze heard over the central airway. His flow–volume loop is shown. What is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
explanation: Flattening of both inspiratory and expiratory limbs of the flow–volume loop is a fixed central obstruction such as subglottic stenosis.

orig.stem: A 65-year-old man has a low-pitched wheeze over the mid-chest and a flow-volume curve showing fixed obstruction. What is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
orig.explanation: Subglottic stenosis A fixed obstruction on the flow-volume loop (box-shaped) is consistent with subglottic stenosis.

stem: A 22-year-old pregnant woman presents with acute dyspnoea. Arterial blood gas shows a raised A–a gradient and the chest X-ray is normal. What is the next best step in diagnosis and management?
options: Initiate therapy with amoxicillin for acute bronchitis
Perform a computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiogram
Reassure the patient that dyspnoea is normal
Treat with clonazepam for a panic attack
explanation: Acute dyspnoea with a raised A–a gradient in pregnancy needs imaging for PE (CTPA or V/Q); D-dimer is unhelpful in pregnancy.

orig.stem: A 22-year-old pregnant woman presents with acute dyspnea and a high A-a gradient on arterial blood gas with a normal chest x-ray. What is the next best step in diagnosis and management?
options: Initiate therapy with amoxicillin for acute bronchitis
Perform a computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiogram
Reassure the patient that dyspnea is normal
Treat with clonazepam for a panic attack
orig.explanation: Perform a computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiogram Suspected pulmonary embolism with an elevated A-a gradient should be confirmed by imaging (CTPA).

stem: Which of the following pulmonary function test results is consistent with myasthenia gravis?
options: Increased TLC, decreased vital capacity, decreased FEV1/FVC ratio
Decreased TLC, decreased VC, decreased RV, increased FEV1/FVC ratio, normal MIP
Decreased TLC, increased RV, normal FEV1/ FVC ratio, decreased MIP
Normal TLC, normal RV, normal FEV1/FVC ratio, normal MIP
explanation: Myasthenia: respiratory muscle weakness gives low TLC, raised RV, normal FEV1/FVC and low MIP.

orig.stem: Which of the following pulmonary function test results is consistent with Myasthenia gravis?
options: Increased TLC, decreased vital capacity, decreased FEV1/FVC ratio
Decreased TLC, decreased VC, decreased RV, increased FEV1/FVC ratio, normal MIP
Decreased TLC, increased RV, normal FEV1/ FVC ratio, decreased MIP
Normal TLC, normal RV, normal FEV1/FVC ratio, normal MIP
orig.explanation: Decreased TLC, increased RV, normal FEV1/FVC ratio, decreased MIP Myasthenia gravis causes a neuromuscular restrictive pattern with decreased maximal inspiratory pressure and air trapping.

stem: A 36-year-old woman rescued from a house fire remains obtunded, with seizures, hypotension and a bitter almond odour on her breath. Which test will confirm the diagnosis?
explanation: Coma, seizures, shock and bitter almond breath after a house fire suggest cyanide; red cell cyanide confirms, but give hydroxocobalamin without waiting.

orig.stem: A 36-year-old woman in a house fire remains obtunded with seizures, hypotension, and a bitter almond odor. Which test will yield the diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Red blood cell cyanide concentration The bitter almond odor and clinical picture suggest cyanide poisoning.

stem: A 28-year-old has recurrent sinus and lung infections and cystic fibrosis is suspected. Which finding best confirms the diagnosis?
options: DNA analysis showing one F508del allele
explanation: Sweat chloride ≥ 60 mmol/L on two occasions with a compatible picture confirms cystic fibrosis.

orig.stem: A 28-year-old has recurrent sinus and lung infections, suspect CF. Which finding best confirms the diagnosis?
options: DNA analysis showing one F508del allele
orig.explanation: Sweat chloride >60 mmol/L A sweat chloride value above 60 mmol/L is diagnostic for cystic fibrosis.

stem: A 42-year-old man has progressive dyspnoea and weight loss. Bronchoalveolar lavage returns milky fluid containing PAS-positive material. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Milky BAL with PAS-positive material is pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (usually autoimmune anti-GM-CSF); CT shows crazy paving.

orig.stem: A 42-year-old man with progressive dyspnea, weight loss, milky bronchoalveolar lavage fluid with PAS-positive debris. Diagnosis?
orig.explanation: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis PAS-positive, proteinaceous material in alveoli is characteristic of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.

stem: A patient has symptomatic pulmonary alveolar proteinosis with hypoxaemia. What is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Symptomatic PAP is treated by whole-lung lavage; inhaled GM-CSF is a newer option. Steroids do not help.

orig.stem: For the patient with pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, what is the most appropriate treatment?
orig.explanation: Whole-lung lavage Whole-lung lavage is the mainstay of treatment for pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.

stem: A 52-year-old man has obesity hypoventilation syndrome. Which statement is true?
options: Mutation of the PHOX2B gene is associated with this condition
CPAP alone is always adequate therapy
Intubation is mandatory for acute hypercapnia
Coexistent obstructive sleep apnoea occurs in only 25% of cases
Weight loss will lead to improvements in PaCO2 over time
explanation: Obesity hypoventilation (daytime PaCO2 > 6 kPa, BMI ≥ 30) improves with weight loss; CPAP or bilevel NIV at night.

orig.stem: A 52-year-old with obesity hypoventilation syndrome (Pickwickian). Which statement is true?
options: Gene PHOX2b is associated with this condition.
CPAP alone is always adequate therapy.
Intubation is mandatory for acute hypercapnia.
Coexistent OSA occurs in only 25% of cases.
Weight loss will lead to improvements in PaCO2 over time.
orig.explanation: Weight loss will lead to improvements in PaCO2 over time Sustained weight reduction improves obesity hypoventilation syndrome.

stem: A 52-year-old man with loud snoring, witnessed apnoeas, daytime sleepiness and a high BMI is thought to have obstructive sleep apnoea. He has no significant cardiopulmonary or neuromuscular disease and no symptoms of another sleep disorder. What is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: Uncomplicated adult with high probability of OSA: a home sleep apnoea test is the first step; full polysomnography if complex or inconclusive.

orig.stem: A 52-year-old man with loud snoring, high BMI, likely obstructive sleep apnea. Next step?
orig.explanation: Home sleep study A validated home sleep study is a cost-effective initial diagnostic tool for OSA.

stem: A 48-year-old man with moderate obstructive sleep apnoea refuses CPAP. Which statement about untreated obstructive sleep apnoea is correct?
options: It has no significant effect on mortality
It is not associated with depression
It increases the risk of motor vehicle accidents
It has no effect on blood pressure
Its complications are prevented by sleeping with extra pillows
explanation: Untreated OSA roughly doubles to triples the risk of road accidents; advise not to drive while sleepy.

orig.stem: A 48-year-old with OSA refuses CPAP. Which advice about untreated OSA is correct?
options: No significant effect on mortality risk
Minimal risk of motor vehicle accidents
orig.explanation: All of the above is good advice to give to the patient Untreated OSA is associated with increased cardiovascular risk, depression, and accidents; thus, all are important.

stem: The polysomnogram shown demonstrates a waxing and waning (crescendo–decrescendo) breathing pattern with central apnoeas. Which patient is most likely to have this pattern?
options: A 6-year-old with enlarged tonsils and adenoids
A 48-year-old obese man with loud snoring
A 52-year-old menopausal woman with frequent awakenings
A 68-year-old with atrial fibrillation and ischaemic cardiomyopathy (EF 15%), raised JVP and oedema
explanation: Crescendo–decrescendo breathing with central apnoeas is Cheyne–Stokes respiration, typical of advanced heart failure.

orig.stem: Which patient is most likely to have the Cheyne-Stokes breathing pattern shown?
options: A 6-year-old with enlarged tonsils and adenoids
A 48-year-old obese man with loud snoring
A 52-year-old menopausal woman with frequent awakenings
A 68-year-old with atrial fibrillation, EF 15%, JVP elevation, edema
orig.explanation: A 68-year-old with atrial fibrillation and ischemic cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 15% Cheyne-Stokes respiration is commonly seen in advanced heart failure.

stem: A 48-year-old man has symptomatic obstructive sleep apnoea with an apnoea–hypopnoea index of 42/hour. What is the most appropriate initial therapy?
explanation: AHI ≥ 30/h is severe OSA: CPAP is first line and improves sleepiness and BP. Oral devices suit mild disease; weight loss helps but is not enough alone.

orig.stem: A 48-year-old man has obstructive sleep apnea with an AHI of 42/hr. What is the most appropriate initial therapy?
orig.explanation: CPAP CPAP is the first-line treatment for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea.

stem: A 25-year-old with cystic fibrosis is referred for lung transplantation. What is the main impediment to long-term survival after transplantation?
explanation: Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (chronic allograft dysfunction) is the main barrier to long-term survival after lung transplant.

orig.stem: A 25-year-old with cystic fibrosis is referred for lung transplantation. The main impediment to long-term survival post-transplant is:
orig.explanation: Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome Chronic rejection in the form of bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome is the main barrier to long-term survival.

stem: A 42-year-old man in haemorrhagic shock has a lactate of 4.8 mmol/L. Which factor is least important in determining oxygen delivery to his tissues?
explanation: O2 delivery = cardiac output × (1.34 × Hb × SaO2 + small dissolved fraction), so PaO2 matters least once saturated.

orig.stem: A 42-year-old with hemorrhagic shock has a lactate of 4.8 mmol/L. Which factor is least important in oxygen delivery?
orig.explanation: PaO2 Oxygen content is more dependent on hemoglobin and saturation than on PaO2.

stem: A 67-year-old woman is intubated for pneumonia on a background of COPD. All of the following are measures that prevent ICU complications EXCEPT:
explanation: Tight glucose control (4.4–6.1 mmol/L) increased mortality (NICE-SUGAR); target ~8–10 mmol/L.

orig.stem: A 67-year-old woman intubated with pneumonia and COPD. All are measures to prevent ICU complications EXCEPT:
orig.explanation: Aggressive blood glucose control Overly tight glucose control has not improved outcomes and may cause harm.

stem: All of the following statements regarding shock pathophysiology are true EXCEPT:
options: Hypotension inhibits the vasomotor centre, reducing adrenergic output
Metabolic derangements raise extracellular osmolarity, pulling fluid from cells
Mitochondrial dysfunction leads to lactate accumulation
Proinflammatory mediators contribute to organ failure
Severe stress increases cortisol, promoting gluconeogenesis and lipolysis
explanation: Hypotension reduces baroreceptor firing, which increases (not inhibits) sympathetic output in shock.

orig.stem: All of the following statements regarding shock pathophysiology are true EXCEPT:
options: Hypotension inhibits the vasomotor center, reducing adrenergic output.
