A 21-year-old man has had productive cough and breathlessness for 2 years; he had severe measles in childhood. There is finger clubbing, cyanosis and bilateral coarse crackles.
items.explanation: Chronic productive cough after childhood measles with clubbing and coarse crackles is bronchiectasis; HRCT confirms.

items.stem: A 63-year-old man presents with massive haemoptysis after 3 months of breathlessness, cough and blood-streaked sputum. He is anaemic, with gynaecomastia and localised wheeze over the right middle zone.
items.explanation: Haemoptysis, anaemia and a fixed localised wheeze with gynaecomastia (ectopic hCG) is bronchial carcinoma.

items.stem: A 66-year-old man has sudden breathlessness with pink frothy sputum; he is cold, clammy and cyanosed, pulse 116/min regular, BP 90/55 mmHg, with bilateral fine inspiratory crackles.
items.explanation: Sudden pink frothy sputum, bilateral crackles, cold peripheries and hypotension is cardiogenic pulmonary oedema with shock.

items.stem: A 70-year-old woman has sudden breathlessness, fever, rigors, rusty sputum and left-sided pleuritic pain; there is reduced expansion, dullness and bronchial breathing over the left lower zone.
items.explanation: Fever, rusty sputum and pleuritic pain with dullness and bronchial breathing is lobar pneumonia (pneumococcal).

items.stem: A 33-year-old farmer has recurrent dry cough and breathlessness several hours after starting work; he is febrile with diffuse end-inspiratory crackles, and the chest X-ray shows mid-zone mottling.
items.explanation: Fever, cough and breathlessness 4–8 h after work in a farmer is acute extrinsic allergic alveolitis (farmer's lung).

items.stem: An 18-year-old student has had fever, night sweats and cough for 3 months and increasing breathlessness for 2 weeks; there is reduced expansion with stony dullness and absent breath sounds over the right middle and lower zones.
items.explanation: Stony dullness with absent breath sounds is a pleural effusion; with fever and sweats in a young person, likely tuberculous.

items.stem: A 24-year-old man has sudden left-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness; he is not cyanosed, pulse 96/min, SpO2 96%, with a resonant percussion note and absent breath sounds on the left.
items.explanation: Sudden pleuritic pain with hyper-resonance and absent breath sounds in a young man is primary spontaneous pneumothorax.

items.stem: A postoperative patient has sudden chest discomfort and breathlessness; he is cyanosed with a raised JVP, pulse 112/min small volume, BP 90/60 mmHg and SpO2 86%, and heart and chest examination are otherwise unremarkable.
items.explanation: Post-operative hypoxaemia, raised JVP and hypotension with a clear chest is massive PE: systemic thrombolysis.

items.stem: A 62-year-old man with an MI 5 days ago suddenly becomes breathless; pulse 118/min, BP 85/50 mmHg with pulsus paradoxus, a raised JVP and soft heart sounds.
items.explanation: Hypotension, pulsus paradoxus, raised JVP and soft heart sounds days after MI is tamponade (free-wall rupture).

items.stem: A 25-year-old man has sudden chest discomfort, breathlessness and syncope while playing football; the pulse is small-volume, the apex forceful with a fourth heart sound, and there is an apical pansystolic murmur and a mid-systolic murmur at the base.
items.explanation: Exertional syncope with S4, basal ejection murmur and apical MR murmur in a young athlete is HOCM.

items.stem: A 16-year-old girl has recurrent episodes of dry cough and breathlessness; there is expiratory wheeze throughout the chest and the chest X-ray is normal.
items.explanation: Recurrent cough and breathlessness with widespread wheeze and a normal CXR is asthma; confirm variable obstruction.

items.explanation: A left atrial mass obstructing the mitral valve with syncope and clubbing is atrial myxoma; excise surgically.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman has fever, fatigue and breathlessness; there is finger clubbing and a new mitral regurgitant murmur.
items.explanation: Fever with a new regurgitant murmur and clubbing suggests subacute infective endocarditis; blood cultures and echo.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman has high remittent fever, rigors, cough, sputum and pleuritic chest pain; there is finger clubbing with stony dullness and absent air entry over the right lower zone.
items.explanation: Swinging fever, pleuritic pain and stony dullness with clubbing is empyema; aspirate (pus, pH < 7.2) and drain.

items.stem: A 36-year-old man has a chronic cough with yellow sputum, sometimes blood-stained; there is clubbing of fingers and toes, weight loss and bibasal coarse crackles, and he has 6 years of infertility.
items.explanation: Chronic purulent sputum with clubbing, crackles and infertility is bronchiectasis (CF or ciliary dyskinesia).

items.stem: A 55-year-old woman has progressive cough and breathlessness, with finger clubbing, restricted expansion and bilateral fine inspiratory crackles.
items.explanation: Progressive dry cough with clubbing and bilateral Velcro crackles is idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman with finger clubbing has tremor, palpitations, weight loss, exophthalmos and pretibial myxoedema.
items.explanation: Clubbing (thyroid acropachy) with exophthalmos and pretibial myxoedema is specific to Graves' disease.

theme: Treatment of respiratory emergencies and diseases

items.stem: A 34-year-old man has severe breathlessness after a car accident; there is central cyanosis, RR 28/min, pulse 124/min small volume, BP 80/50 mmHg, chest expansion 2 cm, a resonant percussion note throughout and absent air entry and breath sounds on the right.
items.explanation: Resonant silent hemithorax with hypotension after trauma is tension pneumothorax: decompress, then chest tube.

items.stem: A patient with an acute asthma attack has central cyanosis. He is given IV hydrocortisone, nebulised salbutamol plus ipratropium and 2 g of IV magnesium sulfate; a few hours later the blood gases show PaO2 7.4 kPa (54 mmHg) and PaCO2 5.8 kPa (44 mmHg).
items.explanation: PaO2 < 8 kPa with a normal PaCO2 despite maximal asthma therapy means tiring: ICU for intubation and ventilation.

items.stem: A 65-year-old bed-bound patient suddenly becomes severely breathless; there is cyanosis, a raised JVP, pulse 118/min small volume, BP 80/50 mmHg, a right ventricular gallop and a loud P2.
items.explanation: Sudden breathlessness with RV strain and SBP < 90 in a bed-bound patient is massive PE: alteplase.

items.stem: A 60-year-old woman has had a dry cough and breathlessness for 2 months; there is finger clubbing, central cyanosis, reduced expansion and bilateral fine inspiratory crackles.
items.explanation: Dry cough, clubbing and fine crackles is IPF; pirfenidone or nintedanib slows FVC decline.

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman takes a new drug prescribed for knee pain and develops generalised itching, severe breathlessness, swelling of the face, eyes, lips and tongue, and widespread wheeze.
items.explanation: Itch, facial/tongue swelling and wheeze after a new drug is anaphylaxis: IM adrenaline 0.5 mg, repeat after 5 min if needed.

items.stem: A 70-year-old woman treated for left lower lobe pneumonia is still febrile with rigors after a week of antibiotics; there is stony dullness and absent breath sounds at the left base, and pleural aspiration yields turbid fluid with pH 7.0.
items.explanation: Persistent fever with a turbid effusion of pH 7.0 after pneumonia is empyema: chest drain plus antibiotics.

items.stem: An older man with 40 pack-years of smoking has breathlessness for 4 years, worse over the last 3; there is reduced chest movement with coarse crackles and wheeze.
items.explanation: Progressive breathlessness in a 40 pack-year smoker with reduced chest expansion, wheeze and coarse crackles is COPD. Diagnosis is confirmed by post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7.

items.stem: A 58-year-old heavy smoker with chronic cough and sputum recovered poorly from a recent pneumonia; his sputum is increasing and occasionally bloody, and the chest X-ray shows a right hilar opacity.
items.explanation: A persistent hilar opacity with bloody sputum in a heavy smoker suggests central carcinoma: CT, then bronchoscopy and biopsy.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman has had a chronic cough with white-grey sputum for 2 months with low-grade fever, sweats and marked weight loss; there are crackles at the right apex and bilateral apical opacities on chest X-ray.
items.explanation: Chronic cough, sweats, weight loss and apical opacities is TB: sputum for AFB smear, culture and NAAT.

items.stem: A 64-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes has severe retrosternal chest pain for 6 hours radiating to the left shoulder, with nausea and vomiting; the ECG shows ST depression in V4–V6.
items.explanation: Ischaemic pain with ST depression: high-sensitivity troponin to separate NSTEMI from unstable angina.

items.stem: A 16-year-old student has had a night-time cough for 2 months, since moving to a new house; amoxicillin did not help. He does not smoke, and one of his brothers has hay fever.
items.explanation: Nocturnal cough after moving house in an atopic non-smoker suggests cough-variant asthma: spirometry with reversibility (± FeNO).

items.stem: A 38-year-old man has recurrent episodes of headache, palpitations and vomiting; he is pale and sweaty, with BP 190/110 mmHg sitting and 150/90 mmHg standing.
items.explanation: Paroxysmal headache, palpitations and sweating with hypertension and postural drop suggest phaeochromocytoma: metanephrines.

items.stem: A 62-year-old woman has progressive exertional breathlessness and dry cough for months; there is finger clubbing and chest expansion of 2 cm. FVC 1.65 L (predicted 2.75 L), FEV1 1.45 L (predicted 2.3 L).
items.explanation: Restriction (FVC 60%, ratio ~0.88) with clubbing is IPF; pirfenidone is recommended at FVC 50–80%.

items.stem: A middle-aged woman is severely breathless after an accident; she is cyanosed, pulse 120/min, BP 90/55 mmHg, with absent air entry on the left and the mediastinum shifted to the right.
items.explanation: Absent air entry with the mediastinum shifted away and hypotension after trauma is tension pneumothorax: decompress and drain.

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman attends her GP for annual review of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; BP 165/95 mmHg on furosemide and aspirin. Which medication should be added?
items.explanation: HFrEF on furosemide and aspirin with BP 165/95: add an ACE inhibitor (lisinopril) for survival and BP.

items.explanation: New COPD with exertional breathlessness: start an as-needed short-acting bronchodilator (salbutamol), stop smoking, rehab.

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman with long-standing COPD presents with breathlessness and cough productive of coloured sputum.
items.explanation: Infective COPD exacerbation: 28% oxygen, nebulised salbutamol + ipratropium, prednisolone and oral amoxicillin.

items.stem: A 70-year-old man with an acute severe exacerbation of COPD does not respond to oxygen, nebulised bronchodilators and oral steroids; on 28% oxygen his ABG shows pH 7.28, PO2 8 kPa and PCO2 9.4 kPa.
items.explanation: COPD exacerbation with persistent acidosis (pH 7.28, PaCO2 9.4) despite treatment: non-invasive ventilation (BiPAP).

items.stem: A 65-year-old non-smoker with advanced COPD on maximal inhaled therapy is still breathless; his PaO2 when clinically stable, measured twice 3 weeks apart, is 6.5 kPa.
items.explanation: Stable PaO2 6.5 kPa twice in a non-smoker with COPD: long-term oxygen therapy (≥ 15 h/day) improves survival.

items.stem: A 55-year-old patient with COPD needs regular add-on therapy because bronchodilators do not control his symptoms.
items.explanation: COPD still symptomatic on short-acting bronchodilators: add a LABA + LAMA inhaler.

items.stem: A 34-year-old woman with nasal obstruction develops cough, haemoptysis and pleuritic chest pain; her chest radiograph shows multiple nodular masses.

items.stem: A 22-year-old man has fever, night sweats, weight loss and cough productive of cupfuls of blood; Ziehl–Neelsen stain is positive for acid-fast bacilli.
items.explanation: Fever, sweats, weight loss and haemoptysis with AFB on ZN stain is pulmonary TB.

items.stem: A tall, thin 19-year-old woman who has had little previous health care complains mainly of reduced vision. She has a strong pulse, BP 180/70 mmHg and a high-pitched, blowing, early diastolic decrescendo murmur.
items.explanation: Tall thin woman with lens dislocation (Marfan), wide pulse pressure and early diastolic decrescendo murmur: aortic regurgitation from root dilatation.

items.stem: A 23-year-old graduate student has had extreme fatigue and a vague sense of feeling ill for a few weeks; he is slightly agitated. BP 110/70 mmHg, pulse 100/min, temperature 38.0 °C. The neck veins are distended with prominent v waves, and a holosystolic murmur at the left sternal border intensifies on inspiration.
items.explanation: Fever with prominent v waves and a pansystolic murmur louder on inspiration is tricuspid regurgitation, likely right-sided endocarditis.

items.stem: An 18-year-old man is sent from his physical education class with dizziness and palpitations after exercise; his instructor thinks he is faking. Vital signs are normal. He has a rapidly rising carotid pulse, an S4 and a harsh systolic crescendo–decrescendo murmur beginning well after S1, best heard at the lower left sternal border.
items.explanation: Exertional dizziness with a brisk carotid upstroke, S4 and crescendo–decrescendo murmur at the lower left sternal border is HCM; AS has a slow-rising pulse.

items.stem: A 72-year-old man has a 2-hour history of chest pain, acute ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF, and sinus bradycardia at 40/min. His BP is 80/40 mmHg.
items.explanation: Symptomatic sinus bradycardia with hypotension in inferior STEMI: IV atropine 500 µg (to 3 mg) first; pacing or isoprenaline if it fails; reperfuse.

items.stem: A 58-year-old female smoker is admitted to the ICU with respiratory distress due to pneumonia. Her course is complicated by an anterior myocardial infarction, and she is on the highest beta-blocker dose her lungs tolerate. Serum potassium and magnesium are normal. She now has 10–12 ventricular premature beats per hour, occasional couplets and a few short runs of non-sustained ventricular tachycardia; her BP and oxygen saturation remain stable.
items.explanation: Asymptomatic ectopics and short NSVT with stable haemodynamics: observe, continue beta-blocker and correct K/Mg. Prophylactic antiarrhythmics do not help.

items.stem: A 60-year-old man on his first day in the coronary care unit after a myocardial infarction develops an accelerated idioventricular rhythm at a rate of 80/min.

items.explanation: Radiofemoral delay with weak femorals and arm hypertension is the hallmark of coarctation; rib notching on CXR.

items.stem: A bounding pulse, warm peripheries, a flapping tremor and drowsiness in a breathless patient with COPD.
items.explanation: Bounding pulse, warm peripheries, flap and drowsiness in COPD reflect acute CO2 retention: ABG, target SpO2 88–92%, NIV if acidotic.

items.stem: A collapsing pulse with a wide pulse pressure and a 'pistol-shot' sound heard over the femoral arteries.
items.explanation: Collapsing pulse, wide pulse pressure and pistol-shot femorals (Traube) indicate severe aortic regurgitation.

items.stem: A slow-rising pulse with a narrow pulse pressure, a heaving apex beat and a fourth heart sound.
items.explanation: A slow-rising pulse with a narrow pulse pressure, a heaving (pressure-loaded) apex and an S4 indicate severe aortic stenosis. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy gives a jerky pulse instead.

items.stem: Pulsus paradoxus with hypotension, a raised JVP with an absent y descent and muffled heart sounds.
items.explanation: Pulsus paradoxus, hypotension, raised JVP with absent y descent and muffled sounds is tamponade; Kussmaul sign and knock suggest constriction.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman has a pansystolic murmur best heard at the apex, radiating to the axilla.
items.explanation: A pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla is mitral regurgitation. A VSD murmur is at the left sternal edge and does not radiate to the axilla.

items.stem: A 29-year-old man has an ejection click and an ejection systolic murmur in the right 2nd intercostal space, with a soft second heart sound.
items.explanation: Ejection click with an aortic-area ejection murmur in a young adult suggests bicuspid aortic valve; a soft A2 means significant stenosis.

items.stem: A 12-year-old boy has a soft ejection systolic murmur in the left 2nd intercostal space with fixed splitting of the second heart sound.
items.explanation: Soft pulmonary flow murmur with fixed S2 splitting is ASD; the murmur is from increased flow across the pulmonary valve.

items.stem: An 11-year-old boy has a harsh ejection systolic murmur heard best posteriorly between the scapulae; his upper-limb blood pressure is raised.
items.explanation: Systolic murmur loudest between the scapulae with arm hypertension is coarctation; check radiofemoral delay.

items.stem: A 7-year-old boy has a harsh ejection systolic murmur with a thrill in the left 2nd intercostal space and a soft second heart sound.
items.explanation: Harsh ejection murmur with thrill in the left 2nd space and a soft delayed P2 is congenital pulmonary stenosis; balloon valvuloplasty.

items.stem: The chest X-ray shows a double shadow at the right heart border, a prominent left atrial appendage and elevation of the left main bronchus.
items.explanation: Double right heart border, prominent LA appendage and elevated left main bronchus mean left atrial enlargement, classically mitral stenosis.

items.stem: CXR shows Kerley B lines, bat wing shadowing, prominent upper lobe vessels and cardiomegaly.
items.explanation: Upper-lobe diversion, Kerley B lines, bat-wing shadowing and cardiomegaly are the CXR signs of left heart failure.

items.stem: The chest X-ray shows the trachea deviated to the right, with the horizontal fissure and right hilum displaced upwards.
items.explanation: Trachea pulled right with elevated horizontal fissure and right hilum is right upper lobe collapse; bronchoscopy to exclude carcinoma.

items.stem: The chest X-ray shows bilateral reticular shadowing with small lung volumes, predominantly in the subpleural areas of both lower zones.
items.explanation: Bilateral subpleural lower-zone reticulation with small lungs is IPF (UIP pattern); HRCT shows honeycombing.

items.stem: The chest X-ray of a man with fever and foul-smelling sputum after an alcoholic binge shows a round cavity with an air–fluid level.

items.stem: Tapping apex beat, loud S1, mid-diastolic murmur loudest at the apex in expiration lying on the left side.
items.explanation: Tapping apex, loud S1 and apical mid-diastolic rumble (left lateral, expiration) is mitral stenosis.

items.stem: Heaving undisplaced apex beat, absent A2 with ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids.
items.explanation: Heaving undisplaced apex, absent A2 and ejection murmur to the carotids indicate severe calcific aortic stenosis.

items.stem: Pansystolic murmur heard best at lower left sternal edge during inspiration in a patient with pulsatile hepatomegaly.
items.explanation: Pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal edge louder on inspiration with a pulsatile liver is tricuspid regurgitation.

items.stem: Displaced, volume-overloaded apex. Soft S1, pansystolic murmur at apex radiating to axilla.
items.explanation: Displaced volume-loaded apex, soft S1 and apical pansystolic murmur to the axilla is chronic mitral regurgitation.

items.stem: A 25-year-old man has a left parasternal heave and a harsh pansystolic murmur with a thrill at the lower left sternal edge, also audible at the apex. The murmur does not vary with respiration and the JVP is normal.
items.explanation: Harsh pansystolic murmur with thrill at the lower left sternal edge, not varying with respiration and with a normal JVP, is a VSD.

items.stem: Elevated JVP with absent pulsation.
items.explanation: A raised non-pulsatile JVP means obstruction above the RA: superior vena cava obstruction (lung cancer, lymphoma).

items.stem: Giant systolic ‘v’ waves.
items.explanation: Giant systolic v waves occur when the RV ejects back through an incompetent tricuspid valve: tricuspid regurgitation.

items.stem: Large ‘a’ waves and slow ‘y’ descent in JVP. Patient has ascites.
items.explanation: Large a waves with a slow y descent and ascites indicate tricuspid stenosis, usually rheumatic with mitral stenosis.

items.stem: Cannon ‘a’ waves.
items.explanation: Cannon a waves (atrium contracting against a closed tricuspid valve) indicate AV dissociation, typically complete heart block.

items.stem: Raised JVP that rises on inspiration.
items.explanation: A JVP rising on inspiration (Kussmaul sign) is classic of constrictive pericarditis.

items.stem: A 26-year-old woman presents acutely unwell with shortness of breath. Her ECG shows sinus tachycardia, deep S waves in I, inverted T waves in III and Q waves in III.
items.explanation: Sinus tachycardia is the commonest ECG finding in PE; S1Q3T3 reflects RV strain but is insensitive. Use Wells, D-dimer and CTPA.

items.stem: An ECG shows a dominant R wave with an RSR' pattern in V1, inverted T waves in V1–V3, deep wide S waves in I and V6, and a QRS duration of 140 ms.
items.explanation: RSR' in V1 with T inversion V1–V3, broad S in I and V6 and QRS ≥ 120 ms is right bundle-branch block.

items.stem: Prolonged P–R interval, depressed ST, flattened T waves, prominent U waves.
items.explanation: Hypokalaemia: long PR, ST depression, flat T waves and prominent U waves.

items.stem: An ECG shows sinus rhythm with broad (0.14 s), notched, bifid P waves best seen in lead II and a biphasic P wave with a deep negative terminal component in V1.
items.explanation: Broad bifid P mitrale in II with a deep negative terminal P in V1 indicates left atrial enlargement, classically mitral stenosis.

items.stem: A 65-year-old man presents with chest pain radiating to the jaw. The ECG shows ST segment elevation in II, III and aVF, with T-wave inversion in V5 and V6.
items.explanation: ST elevation in II, III and aVF is inferior MI (usually RCA): primary PCI and check V4R for RV infarction.

items.stem: The ECG of a 55-year-old man being treated for hypertension with ramipril and spironolactone shows tall tented T waves.
items.explanation: Tall tented T waves are the earliest sign of hyperkalaemia (ACEi + spironolactone); check K⁺ and give IV calcium if ECG changes.

items.stem: A 34-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a road traffic accident in which his chest struck the steering wheel. His neck veins are distended, the trachea is central and breath sounds are equal on both sides. He then loses his pulse while the monitor still shows organised electrical activity (pulseless electrical activity).
items.explanation: PEA after blunt chest trauma with distended neck veins, central trachea and equal breath sounds is tamponade: immediate pericardiocentesis.

items.stem: An 85-year-old man with pneumonia complains of palpitations. The ECG shows an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with absent P waves.
items.explanation: Irregularly irregular narrow complexes without P waves is atrial fibrillation, often triggered by acute illness such as pneumonia.

items.stem: ECG of a 45-year-old man with sarcoidosis shows an ‘M’ pattern in V5 and inverted T waves in I, aVL and V5–V6.
items.explanation: Broad QRS with M-shaped R in V5–V6 and lateral T inversion is LBBB; cardiac sarcoid infiltrates the conducting system.

items.stem: ECG of an 8-year-old girl shows normal P waves and QRS complexes but shows T-wave inversion in V1.
items.explanation: T-wave inversion in V1 (often V2–V3) is a normal juvenile pattern in children.

items.explanation: Inferior STEMI < 12 h: aspirin, P2Y12 loading and primary PCI within 120 min; fibrinolysis only if PCI is not available in time.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman collapses after a flight with breathlessness and right-sided pleuritic chest pain.
items.explanation: Collapse with breathlessness and pleuritic pain after a flight is PE: oxygen, therapeutic anticoagulation and fluids; thrombolyse if unstable.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man with chronic glomerulonephritis presents with severe headache, papilloedema and bilateral retinal haemorrhages. His BP is 240/132 mmHg.
items.explanation: Malignant hypertension (papilloedema, haemorrhages) from glomerulonephritis: IV labetalol in a monitored bed, lowering MAP ≤ 25%. Avoid sublingual nifedipine.

items.explanation: A clinic reading of 140/90–179/119 must be confirmed by ABPM (or HBPM) before diagnosis (NICE NG136); then treat promptly given his diabetes.

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman has a blood pressure persistently above 160/90 mmHg over a 2-month assessment period with her GP, despite repeated lifestyle advice. She is otherwise fit and well and asymptomatic.
items.explanation: Confirmed persistent hypertension despite lifestyle change needs drug treatment started in primary care; admission is unnecessary.

items.stem: A 67-year-old man presents to the emergency department with headaches. His blood pressure is 220/120 mmHg. Fundoscopy shows some arteriovenous nipping but no haemorrhages, exudates or papilloedema, and he has no other symptoms or signs of acute organ damage.
items.explanation: BP 220/120 without acute organ damage is hypertensive urgency: start oral treatment and review early; rapid lowering is dangerous.

items.explanation: BP 240/140 with papilloedema, haemorrhages and confusion is a hypertensive emergency: HDU, arterial line, IV labetalol/nitroprusside.

items.stem: An 80-year-old woman with ischaemic heart disease presents to the emergency department with a 3-month history of worsening breathlessness and swollen ankles. Her ECG shows no abnormality, but you suspect heart failure. Which simple blood test could effectively rule out heart failure?
items.explanation: A normal NT-proBNP (< 400 ng/L non-acute) makes heart failure very unlikely; above 2000 ng/L, echo within 2 weeks.

items.stem: An 80-year-old woman with suspected heart failure has a raised NT-proBNP. Which investigation should be requested next to confirm chronic heart failure?
items.explanation: Transthoracic Doppler echo confirms heart failure and its type (EF), valve disease and wall motion.

items.stem: An 80-year-old woman has newly confirmed heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and is starting a beta-blocker. Which class of drug acting on the renin–angiotensin system is recommended first line, reduces mortality and helps reverse left ventricular remodelling?
items.explanation: An ACE inhibitor with a beta-blocker is first line in HFrEF, reducing mortality and reversing remodelling; ARB if intolerant.

items.stem: An 80-year-old woman admitted with chronic heart failure is still breathless with ankle oedema 2 days after admission. Which class of diuretic is the first-line symptomatic treatment of fluid overload in chronic heart failure?
items.explanation: Loop diuretics are first-line for fluid overload in heart failure; thiazides are add-on for resistance.

items.stem: An 80-year-old woman with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction remains breathless, especially when lying flat, 6 months after diagnosis. She takes enalapril, bisoprolol, aspirin and furosemide at optimised doses, and her potassium and renal function are normal. Which additional treatment should be prescribed?
items.explanation: Still symptomatic on ACEi and beta-blocker: add spironolactone (RALES ~30% mortality reduction) and an SGLT2 inhibitor; check K⁺.

notes: source key: J, I, H, F, H

items.stem: A 34-year-old woman has been suffering from profuse diarrhoea and vomiting for 4 days. She is now complaining of extreme muscle weakness and muscle cramps.
items.explanation: Diarrhoea and vomiting cause hypokalaemia: weakness, cramps and prominent U waves. Replace K⁺ and check magnesium.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man known to be in end-stage renal failure presents to the emergency department feeling generally unwell and experiencing palpitations. He admits to missing his last haemodialysis appointment as he went away on holiday.
items.explanation: Missed dialysis causes hyperkalaemia, first seen as tall tented T waves; give IV calcium, insulin–glucose and urgent dialysis.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman presents with left-sided chest pain that is worse on breathing in. She is also experiencing shortness of breath on exertion and has coughed up a small amount of frank blood. She is otherwise well, with no significant past medical history. Her only regular medication is the oral contraceptive pill.
items.explanation: Pleuritic pain, haemoptysis and breathlessness on the pill suggest PE, whose commonest ECG finding is sinus tachycardia; confirm with CTPA.

items.stem: An 85-year-old man with dementia is brought to the emergency department by the ambulance after escaping from his care home during the night. He was found wandering on the local moors by a farmer in the early hours of the morning. He is shivering and confused. His core temperature is 31°C.
items.explanation: Hypothermia (31 °C) produces J (Osborn) waves at the QRS–ST junction; rewarm gently as the cold heart is prone to VF.

items.stem: A 32-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a road traffic collision. He has no obvious injuries but is anxious and in pain, with a regular pulse of 118 beats/min.
items.explanation: Pain and anxiety after trauma cause sinus tachycardia; persistent tachycardia should prompt a search for occult bleeding.

notes: source key: B, H, G, F, J

items.stem: A 68-year-old woman had an inferior myocardial infarction 2 days ago. She has become acutely short of breath and is coughing up pink frothy sputum. There is a new pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla, and bilateral crackles are heard at the lung bases.
items.explanation: Pulmonary oedema with a new apical pansystolic murmur 2–7 days after inferior MI is acute MR from posteromedial papillary rupture; urgent echo and surgery.

items.stem: A 58-year-old man complains of central chest pain, fever and lethargy 4 weeks after suffering a myocardial infarction. The chest pain is worse on inspiration, is stabbing in nature, and is relieved by ibuprofen and sitting forward.
items.explanation: Fever and pleuritic pain relieved by sitting forward 4 weeks after MI is Dressler syndrome; aspirin/NSAID plus colchicine.

items.stem: You are asked to review a 72-year-old woman who had a myocardial infarction 12 hours ago. Her heart rate is 40 beats/min and her blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg. The ECG shows abnormally wide QRS complexes occurring at a rate of 40 beats/min and P-waves occurring at a rate of 90 beats/min. There is no relationship between the P-waves and QRS complexes.
items.explanation: P waves at 90/min unrelated to broad QRS at 40/min is complete heart block; with hypotension give atropine and temporary pacing.

items.stem: A 66-year-old man, known to have had an anterior myocardial infarction 2 days previously, collapses. On examination, you notice that he has a raised jugular venous pressure that rises with inspiration. Auscultation seems normal. His blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg and his heart rate is 100 beats/min. The ECG shows sinus tachycardia with small QRS complexes.
items.explanation: Collapse 2–5 days after anterior MI with hypotension, raised JVP and small QRS complexes is tamponade from free-wall rupture.

items.stem: A 60-year-old man who had a myocardial infarction 4 weeks ago presents to his GP complaining of increasing shortness of breath since discharge. It is worse at night time on lying flat, and he occasionally wakes up acutely short of breath in the early hours of the morning.
items.explanation: Orthopnoea and PND weeks after MI indicate left ventricular failure; echo, diuretics and prognostic HF therapy.

notes: source key: F, J, E, B, G

items.stem: A 30-year-old man presents to the emergency department with headache and muscle weakness. He also complains of increased thirst and urine output. Apart from a blood pressure of 190/95 mmHg, examination is normal. Serum potassium is 2.2 mmol/L, sodium 150 mmol/L, urea 4.3 mmol/L and creatinine 69 μmol/L.
items.explanation: Hypertension with K⁺ 2.2, high-normal sodium and polyuria is Conn's syndrome; aldosterone:renin ratio, then adrenal CT and venous sampling.

items.stem: A previously fit and well 35-year-old female doctor presents to her GP with a history of ‘panic attacks’, during which she feels extremely anxious and experiences palpitations, chest tightness and headaches. While in the surgery, she experiences a similar episode, becoming flushed and anxious. Her heart rate was 120 beats/min and her blood pressure reached 185/80 mmHg.
items.explanation: Paroxysmal anxiety, palpitations, headache and flushing with hypertension suggest phaeochromocytoma; measure metanephrines, alpha-block first.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman with known Turner’s syndrome presents to her GP with recurrent nose bleeds. On examination, her blood pressure is 190/95 mmHg. Auscultation reveals a mid-late systolic murmur best heard in between the shoulder blades.
items.explanation: Turner syndrome with hypertension and an interscapular systolic murmur is coarctation; check radiofemoral delay.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man was found to have a persistently raised blood pressure by his GP. On examination, a vague mass could be felt on the left side of the abdomen. He mentioned that his father died at 26 years of age following a ‘brain haemorrhage’.
items.explanation: Hypertension, flank mass and a family history of early brain haemorrhage (berry aneurysm) point to ADPKD; confirm by renal ultrasound.

items.stem: A 55-year-old woman is noted to have an elevated blood pressure on three separate occasions by her GP. She has a recent history of persisting acne and hirsutism, for which a dermatology referral has been made. Marked bruising is observed on examination.
items.explanation: Hypertension with acne, hirsutism and bruising suggests Cushing's syndrome; screen with overnight dexamethasone suppression, then ACTH.

items.stem: A 67-year-old man presents with symptoms of acute left ventricular failure. On examination, you notice that his heart rate is 120 beats/min. On auscultation, there are more than two heart sounds present, but you cannot distinguish them from each other.
items.explanation: In acute LVF at fast rates S3 and S4 fuse into one loud extra sound: a summation gallop.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a severe headache. He is known to have mitral valve regurgitation.
items.explanation: MR gives a pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla; loudness does not reflect severity.

items.stem: You are called to see an 87-year-old female inpatient who is complaining of chest pain. On examination, you notice a murmur. A brief look in her hospital notes confirms that she has known ischaemic heart disease, hypertension and aortic valve sclerosis.
items.explanation: Aortic sclerosis gives an ejection murmur at the right 2nd space without carotid radiation, with a normal pulse and A2.

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman with known systemic lupus erythematosus presents with central chest pain that is very similar to the pain that she feels when suffering from pericarditis. Echocardiography demonstrates a pericardial effusion that is likely to be chronic. On auscultation, the heart sounds do not sound as they should.
items.explanation: A large chronic pericardial effusion muffles the heart sounds; look for tamponade signs (pulsus paradoxus, raised JVP).

items.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with abdominal pain. He is known to have Marfan’s syndrome with advanced aortic valve regurgitation.
items.explanation: Severe AR can cause an Austin Flint murmur (apical mid-diastolic rumble from the jet hitting the mitral leaflet), without opening snap.

items.stem: On examination of a 75-year-old man who presented with shortness of breath, mild chest pain and palpitations, you note that he has an irregularly irregular pulse.
items.explanation: An irregularly irregular pulse is characteristic of AF; confirm by ECG and assess CHA2DS2-VASc.

items.stem: You are asked to see a 37-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with chest pain. He is extremely anxious, as both his father and grandfather died suddenly in their 30s. On examination, you notice a pale ring around his cornea and yellow plaques just below his eye. When you mention these findings to the patient, he says that he has similar lesions on his elbows and within his Achilles’ tendon.
items.explanation: Arcus, xanthelasma and tendon xanthomas with premature family CAD is heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (~1 in 250); cascade testing.

items.stem: On examination of a 50-year-old man who presented with fever, weight loss and lethargy, you notice small linear red lesions beneath his fingernails.
items.explanation: Fever, weight loss and splinter haemorrhages suggest subacute bacterial endocarditis; 3 blood cultures and echo.

items.stem: While examining a 62-year-old man who presented in a state of collapse, you note that his heart rate is only 40 beats/min. Additionally, there appears to be an abnormally large wave within the jugular venous pressure waveform.
items.explanation: Bradycardia with intermittent cannon a waves and collapse is complete heart block (Stokes–Adams): permanent pacing.

items.stem: While examining a 65-year-old man who is being treated for a suspected type A aortic dissection with sudden acute pulmonary oedema, you hear a short, soft early diastolic murmur. He is tachycardic and hypotensive, and his pulse pressure is not widened.
items.explanation: Acute AR (e.g. type A dissection) causes shock with a short soft diastolic murmur and no wide pulse pressure; needs emergency surgery.

notes: source key: I, N, G, K, M

items.stem: A 64-year-old man develops a dry cough about 1 week after starting a new blood pressure medication.
items.explanation: ACE inhibitors (ramipril) cause dry cough in ~10% via bradykinin; switch to an ARB.

items.stem: A 58-year-old woman develops bilateral swelling of her ankles 2 weeks after her GP has prescribed an antihypertensive drug.
items.explanation: Amlodipine causes dose-dependent ankle oedema from precapillary dilatation; it responds poorly to diuretics.

items.stem: A 74-year-old man is being treated for left ventricular failure as an inpatient. He is noticed to have U-waves on a routine ECG.
items.explanation: Furosemide causes hypokalaemia, giving U waves, flat T waves and ST depression.

items.stem: A 56-year-old woman presents to her GP with profound muscular pain, weakness and fever 5 days after beginning a course of an unknown ‘heart tablet’.
items.explanation: Statins (simvastatin) can cause myositis and rhabdomyolysis, especially with interacting drugs; stop it and check CK.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man who is being treated for ST-elevation myocardial infarction in the emergency department resuscitation room suddenly becomes hypotensive.
items.explanation: Streptokinase commonly causes hypotension and allergy (bacterial protein) and must not be reused because of antibodies.

notes: source key: A, B, C, G, D

items.stem: This drug is used during cardiac arrest to increase coronary perfusion pressure.
items.explanation: Adrenaline's alpha effect raises aortic diastolic and coronary perfusion pressure; 1 mg IV every 3–5 min.

items.stem: This anti-arrhythmic drug is used in the standard management of ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia.
items.explanation: Amiodarone 300 mg IV after the third shock (150 mg after the fifth) is the standard antiarrhythmic in VF/pVT.

items.stem: This drug is the first-line treatment of peri-arrest bradycardia with adverse features, given as 500 micrograms IV and repeated to a maximum of 3 mg.
items.explanation: Atropine 500 µg IV (to 3 mg) blocks vagal tone and is first-line for unstable bradycardia; no longer used in asystole/PEA.

items.stem: This drug is given in cardiac arrest or peri-arrest instability caused by polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (torsades de pointes), or when hypomagnesaemia is suspected.
items.explanation: Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV suppresses torsades de pointes and corrects hypomagnesaemia.

items.stem: This drug should be considered for use in cardiac arrest secondary to hyperkalaemia.
items.explanation: In hyperkalaemic arrest IV calcium stabilises the myocardium; it does not lower K⁺ (insulin–glucose, dialysis do).

notes: source key: B, G, D, C, H

items.stem: A 60-year-old man with known hypertension presents to the emergency department with a 2-hour history of central chest pain and interscapular back pain. Over the next 30 minutes, he develops slurred speech and reduced power and sensation on his left side.
items.explanation: Tearing chest and interscapular pain then a stroke in a hypertensive man suggests dissection into the carotids; CT aortography, no thrombolysis.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman with a known congenital heart defect presents to her GP with a 4-week history of left-sided chest pain and palpitations that are worse on exertion. The pain does not radiate, has no other associated symptoms and is not worse on inspiration. On examination, there is a mid-systolic click best heard at the apex on auscultation of the heart.
items.explanation: Atypical chest pain and palpitations with an apical mid-systolic click is mitral valve prolapse; echo confirms.

items.stem: A 70-year-old man presents to his GP following an episode of central crushing chest pain that started 30 minutes after going to bed. The pain did not radiate and there were no associated symptoms. Following two puffs of sublingual glyceryl trinitrate spray, his chest pain resolved. The ECG shows no abnormalities. This is the third time in the last 2 weeks that these symptoms have occurred on going to bed.
items.explanation: Angina on lying flat (decubitus angina) reflects increased venous return and implies severe CAD or LV dysfunction; refer for angiography.

items.stem: A 36-year-old man with alcohol dependence presents to the emergency department with a 5-hour history of vomiting followed by chest pain. His heart sounds are normal. There is reduced air entry at the left lung base, which is also dull to percussion, and you feel crepitus (surgical emphysema) in the neck. The ECG shows sinus tachycardia.
items.explanation: Chest pain and surgical emphysema after forceful vomiting in a drinker is Boerhaave syndrome; CT with water-soluble contrast and surgery.

items.stem: A 70-year-old man presents to the emergency department with retrosternal chest pain that is crushing in nature. This has happened on several occasions previously, and usually occurs after drinking hot fluids. Despite there being no ECG changes, he is given glyceryl trinitrate, which partially relieves the pain. After 30 minutes, the pain relieves spontaneously.
items.explanation: Crushing pain triggered by hot or cold drinks, partly relieved by GTN, with a normal ECG is diffuse oesophageal spasm.

notes: source key: F, E, B, K, G
theme: Diseases of the myocardium and pericardium

items.stem: A 23-year-old amateur footballer collapses and dies while training, with no contact from other players. He had two previous episodes of syncope at the gym for which no cause was found, and a harsh ejection systolic murmur that became louder on standing had been noted at a pre-season medical.
items.explanation: Sudden death in a young athlete with a murmur louder on standing is HOCM; screen first-degree relatives.

items.stem: A 46-year-old man presents to the GP with a history of shortness of breath that occurs on exertion and when lying down at night. On general inspection, he notices multiple spider naevi on his chest and face. On examination of his heart, the apex beat is displaced laterally and there is a pansystolic murmur that is difficult to identify since the heartbeat is irregularly irregular.
items.explanation: Heavy alcohol use with heart failure, functional MR and AF is alcoholic dilated cardiomyopathy; abstinence may reverse it.

items.stem: A 64-year-old woman is referred for echocardiography after a history of weight loss, low-grade fever, non-specific chest pain and palpitations. The echocardiogram shows a pedunculated mass in the left atrium attached to the interatrial septum.
items.explanation: A pedunculated LA mass on the septum with fever and weight loss is atrial myxoma; excise surgically.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man presents to the emergency department with stabbing central chest pain that is worse when lying down at night. Potassium is 5.4 mmol/L, sodium 145 mmol/L, urea 15 mmol/L and creatinine 540 μmol/L.
items.explanation: Positional pericarditic pain in advanced renal failure is uraemic pericarditis: start or intensify dialysis.

items.stem: A 46-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a short history of worsening shortness of breath and a reduced exercise tolerance. She has been suffering with lethargy, muscle aches, fever and palpitations for 2 weeks. Routine blood tests show a raised white blood cell count and a raised C-reactive protein. A plasma troponin returns at 1.2 ng/mL.
items.explanation: Breathlessness after a febrile viral illness with raised CRP and troponin suggests myocarditis; cardiac MRI and avoid exercise 3–6 months.

notes: source key: E, F, D, I, G

items.stem: A 76-year-old man with known ischaemic heart disease is referred for a 24-hour ECG tape after suffering occasional palpitations. The tape shows periods of sinus bradycardia followed by episodes of sinus tachycardia.
items.explanation: Alternating sinus bradycardia and tachycardia in an older patient is sick sinus syndrome; pacemaker if symptomatic.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man is noticed to have a heart rate of 110 beats/min while on the high-dependency unit following abdominal surgery. His other observations include blood pressure 146/92 mmHg, respiratory rate 14/min and oxygen saturations 99% on 2 L of oxygen via nasal cannulae. His epidural analgesia was stopped that morning, and he is complaining of abdominal pain with a severity of 8/10.
items.explanation: Tachycardia with severe pain after epidural removal is sinus tachycardia from pain; give analgesia and exclude bleeding or sepsis.

items.stem: A 75-year-old woman who suffers occasional episodes of palpitations presents to the emergency department with a painful left leg. She was previously fit and well. The leg is pale, cold and slightly mottled at presentation. The ankle-brachial pulse index is 0.3 on the left and 0.9 on the right. An ECG performed by the nursing staff is normal.
items.explanation: Embolic limb ischaemia with intermittent palpitations but a normal ECG suggests paroxysmal AF; ambulatory monitoring and anticoagulation.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a sudden collapse while gardening. He is unconscious and unresponsive, with no palpable pulse or respiratory effort. The monitor shows a disorganised, irregular, broad-complex rhythm with a fluctuating baseline.
items.explanation: Pulseless, unresponsive collapse with a chaotic, irregular broad-complex rhythm and a fluctuating baseline is ventricular fibrillation. Start CPR and defibrillate immediately.

items.stem: A 36-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with chest pain and a sensation of feeling her heart pounding. Apart from a history of schizophrenia, she has no medical problems. A heart monitor is attached and shows a broad complex tachycardia with a rate of 210 beats/min on a variable axis.
items.explanation: Antipsychotics prolong QT and cause torsades (broad tachycardia with twisting axis): IV magnesium, stop drug, defibrillate if pulseless.

items.stem: A 62-year-old man with diabetes presents to a district general hospital with sudden-onset, central, crushing chest pain that began at rest. The junior doctor on call records an ECG showing an acute inferior myocardial infarction that meets the criteria for reperfusion therapy. Which ECG change has he seen?
items.explanation: ST elevation ≥ 1 mm in two contiguous inferior leads (II, III, aVF) defines inferior STEMI, an indication for reperfusion.

items.stem: A 62-year-old diabetic man presents to a large teaching hospital with sudden-onset, central, crushing chest pain that commenced at rest. An ECG shows significant ST elevation in the inferior leads. Before the attending junior doctor can administer thrombolysis, the cardiology registrar suggests a preferable intervention.
items.explanation: Primary PCI within 120 min is preferred over fibrinolysis: better patency, fewer reinfarctions, strokes and deaths.

items.stem: A 62-year-old diabetic man presents to the district general hospital with sudden-onset, central, crushing chest pain that commenced at rest. An ECG shows significant ST elevation in the inferior leads, and the attending junior doctor considers thrombolysis. What would be considered as an absolute contraindication to thrombolysis?
items.explanation: Any previous intracranial haemorrhage is an absolute contraindication to thrombolysis (also ischaemic stroke < 6 months, active bleeding, dissection).

items.stem: A 62-year-old diabetic man presents to a large teaching hospital with sudden-onset, central, crushing chest pain that commenced at rest. He is complaining of a variety of symptoms, including pain, breathlessness, nausea and headache. Before considering management, which drug should ideally be avoided in this case?
items.explanation: Cyclizine raises SVR and LV filling pressure in MI/heart failure; use metoclopramide as the antiemetic.

items.stem: A 62-year-old man with diabetes presents to a district general hospital with sudden-onset, central, crushing chest pain that began at rest. The junior doctor starts treatment according to an evidence-based hospital protocol. Which drug, given as early as possible as a 300 mg loading dose, reduced 5-week vascular mortality after acute myocardial infarction by about a quarter in the ISIS-2 trial?
items.explanation: Aspirin cut 5-week vascular mortality by ~23% in ISIS-2 (additive to streptokinase); give 300 mg chewed at once.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man is admitted with tiredness and worsening shortness of breath. On examination, you note gynaecomastia and a midline sternotomy scar. He is subsequently found to have a normocytic anaemia with a number of red cell fragments on the blood film. Coombs’ test is negative.
items.explanation: Sternotomy scar with Coombs-negative anaemia and schistocytes is mechanical haemolysis from a prosthetic valve; echo for paravalvular leak.

items.stem: A 47-year-old woman has developed aortic stenosis in association with a degree of aortic regurgitation. She is told by her cardiologist that it is likely that she has a congenital abnormality of one of her valves.
items.explanation: Bicuspid aortic valve (1–2%) causes mixed AS/AR presenting in middle age; image the whole aorta.

items.stem: A 58-year-old man is admitted following an episode of haematemesis. He is a heavy drinker and is already under investigation for heart failure. On examination, he is found to have a murmur that is best heard at the apex and radiates into his axilla.
items.explanation: Apical pansystolic murmur to the axilla in a heavy drinker is functional MR from alcoholic dilated cardiomyopathy.

items.stem: A 35-year-old Indian woman who has known valvular heart disease as a result of rheumatic fever presents to the emergency department with chest pain. An ECG demonstrates bifid P-waves.
items.explanation: Bifid P waves (P mitrale) reflect LA enlargement, the hallmark of rheumatic mitral stenosis.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman with known primary pulmonary hypertension is admitted with a long history of abdominal pain. On examination, you find a murmur and peripheral oedema. Her liver is enlarged and tender to palpation.
items.explanation: Pulmonary hypertension causes functional TR with a pansystolic murmur, oedema and a tender congested liver.

notes: source key: F, J, H, C, G

items.stem: A 32-year-old male intravenous drug user presents with a 4-week history of fever, lethargy and weight loss. On examination, you find that he has swollen ankles and a raised jugular venous pressure. On auscultation, you notice a pansystolic murmur that is best heard over the left sternal border.
items.explanation: Tricuspid endocarditis in a drug injector is most often S. aureus; septic pulmonary emboli are common.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with a 3-week history of night sweats, weight loss and palpitations approximately 1 month after having a dental abscess removed. On auscultation, you notice a pansystolic murmur that is best heard at the apex. She had rheumatic fever as a child.
items.explanation: Subacute IE on a rheumatic mitral valve after dental work is classically viridans streptococci.

items.stem: A 64-year-old man presents to the emergency department with fever. His temperature is 40.2 °C, blood pressure 100/48 mmHg and heart rate 114 beats/min. He had a metallic aortic valve replacement 1 month ago. Transoesophageal echocardiography shows vegetations at the sewing ring, and blood cultures grow Gram-positive cocci in clusters that are coagulase negative.
items.explanation: Early prosthetic valve IE with coagulase-negative staphylococci is S. epidermidis (biofilm on the sewing ring); surgery plus vancomycin, rifampicin, gentamicin.

items.stem: A 72-year-old man with known benign prostatic hypertrophy and a past history of rheumatic fever presents to the emergency department. He was last admitted 3 weeks ago with acute urinary retention, for which he was catheterized and then taught intermittent self-catheterization. He is lethargic, feverish and has lost a stone (6 kg) in weight since his discharge. On examination, you notice a diastolic murmur and signs of left ventricular failure that were not documented on his previous admission.
items.explanation: Enterococcus faecalis IE follows genitourinary instrumentation in older men; treat with amoxicillin plus gentamicin or ceftriaxone.

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman, who was diagnosed with sigmoid carcinoma 5 years previously, presents with a 5-week history of malaise, fever, palpitations and weight loss. On examination, you notice a number of splinter haemorrhages under her fingernails. Auscultation reveals a diastolic murmur that is best heard over the second intercostal space on the left-hand side while in expiration. The murmur was not present at her last colonoscopy 2 years ago.
items.explanation: S. bovis (gallolyticus) IE is strongly linked to colorectal neoplasia; any such bacteraemia needs colonoscopy.

notes: source key: F, N, E, P, A

items.stem: A 55-year-old man presents to his GP following several episodes of central chest pain that occurred while gardening. On each occasion, the pain was relieved by rest within 5 minutes. His resting ECG, full blood count and thyroid function tests are normal. Which investigation should be requested first to diagnose the cause?
items.explanation: Typical stable angina: CT coronary angiography is first line (NICE, ESC 2024); exercise ECG is no longer used for diagnosis.

items.stem: A 67-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a 12-hour history of central chest pain that commenced at rest and radiated to both arms. She is nauseated and appears pale and sweaty. The resting ECG shows an ST depression of 1 mm in leads II, III and aVF, associated with non-specific T-wave changes. A chest X-ray is normal.
items.explanation: Rest pain with inferior ST depression is NSTE-ACS; serial high-sensitivity troponin (0/1 h or 0/3 h) separates NSTEMI from unstable angina.

items.stem: A 40-year-old female inpatient develops a red, tender swelling of her left leg 10 days after a hysterectomy. The affected leg is painful and hard to touch, and the peripheral veins appear engorged. A full blood count is unremarkable and her observations are stable.
items.explanation: Swollen tender leg 10 days after pelvic surgery is high-probability DVT (Wells ≥ 2): compression ultrasound. D-dimer is raised post-op anyway.

items.stem: A 50-year-old man with a past history of rheumatic fever becomes acutely unwell 5 days after an elective tooth extraction. On examination, he has a temperature of 38.3°C and has a pansystolic murmur that was not documented on his previous admission. Blood cultures have been sent, but the results are not yet available.
items.explanation: Suspected native-valve IE: blood cultures then transthoracic echo first; TOE if TTE negative with ongoing suspicion, prosthetic valves or abscess.

items.stem: A 56-year-old man with hypertension and ischaemic heart disease presents to his GP with almost daily episodes of palpitations. Each episode lasts approximately 1 hour and terminates spontaneously. A resting ECG performed in the practice shows no abnormalities. Routine blood tests taken a week previously were within normal limits.
items.explanation: Near-daily palpitations with a normal ECG: 24–48 h Holter monitoring; rarer episodes need an event or loop recorder.

notes: source key: F, D, K, M, L
options: Chronic left ventricular failure (NYHA class I)
Chronic left ventricular failure (NYHA class III)

items.stem: A 75-year-old man wakes from sleep feeling extremely breathless and anxious. His breathlessness resolves after a few minutes of walking around the bedroom. During the day he is comfortable at rest but becomes breathless while getting dressed or walking a few metres around the house.
items.explanation: PND and breathlessness on less than ordinary activity but comfort at rest is chronic LVF, NYHA class III.

items.stem: A 65-year-old man presents with a 6-hour history of shortness of breath and palpitations, and is coughing up pink frothy sputum. He refuses to be laid flat.
items.explanation: Pink frothy sputum and inability to lie flat is acute pulmonary oedema: sit up, oxygen, IV furosemide, nitrates if BP allows.

items.stem: A 70-year-old man with known angina, hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia is experiencing severe episodic abdominal pains. These occur approximately 30 minutes after eating. A gastroscopy and colonoscopy show no abnormalities.
items.explanation: Post-prandial abdominal pain with normal endoscopy in an arteriopath is chronic mesenteric ischaemia ('intestinal angina'); CT angiography.

items.stem: A 12-year-old girl is complaining of lethargy, fever and shortness of breath. These symptoms were initially associated with painful and swollen knee joints, which have now resolved to be replaced by a swollen elbow joint. Apart from a recent sore throat, she is otherwise fit and well.
items.explanation: Migratory large-joint arthritis, fever and carditis after a sore throat is acute rheumatic fever; ASO titre, penicillin, aspirin, prophylaxis.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman with known Addison’s disease collapsed while getting out of bed in the morning. She denies any chest pain or palpitations. She was unresponsive for 40 seconds, during which her ‘legs twitched a little’. She recovered fully after 2 minutes. This has happened on several previous occasions when standing up from a lying or sitting position.
items.explanation: Recurrent collapse on standing in Addison's disease is postural hypotension; check lying/standing BP and fludrocortisone dose.

options: Chronic left ventricular failure (NYHA class I)
Chronic left ventricular failure (NYHA class III)

notes: source key: H, D, L, J, K
options: Tenecteplase followed by intravenous heparin infusion

items.stem: A 67-year-old man presents to the emergency department with palpitations. He has known ischaemic heart disease and hypertension. On examination, he is pale and appears confused, and his hands are cool and clammy. His pulse is 160 beats/min and irregularly irregular, his blood pressure is 70/40 mmHg and his capillary refill time is 6 s.
items.explanation: Fast AF with shock is unstable: synchronised DC cardioversion (up to 3 attempts), then amiodarone if it fails.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents to her GP with a 2-day history of sharp central chest pain. The pain does not radiate and there is no associated shortness of breath. She only gains relief by sitting forward in bed at night. Examination is unremarkable, and an ECG shows widespread concave ST elevation with PR-segment depression. She has a past history of rheumatoid arthritis.
items.explanation: Pleuritic pain eased sitting forward with saddle ST elevation and PR depression is pericarditis: NSAID with PPI plus colchicine.

items.stem: A 25-year-old asthmatic man presents to the emergency department with palpitations. Examination reveals a regular heart rate of 168 beats/min. The ECG shows a regular narrow complex tachycardia with no obvious P-waves. The Valsalva manoeuvre and carotid sinus massage have failed to slow the heart rate.
items.explanation: Regular narrow tachycardia after failed vagal manoeuvres in an asthmatic: IV verapamil, as adenosine may cause bronchospasm.

items.stem: A 69-year-old man presents to a rural hospital with central chest pain radiating to his left arm that came on suddenly at rest 1 hour ago. He is nauseated, sweaty and short of breath. He had a heart attack 4 years ago, during which he received a 'clot-busting' drug that he was told never to have again. The ECG shows ST elevation of 4 mm in V2, V3 and V4. The nearest PCI-capable centre is more than 2 hours away and he has no contraindications to thrombolysis. Aspirin, clopidogrel, morphine and metoclopramide have been given so far.
items.explanation: Anterior STEMI without timely PCI: fibrinolysis with tenecteplase (not repeat streptokinase) plus heparin, then transfer for angiography.

items.stem: A 57-year-old man with known end-stage renal failure awaiting renal transplantation collapses at home with chest pain. He is brought to the emergency department attached to a cardiac monitor. The monitor shows a regular broad complex tachycardia with a rate of 230 beats/min. On examination, the carotid pulse is not palpable.
items.explanation: Pulseless broad-complex tachycardia is pulseless VT: unsynchronised shocks with CPR; correct likely hyperkalaemia.

options: Tenecteplase followed by intravenous heparin infusion

items.stem: A 60-year-old man presents with heart failure. On examination he has a collapsing pulse, an early diastolic murmur and a displaced apex beat.
items.explanation: Collapsing pulse, early diastolic murmur and displaced apex is chronic aortic regurgitation; operate once symptoms or LV dilatation appear.

items.stem: A 56-year-old man gives a history of rheumatic fever. He has flushed cheeks, an irregularly irregular pulse and a mid-diastolic murmur.
items.explanation: Rheumatic history, malar flush, AF and a mid-diastolic rumble is mitral stenosis; anticoagulate with warfarin.

items.stem: A 75-year-old woman presents to the emergency department following a sudden collapse. Her ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy. On examination, a harsh ejection systolic murmur is heard at the right upper sternal edge radiating to both carotid arteries.
items.explanation: Syncope, LVH and a harsh ejection murmur to both carotids is severe aortic stenosis; valve replacement (surgical or TAVI).

items.stem: Three days after a myocardial infarction, a 64-year-old man suddenly deteriorates with acute left ventricular failure. He has a new pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla.
items.explanation: Acute LVF with a new apical pansystolic murmur to the axilla 3 days after MI is acute MR from papillary muscle rupture.

items.stem: A baby is cyanosed at birth and has a loud, long ejection systolic murmur at the left upper sternal edge. Tetralogy of Fallot is suspected. What lesion produces the murmur?
items.explanation: In tetralogy the loud ejection murmur comes from RV outflow (pulmonary) stenosis; the large VSD is silent.

items.stem: A middle-aged man has central crushing chest pain on exertion that is relieved by rest within a few minutes.
items.explanation: Exertional crushing pain relieved by rest within minutes is stable angina; it also responds to GTN.

items.stem: A 60-year-old man has central crushing chest pain at rest for the last hour, radiating to his jaw and left arm, with sweating.
items.explanation: Crushing rest pain > 20 min radiating to jaw/arm with sweating is acute MI until proven otherwise: ECG within 10 min and troponin.

items.stem: A 65-year-old hypertensive man has sudden severe tearing chest pain radiating to his back.
items.explanation: Sudden tearing pain through to the back in a hypertensive is aortic dissection; check arm pulses, CT aortography, no thrombolysis.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman has sharp central chest discomfort with a localised tender area over the costal cartilages on palpation.
items.explanation: Localised anterior pain reproduced by pressure over the costal cartilages is costochondritis; NSAIDs.

items.stem: A 25-year-old man has sharp central chest pain that is worse on deep inspiration and lying flat, and relieved by sitting forward.
items.explanation: Pain worse on inspiration and lying flat, eased sitting forward, is acute pericarditis.

orig.answers_raw: 2. A. Angina pectoris, C. Myocardial infarction, D. Aortic dissection, H. Costochondritis, B. Pericarditis

items.stem: Used in the treatment of cardiac failure. Known to cause a persistent cough.
items.explanation: ACE inhibitors (captopril) improve HFrEF survival but cause dry cough in ~10%; switch to an ARB.

items.stem: Contraindicated in renal artery stenosis.
items.explanation: In bilateral renal artery stenosis GFR depends on angiotensin II, so ACE inhibitors can cause AKI.

items.stem: Associated with headache, flushing, reflex tachycardia and ankle swelling.
items.explanation: Dihydropyridine CCBs (nifedipine) cause headache, flushing, reflex tachycardia and ankle oedema.

items.stem: First-line management in acute coronary syndrome.
items.explanation: Aspirin 300 mg chewed is given as soon as ACS is suspected; a P2Y12 inhibitor is added.

items.stem: Specifically contraindicated in asthmatics and individuals with peripheral vascular disease.
items.explanation: Non-selective propranolol causes bronchospasm in asthma and worsens peripheral vascular disease.

orig.answers_raw: 3. E. Captopril, E. Captopril, D. Nifedipine, C. Aspirin, A. Propranolol

items.stem: A pansystolic murmur auscultated at the apex and radiating into the axilla.
items.explanation: An apical pansystolic murmur radiating to the axilla is mitral regurgitation.

items.stem: Associated with erythematous macules on the palms and haemorrhages under the nails.
items.explanation: Janeway lesions and splinter haemorrhages are vascular signs of infective endocarditis.

items.stem: Associated with pink rings with pale centres on the trunk and subcutaneous nodules over the extensor surfaces of the joints.
items.explanation: Erythema marginatum and subcutaneous nodules are major Jones criteria for acute rheumatic fever.

items.stem: Associated with a slow rising carotid pulse and ejection systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border.
items.explanation: Slow-rising carotid pulse with an ejection murmur at the right upper sternal edge is aortic stenosis.

items.stem: Known to cause a left parasternal heave and a loud pulmonary component of the second heart sound.
items.explanation: A left parasternal heave and loud P2 are signs of pulmonary hypertension; confirm with right heart catheter (mPAP > 20 mmHg).

items.stem: A 60-year-old Egyptian man with a pansystolic murmur loudest at the right sternal edge, a raised JVP and a pulsatile liver.
items.explanation: Pansystolic murmur at the lower sternal edge with giant v waves and a pulsatile liver is TR (schistosomal pulmonary hypertension in Egypt).

items.stem: A 70-year-old woman in atrial fibrillation, an apex beat palpable in the mid-axillary line and a loud pansystolic murmur which is heard all over the heart.
items.explanation: AF with an apex in the mid-axillary line and a loud pansystolic murmur is chronic severe MR.

items.stem: A 14-year-old girl with a flat occiput, single palmar crease and a pansystolic murmur. She has a chromosomal abnormality affecting chromosome 21.
items.explanation: Down syndrome is associated with AV septal and ventricular septal defects; a pansystolic murmur fits a VSD.

items.stem: An elderly gentleman with a collapsing pulse and an early diastolic murmur which is loudest when sitting forward.
items.explanation: Collapsing pulse with an early diastolic murmur loudest sitting forward is aortic regurgitation.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman with severe rheumatic mitral stenosis and pulmonary hypertension has a high-pitched early diastolic murmur at the left upper sternal edge that is louder on inspiration.
items.explanation: Graham Steell murmur: early diastolic pulmonary regurgitation from pulmonary hypertension (e.g. severe MS), louder on inspiration.

orig.answers_raw: 5. H. Tricuspid regurgitation, F. Mitral regurgita

items.stem: A patient has been on a cardiology ward for 3 weeks with a diagnosis of pulmonary oedema and is receiving large doses of furosemide. His systolic blood pressure is now 74 mmHg and rises when he is tilted head-down. He has finger clubbing, and fine end-inspiratory 'velcro' crackles are still heard throughout both lung fields.
items.explanation: Persistent velcro crackles with clubbing in a now volume-depleted patient is pulmonary fibrosis misdiagnosed as oedema; HRCT, reduce diuretic.

items.stem: A patient complains of waking in the middle of the night and racing out of bed to the window, gasping for breath.
items.explanation: Waking at night gasping and rushing to the window is paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, fairly specific for LV failure.

items.stem: A patient sleeps on four pillows at night so he can catch his breath.
items.explanation: Needing several pillows to breathe at night is orthopnoea; pillow count tracks severity.

items.stem: A patient with a diagnosis of heart failure complains of this symptom several weeks after starting an ACE inhibitor.
items.explanation: A dry cough weeks after starting an ACE inhibitor is from bradykinin; switch to an ARB after excluding pulmonary oedema.

items.stem: Congestion due to right heart failure can give the liver a 'nutmeg' appearance and cause this sign.
items.explanation: Chronic congestion in right heart failure gives a 'nutmeg' liver and tender hepatomegaly.

orig.answers_raw: 6. G. Pulmonary fibrosis, E. Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, D. Orthopnoea, B. Cough, C. Hepatomegaly

items.stem: ST depression in V1–3 and tall R wave in V1 and V2.
items.explanation: ST depression with tall R waves in V1–V3 is a posterior MI (mirror image); V7–V9 show elevation.

items.stem: Concave (saddle-shaped) ST elevation in most leads except aVR, with PR-segment depression.
items.explanation: Widespread saddle ST elevation (except aVR) with PR depression is pericarditis.

items.stem: ST elevation of 3 mm in leads II, III and aVF.
items.explanation: ST elevation in II, III and aVF is inferior MI (RCA); check V4R and watch for AV block.

items.stem: Broad QRS complexes at a regular rate of 45 beats/min; P waves are present at a faster rate but bear no relationship to the QRS complexes.
items.explanation: P waves unrelated to a slow broad escape rhythm (45/min) is third-degree heart block: pace.

items.stem: No P waves, narrow complex QRS rate of 150 beats/min with sawtooth baseline.
items.explanation: Sawtooth flutter waves with a regular rate of 150/min is atrial flutter with 2:1 block.

orig.answers_raw: 7. G. Posterior myocardial infarction, F. Pericarditis, E. Inferior myocardial infarction, D. Digitalis effect, C. Atrial flutter with 2:1 block

items.stem: A 58-year-old woman with known asymptomatic aortic stenosis presents with fever and feeling generally unwell. She has just had three fillings performed by her dentist.
items.explanation: Fever after dental work with a known stenotic aortic valve is infective endocarditis until proven otherwise.

items.stem: A 49-year-old man presents to his GP with shortness of breath on walking up hills. He also experiences central chest pain which is relieved by resting, as well as occasional dizziness. He has a loud systolic murmur.
items.explanation: Exertional dyspnoea, angina and presyncope with a loud systolic murmur at 49 is symptomatic AS (likely bicuspid): valve replacement.

items.stem: On the second day post-MI, a 71-year-old man develops pleuritic sounding chest pain. This is relieved by ibuprofen. The ECG demonstrates saddle-shaped ST changes.
items.explanation: Pleuritic pain with saddle ST changes on day 2 after MI is early fibrinous pericarditis; Dressler syndrome comes weeks later.

items.stem: A 63-year-old man presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath. He has a pansystolic murmur at the apex and a displaced apex beat. A chest X-ray shows a globular enlarged heart with a cardiothoracic ratio >50%. He admits to many years of heavy alcohol intake.
items.explanation: Heavy alcohol use with heart failure, functional MR and a globular heart is alcoholic DCM; abstinence may restore function.

items.stem: A 44-year-old woman with known COPD and a history of heavy smoking attends her respiratory clinic appointment. She now has ankle swelling and her exercise tolerance has fallen to about 15 metres.
items.explanation: Ankle oedema and severe limitation in COPD is cor pulmonale; LTOT and diuretics.

orig.answers_raw: 8. H. Infective endocarditis, B. Aortic stenosis, G. Fibrinous pericarditis, F. Dilated cardiomyopathy, E. Cor pulmonale

items.stem: A 48-year-old woman is admitted with left-sided sharp chest discomfort that is worse on coughing. She has no sputum. She takes the combined oral contraceptive pill and propranolol. Her father and uncle died in their 60s from 'heart attacks'. She smokes 30 cigarettes a day. ECG: sinus tachycardia and right bundle-branch block. D-dimer 0.71 mg/L (reference <0.5); troponin I normal. Chest X-ray: normal.
items.explanation: Pleuritic pain on the pill with tachycardia, new RBBB and raised D-dimer but normal CXR is PE; CTPA and anticoagulate meanwhile.

items.stem: A 58-year-old man with insulin-treated diabetes is admitted with intermittent central burning chest pain for the past month. It is worse after large meals and on lying flat and is eased by antacids. He has had atrial fibrillation and hypertension for 6 years and takes digoxin, atenolol, diclofenac and simvastatin. BMI 31 kg/m²; no chest wall tenderness; ejection systolic murmur in the aortic area. HbA1c 91 mmol/mol (10.5%), digoxin level 1.3 µg/L (therapeutic). ECG: rate-controlled AF with 1-mm sagging ST depression in V1–V6. An exercise stress test is negative. Chest X-ray: normal.
items.explanation: Meal- and posture-related burning pain relieved by antacids on an NSAID is GORD; the sagging ST depression is digoxin effect. Stop NSAID, start PPI.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man from Morocco attends the emergency department with a 1-week history of sharp central chest pain ('like a knife') that eases when he sits forward. There is no recent trauma. Examination is unremarkable. ECG: widespread concave ST elevation. Chest X-ray: scarring of the right apex and calcified hilar nodes. He confirms he was treated for tuberculosis in Morocco.
items.explanation: Positional pain with saddle ST elevation and previous TB with calcified hilar nodes suggests tuberculous pericarditis; echo and fluid ADA/culture.

items.stem: A 36-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with right-sided chest pain and breathlessness 2 days after falling while drunk. There is no fever. He is thin and smells of tobacco and alcohol. There is bruising and marked point tenderness over the right lateral chest wall with crepitus, and breath sounds are reduced on the right. Chest X-ray shows a small peripheral area devoid of lung markings on the right.
items.explanation: Point tenderness and crepitus after a fall are rib fractures, here complicated by a small traumatic pneumothorax; analgesia and assess size.

items.stem: A 56-year-old man with insulin-treated diabetes is admitted at the request of a relative. He has had niggling chest pain for 2 days with a feeling of breathlessness. He is apyrexial with no chest wall tenderness, clear lungs and normal heart sounds. Chest X-ray: normal. ECG: ST elevation of 3 mm in V4–V6 with T-wave inversion. Troponin I markedly raised.
items.explanation: ST elevation in V4–V6 with markedly raised troponin is an anterolateral STEMI; diabetics often have atypical pain. Reperfuse if < 12 h.

orig.answers_raw: 9. B. Pulmonary embolus, F. Oesophageal reflux disease, C. Pericarditis, E. Rib fracture, A. Myocardial infarct

items.stem: A 50-year-old man has had 90 minutes of central chest pain. His ECG shows no ST elevation, only non-specific T-wave flattening.
items.explanation: Ischaemic pain with a non-diagnostic ECG: high-sensitivity troponin at presentation and at 1–3 h to diagnose or exclude NSTEMI.

items.stem: A 70-year-old woman has fever, sharp left-sided chest pain, a pericardial friction rub and diffuse ST elevation on her ECG.
items.explanation: Fever, pleuritic chest pain, a pericardial rub and diffuse ST elevation are acute pericarditis; transthoracic echocardiography is recommended in all cases to detect an effusion or tamponade.

items.stem: A 30-year-old man has had two episodes of syncope during exercise. He has a jerky pulse and an ejection systolic murmur at the left sternal edge that becomes louder on standing and during the Valsalva manoeuvre. His brother died suddenly aged 25.
items.explanation: Exertional syncope, jerky pulse, murmur louder on Valsalva and familial sudden death suggest HCM; transthoracic echo is the key test.

items.stem: A 45-year-old smoker with exertional retrosternal chest pain recovering with rest.
items.explanation: Exertional angina in a smoker: exercise testing is the best listed option, though NICE/ESC now prefer CT coronary angiography first.

items.stem: A 15-year-old with congenital heart disease, prolonged fever, weight loss, diastolic murmur and other systemic signs.
items.explanation: Prolonged fever, weight loss and a murmur in congenital heart disease is IE: ≥ 3 blood culture sets before antibiotics.

items.stem: A patient with a thyroid goitre is found to have an ejection systolic murmur at the left upper sternal edge with wide, fixed splitting of the second heart sound. Transthoracic echocardiography is reported as normal.
items.explanation: Fixed S2 splitting with a flow murmur but normal TTE suggests an ASD missed by TTE (e.g. sinus venosus); TOE or cardiac MRI.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman develops sudden chest tightness, breathlessness and hypotension 3 days after an operation. Her ECG shows only sinus tachycardia.
items.explanation: Sudden chest tightness and hypotension after surgery is PE until proven otherwise: CTPA (bedside echo if too unstable).

options: CT angiography for the pulmonary arteries
