items.stem: A 62-year-old man has had 2 hours of crushing central chest pain. His ECG shows 3 mm ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with ST depression in I and aVL.
items.explanation: ST elevation in II, III, aVF with reciprocal I/aVL depression is inferior STEMI (RCA); record V4R and avoid nitrates if RV involved.

items.stem: A 58-year-old smoker has had 1 hour of severe central chest pain with sweating. His ECG shows 4 mm ST elevation in V1–V4 with early Q waves.
items.explanation: ST elevation V1–V4 with evolving Q waves is anterior STEMI (LAD), the worst-prognosis territory: primary PCI.

items.stem: A 66-year-old woman has 90 minutes of chest pain. Her ECG shows ST elevation in I, aVL, V5 and V6 with reciprocal ST depression in III and aVF.
items.explanation: ST elevation in I, aVL, V5–V6 with reciprocal inferior depression is lateral STEMI (circumflex or diagonal).

items.stem: A 28-year-old man has sharp central chest pain for 2 days, worse on lying flat and relieved by sitting forward, 1 week after a flu-like illness. His ECG shows concave ST elevation in I, II, aVL, aVF and V2–V6 with PR-segment depression; aVR shows ST depression.
items.explanation: Widespread concave ST elevation with PR depression after a viral illness is acute pericarditis: NSAID plus colchicine.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman who smokes has recurrent episodes of chest pain at rest in the early morning. During an episode her ECG shows ST elevation in V1–V4 that resolves completely within minutes of sublingual GTN. Troponin is normal and coronary angiography shows no significant stenosis.
items.explanation: Early-morning rest pain with transient ST elevation, normal troponin and normal coronaries is Prinzmetal angina: CCB and nitrates.

items.stem: A 65-year-old man had an anterior myocardial infarction 8 weeks ago. He now has increasing breathlessness but no chest pain. His ECG still shows Q waves with 2 mm ST elevation in V1–V4, unchanged over several weeks, and troponin is not rising.
items.explanation: Persistent ST elevation with Q waves 8 weeks after anterior MI with heart failure suggests LV aneurysm; echo confirms.

items.stem: A 1-year-old child with repeated chest infections, a continuous harsh murmur in the left infraclavicular area and bounding pulses.
items.explanation: Continuous machinery murmur below the left clavicle with bounding pulses and chest infections is PDA; device or surgical closure.

items.stem: A 55-year-old hypertensive woman has had 3 hours of central chest pain. Her ECG shows ST elevation in V1–V4, troponin is raised, and echocardiography shows anterior wall akinesia with an ejection fraction of 35%.
items.explanation: Chest pain, ST elevation, raised troponin and new anterior akinesia is acute STEMI: primary PCI, then ACEi and beta-blocker.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman who had rheumatic fever in childhood has exertional breathlessness and orthopnoea. Her pulse is irregularly irregular, the apex beat is tapping and undisplaced, and there is a low-pitched mid-diastolic murmur at the apex. Chest X-ray shows upper-lobe venous diversion, but echocardiography shows normal left ventricular function.
items.explanation: Rheumatic history with congestion, preserved LV function, AF, tapping apex and diastolic rumble is MS with AF: warfarin.

items.stem: A woman who is 8 months pregnant, with no previous heart disease, has acute breathlessness, orthopnoea, pink frothy sputum and a third heart sound.
items.explanation: New heart failure at 8 months' pregnancy without another cause is peripartum cardiomyopathy (EF < 45%).

items.stem: A 70-year-old man with recurrent syncope, slow-rising pulse, narrow pulse pressure, and an ejection systolic murmur in the aortic area.
items.explanation: Recurrent syncope with a slow-rising pulse, narrow pulse pressure and aortic ejection murmur is severe AS: valve replacement.

options: Ventricular septal defect *(keyed in some papers for PDA)*

notes: source key: 4. 1. J; 2. I; 3. F; 4. G; 5. H 1-e 2-c 3-f

items.stem: A 42-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension, 2 days after an inferior myocardial infarction, has repeated episodes of third-degree AV block with a ventricular rate of 30 beats/min and hypotension that do not respond to atropine.
items.explanation: Recurrent symptomatic complete heart block after inferior MI unresponsive to atropine needs temporary transvenous pacing.

items.stem: A 32-year-old man on the coronary care unit becomes hypotensive with a raised JVP, pulsus paradoxus, muffled heart sounds and electrical alternans on the ECG.
items.explanation: Hypotension, pulsus paradoxus, raised JVP and electrical alternans is tamponade: urgent echo-guided pericardiocentesis.

items.stem: A 46-year-old woman has sudden-onset regular palpitations at 180 beats/min. The ECG shows a regular narrow-complex tachycardia with no visible P waves. Her blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, and vagal manoeuvres have failed.
items.explanation: Stable regular narrow-complex tachycardia after failed vagal manoeuvres: IV adenosine 6, 12, then 18 mg.

items.stem: A 70-year-old man has atrial fibrillation of a few hours' duration at 140 beats/min with acute pulmonary oedema and a blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg.
items.explanation: Recent AF with pulmonary oedema and hypotension is unstable: synchronised DC cardioversion under sedation.

items.stem: A 31-year-old man with no symptoms is found to have frequent unifocal ventricular ectopics (4% of beats on Holter monitoring). Echocardiography and electrolytes are normal.
items.explanation: Frequent unifocal ectopics in an asymptomatic man with a normal heart are benign: reassure and cut caffeine and alcohol.

options: Heparin then continue warfarin for 3–6 months
DC shock (cardioversion) should be given rapidly (within ~7 minutes)
IV adenosine is the appropriate drug
Oxygen, low-molecular-weight heparin and intravenous fluids

items.stem: A 26-year-old woman taking the combined oral contraceptive pill presents with sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. SpO2 is 90% on air and blood pressure 112/70 mmHg. Her ECG (shown) shows sinus tachycardia. CT pulmonary angiography confirms pulmonary embolism.
items.explanation: Non-massive PE (hypoxaemic, normotensive) on the pill: oxygen and therapeutic LMWH; thrombolysis only if haemodynamically compromised.

items.stem: A 24-year-old man has muscle weakness and cramps after a week of profuse diarrhoea. Serum potassium is 2.4 mmol/L. His ECG (shown) shows ST depression, flattened T waves and prominent U waves.
items.explanation: Weakness after diarrhoea with ST depression, flat T and U waves is hypokalaemia: replace K⁺ (and Mg) with monitoring.

items.stem: A 34-year-old man collapses in the emergency department waiting room. He is unresponsive, not breathing normally and has no pulse. The monitor rhythm is shown.
items.explanation: Chaotic waveforms without QRS in a pulseless patient is VF: immediate defibrillation and CPR.

items.stem: A 26-year-old woman taking erythromycin and citalopram has recurrent self-terminating episodes of palpitations and near-syncope. Her resting QTc is 560 ms, and the monitor during an episode is shown (polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with a QRS axis that twists around the baseline).
items.explanation: Polymorphic VT with twisting axis on QT-prolonging drugs is torsades: IV magnesium 2 g and stop the drugs.

items.stem: A 68-year-old woman with hypertension, diabetes and treated hypothyroidism (now euthyroid) has recurrent symptomatic paroxysms of the rhythm shown. Her CHA2DS2-VASc score is 4, and a rhythm-control strategy together with stroke prevention is planned.
items.explanation: Paroxysmal AF needing rhythm control with CHA2DS2-VASc 4: an antiarrhythmic (sotalol) plus anticoagulation (DOAC preferred).

items.stem: A 74-year-old man has recurrent syncope. He takes no rate-limiting drugs, and thyroid function and electrolytes are normal. Ambulatory monitoring captures the rhythm shown, a prolonged sinus pause with no P waves, at the time of a syncopal episode.
items.explanation: A long sinus pause coinciding with syncope and no reversible cause is sinus node dysfunction: permanent pacemaker.

items.stem: A 40-year-old man complains of troublesome 'missed beats'. Echocardiography, electrolytes and thyroid function are normal. His symptoms have continued despite reassurance and stopping caffeine. His rhythm strip is shown.
items.explanation: Symptomatic benign unifocal ventricular ectopics despite reassurance and no caffeine: a beta-blocker is first line.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman has sudden-onset regular palpitations. She is haemodynamically stable, and a modified Valsalva manoeuvre has failed. Her ECG is shown.
items.explanation: Stable regular narrow-complex SVT after failed modified Valsalva: IV adenosine with ECG recording.

items.stem: Late systolic murmur with a mid-systolic click at the left 5th intercostal space.
items.explanation: Mid-systolic click then late systolic murmur at the apex is mitral valve prolapse.

items.stem: Mid-diastolic rumbling murmur with a loud S1.
items.explanation: A low-pitched rumbling mid-diastolic murmur at the apex with a loud S1 (and often an opening snap) is mitral stenosis, heard best with the bell in the left lateral position in expiration.

items.stem: A patient with a collapsing pulse and an early diastolic murmur at the left sternal edge also has a mid-diastolic rumble at the apex, with a normal first heart sound and no opening snap.
items.explanation: An apical mid-diastolic rumble with a collapsing pulse and early diastolic murmur is the Austin Flint murmur of severe AR.

items.stem: A pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal edge that increases with inspiration.
items.explanation: Pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal edge louder on inspiration (Carvallo) is tricuspid regurgitation.

items.stem: A 70-year-old man with no chest pain has a routine pre-operative ECG (shown), unchanged from 2 years ago. The QRS duration is 140 ms, with deep QS complexes and discordant ST elevation in V1–V3, left axis deviation and broad upright complexes in I and aVL.
items.explanation: Broad QRS with QS in V1–V3, discordant ST changes and left axis is old LBBB; echo for structural disease (new LBBB with pain = STEMI equivalent).

items.stem: A 60-year-old man has had 1 hour of central chest pain. He is hypotensive with clear lung fields and a raised JVP. His ECG, including right-sided chest leads (V1R–V6R), is shown: there is ST elevation in II, III and aVF (greater in III than II) with ST depression in I and aVL, and ST elevation in V4R.
items.explanation: Inferior STEMI with ST elevation in V4R, hypotension and clear lungs is RV infarction: fluids, no nitrates, primary PCI.

items.stem: A 25-year-old athlete is found to have an irregular pulse at a medical check. His ECG shows sinus P waves at a regular rate; the PR interval lengthens progressively over 3–4 beats until one P wave is not followed by a QRS complex, after which the cycle repeats.
items.explanation: Progressive PR lengthening until a dropped beat with grouped beating is Mobitz I (Wenckebach), benign in athletes.

items.stem: A 52-year-old man with alcohol dependence develops left-sided chest pain after repeated bouts of vomiting. He is sweaty, temperature 38.6 °C, pulse 126/min, BP 84/52 mmHg, with crackles and moderate dullness at the left base, a clear right lung and subcutaneous emphysema in the left supraclavicular fossa.
items.explanation: Pain and surgical emphysema after vomiting is Boerhaave rupture: left effusion with pH ~6, food particles and high amylase.

items.stem: A 72-year-old woman is admitted from a nursing home with fever and cough, and a chest X-ray shows right lower lobe pneumonia with a moderate pleural effusion. Despite vancomycin and levofloxacin she remains febrile, her breathlessness worsens and a repeat chest X-ray shows the effusion enlarging.
items.explanation: Turbid neutrophilic fluid with pH < 7.2 and very low glucose not responding to antibiotics is empyema: chest drain.

items.stem: A 52-year-old woman is admitted with abdominal pain and hypertriglyceridaemia. Her amylase is elevated and she is treated for acute pancreatitis with IV fluids and opioid analgesia. Over the next few days she becomes increasingly breathless and dullness develops at the left base.
items.explanation: Pancreatitis causes a left-sided exudate with very high pleural amylase.

items.stem: A 40-year-old construction worker has had increasing breathlessness and cough for many years. There are bilateral inspiratory crackles, and the chest X-ray shows eggshell calcification of the hilar nodes and small nodules in both upper zones.

items.explanation: Bilateral upper-lobe cavitation with sweats, weight loss and haemoptysis in a migrant is post-primary TB; isolate and send sputum.

items.stem: A 55-year-old woman who smokes heavily has a cough with small amounts of bright red blood, loss of appetite and 5.5 kg weight loss. The chest X-ray shows a solitary 3-cm pulmonary nodule with spiculated (shaggy) margins.
items.explanation: A solitary spiculated nodule with haemoptysis and weight loss in a heavy smoker is primary lung cancer until proven otherwise.

items.stem: A 38-year-old woman with hypertriglyceridaemia and severe acute pancreatitis becomes increasingly breathless and hypoxaemic, with bilateral infiltrates on chest X-ray.

items.stem: The chest X-ray of a 13-year-old boy with cystic fibrosis shows tramline and ring shadows.
items.explanation: Tramline and ring shadows are the plain-film signs of bronchiectasis, universal in CF.

items.stem: A 65-year-old dockyard worker presents with weight loss and shortness of breath. He is clubbed and cachectic. His chest radiograph shows pleural calcification and a lobulated pleural mass.
items.explanation: A lobulated pleural mass with pleural calcification in a dockyard worker is mesothelioma; pleural biopsy.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman presents with gross clubbing and progressive shortness of breath. Examination reveals fine end-inspiratory crackles. Her chest radiograph shows a ground-glass appearance of the lung.
items.explanation: Gross clubbing with fine end-inspiratory crackles and ground-glass/reticular shadowing is IPF.

items.stem: A 65-year-old smoker has breathlessness. On the chest X-ray eight anterior ribs are visible above the diaphragm in the mid-clavicular line on each side, and the diaphragms are flat.
items.explanation: More than six anterior ribs above flat diaphragms indicate hyperinflation, as in emphysema.

items.stem: A 65-year-old man with long-standing COPD presents with severe breathlessness. He has been treated with controlled oxygen, nebulised bronchodilators and steroids. An hour later, on 28% oxygen, his ABG shows PaO2 7.5 kPa, PaCO2 9.0 kPa and pH 7.26.
items.explanation: Persistent hypercapnic acidosis (pH 7.26, PaCO2 9.0) despite treatment in COPD: non-invasive ventilation.

items.stem: A 17-year-old woman presents with wheeze and marked perioral swelling after eating a peanut snack: PaO2 7.0 kPa on 28% oxygen, PaCO2 4.1 kPa.
items.explanation: Wheeze and angio-oedema after peanuts is anaphylaxis: IM adrenaline 0.5 mg and high-flow oxygen.

items.stem: A 14-year-old with asthma has an acute attack and is tiring despite nebulised bronchodilators and steroids: PaO2 10.0 kPa on 28% oxygen, PaCO2 8.0 kPa.
items.explanation: A raised PaCO2 in acute asthma is near-fatal asthma, reflecting exhaustion; the patient needs ICU for intubation and mechanical ventilation. NIV is not recommended in acute asthma.

items.stem: A 28-year-old man involved in a road traffic accident presents with severe respiratory distress. Examination reveals decreased expansion on the right side of the chest with mediastinal shift to the left.
items.explanation: Respiratory distress after trauma with mediastinal shift away from the right is right tension pneumothorax: needle decompression.

items.stem: A young man presents with sudden breathlessness. Examination reveals reduced expansion on the right; he is haemodynamically stable with SaO2 95%.
items.explanation: A stable suspected spontaneous pneumothorax needs a chest X-ray to confirm and size it before deciding management.

items.stem: A 30-year-old man with a stab wound to the right chest is breathless but haemodynamically stable; there is dullness and absent breath sounds at the right base, and the chest X-ray shows a large right haemothorax.
items.explanation: Large traumatic haemothorax: large-bore chest drain (> 1500 mL initially or 200 mL/h means thoracotomy).

items.stem: Standard therapy for community-acquired pneumococcal pneumonia not requiring hospital admission.
items.explanation: Low-severity CAP managed at home: oral amoxicillin (macrolide or doxycycline if allergic).

items.stem: A 35-year-old inpatient, admitted 10 days ago for another condition, develops severe pneumonia.
items.explanation: Late-onset severe hospital-acquired pneumonia needs antipseudomonal cover, e.g. IV ceftazidime or piperacillin–tazobactam.

items.stem: A 40-year-old builder presents with a severe community-acquired pneumonia. Atypical pathogens are suspected.
items.explanation: Severe CAP: IV beta-lactam plus macrolide (e.g. cefuroxime plus erythromycin) to cover atypicals.

items.stem: A 22-year-old man with HIV infection presents with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
items.explanation: Pneumocystis pneumonia: high-dose co-trimoxazole (IV if moderate–severe) with steroids if PaO2 < 9.3 kPa.

items.stem: A 19-year-old man contracts pneumonia with symptoms of headache, fever and dry cough. Serology shows evidence of chlamydia infection.
items.explanation: Chlamydial pneumonia is intracellular: treat with a tetracycline (doxycycline) or macrolide, not beta-lactams.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman collapses during a church service in summer. Her husband states that she turned pale and collapsed shortly after standing up. She did not jerk or lose urinary continence. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath and palpitations. She recovered after 30 seconds and now feels back to her usual self. All observations – including blood tests, ECG, and lying and standing blood pressure – are normal.
items.explanation: Brief faint with pallor on prolonged standing in a warm place, rapid recovery and normal ECG is vasovagal syncope.

items.stem: A 25-year-old man collapses suddenly while visiting his grandmother in hospital. There appears to be no pulse. The crash team is called, and manage to resuscitate him after identifying ventricular fibrillation on the cardiac monitor. The attending anaesthetist records a repeat ECG and notes that the QRS complexes are broad with slurred upstroke of the R wave.
items.explanation: A slurred QRS upstroke (delta wave) with short PR is WPW; AF conducting down the pathway can cause VF and collapse. Ablate.

items.stem: A 75-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after collapsing. On examination, her heart rate is 80 beats/min and irregular, with a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg. She has difficulty in moving her left arm and leg.
items.explanation: Collapse with AF and new left hemiparesis is a right-hemisphere stroke (cardioembolic): urgent CT before thrombolysis/thrombectomy.

items.stem: A 67-year-old man presents to the emergency department following a collapse. He has a history of ischaemic heart disease and was diagnosed with hypertension last week, when he was started on antihypertensive treatment. He felt dizzy when he got out of his chair to go to the toilet and then fainted. He regained consciousness almost immediately and had fully recovered within 5 minutes.
items.explanation: Postural syncope soon after starting an antihypertensive (e.g. doxazosin) is first-dose hypotension; start low at bedtime.

items.explanation: Haemoptysis with a monophonic wheeze and SIADH suggests small cell lung cancer.

items.stem: A 12-year-old boy is brought to the GP by his mother. Over the last couple of years he has had repeated chest infections, and his mother is worried that he is not putting on weight. On examination, there are coarse crackles throughout both lung fields.
items.explanation: Recurrent chest infections, failure to thrive and coarse crackles in a child suggest cystic fibrosis; sweat test.

items.stem: A 58-year-old builder complains of left-sided chest discomfort that has been progressing over the last fortnight. He is otherwise well. On examination, the left lower zone is dull to percussion. A pleural tap yields blood-stained fluid.
items.explanation: Progressive chest-wall pain with a blood-stained effusion in a builder is mesothelioma; pleural biopsy.

items.stem: A 53-year-old shopfitter is admitted for an elective inguinal hernia repair. A routine chest X-ray shows irregular white plaques over both lungs that cross the lobar boundaries. He feels well and auscultation is normal.
items.explanation: Holly-leaf plaques crossing lobar boundaries in an asymptomatic tradesman are calcified pleural plaques (asbestos exposure); benign.

items.stem: A 16-year-old boy presents to his GP with a 6-month history of night cough and intermittent wheeze. He has previously been well and has never had a chest infection. Examination of the chest is unremarkable.
items.explanation: Six months of nocturnal cough and intermittent wheeze in a well teenager is asthma; confirm objectively.

items.explanation: Haemoptysis, weight loss and sweats with apical consolidation is post-primary TB; isolate and send 3 sputum samples.

items.stem: A 42-year-old woman presents to the GP with a 6-month history of worsening shortness of breath associated with a dry cough. A chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.
items.explanation: BHL with dry cough and breathlessness is most often sarcoidosis.

items.stem: A 56-year-old man presents to the GP with a 6-month history of worsening shortness of breath. Examination reveals bilateral end-inspiratory crackles and clubbing. A chest X-ray shows reticulonodular shadowing, especially in the lower zones.
items.explanation: Clubbing, Velcro crackles and lower-zone reticulation is IPF; HRCT UIP pattern, antifibrotics.

items.stem: A 47-year-old man who has kept racing pigeons for many years presents to the GP with a 4-month history of worsening shortness of breath. Examination reveals bilateral end-inspiratory crackles without clubbing. A chest X-ray shows reticulonodular shadowing, especially in the upper zones.
items.explanation: Upper-zone reticulation in a pigeon keeper without clubbing is chronic extrinsic allergic alveolitis; avoid antigen.

items.stem: A 38-year-old man presents with an episode of massive haemoptysis. He says that he has had two similar episodes in the last month. He often feels short of breath, but has recently finished a course of treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis. Examination is unremarkable. A chest X-ray shows a cavitating lesion with an opaque mass within it.
items.explanation: A mass within a cavity with recurrent massive haemoptysis is an aspergilloma; Aspergillus IgG, embolise or resect.

items.stem: A 67-year-old man has a 3-day history of worsening shortness of breath. He can normally walk 100 m but now can barely get to the front door. Although he says he normally coughs up small amounts of clear sputum, he is now expectorating large amounts of greeny-yellow sputum. Auscultation reveals widespread wheeze.
items.explanation: Increased purulent sputum and breathlessness on a background of COPD is an infective exacerbation: bronchodilators, prednisolone, antibiotic.

items.stem: A 32-year-old man is stabbed in the right side of his chest. He struggles to the hospital. On arrival, he is in some respiratory distress. On examination, there is decreased air entry and hyper-resonance to percussion on the right side. The trachea is not deviated. The doctor notes the presence of a ‘sucking’ wound in the right chest.
items.explanation: A sucking chest wound with central trachea is an open (non-tension) pneumothorax: three-sided dressing, then drain away from the wound.

items.stem: A 26-year-old man presents with a 2-day history of feeling generally unwell and shortness of breath. Today, he started coughing up thick green sputum that had flecks of dry blood in. He complains of a sharp pain over the right side of his chest, which is worse on breathing in. Auscultation reveals bronchial breathing at the right base.
items.explanation: Fever, pleuritic pain and bronchial breathing at one base is pneumonia; assess with CURB-65.

items.stem: A 48-year-old woman presents with sudden-onset shortness of breath and a sharp pain on the right side of her chest. She was previously well. On examination, there is no wheeze or crackles and no areas of hyper-resonance.
items.explanation: Sudden pleuritic pain and breathlessness with a normal chest examination is PE until proven otherwise.

items.stem: A 21-year-old woman is involved in a road traffic accident. When the paramedics arrive, she has a heart rate of 122 beats/min, a respiratory rate of 32/min and a blood pressure of 86/42 mmHg. On examination, there are absent breath sounds and hyper-resonance to percussion on the left side. The trachea is deviated to the right.
items.explanation: Hyper-resonance, absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation away and shock is tension pneumothorax: decompress without waiting for X-ray.

items.stem: An 8-year-old boy presents to his GP with a 6-month history of night cough and intermittent wheeze. He has previously been well. On examination, he is small for his age and has mild eczema on his upper limbs.
items.explanation: Atopic child with nocturnal cough and wheeze: start paediatric low-dose ICS plus as-needed SABA.

items.stem: A 16-year-old boy attends the GP with poorly controlled chronic asthma. He is currently being managed with an inhaled long-acting B2-agonist and high-dose inhaled steroids. His parents want to know if there is anything else that he can be given.
items.explanation: Uncontrolled on high-dose ICS + LABA (after checking adherence and technique): add montelukast; refer if still poor.

items.stem: A 14-year-old girl attends the GP with poorly controlled chronic asthma despite good adherence and inhaler technique. She is taking an inhaled long-acting β2-agonist, a high-dose inhaled corticosteroid and montelukast. Her parents want to know if anything else can be done.
items.explanation: Uncontrolled on high-dose ICS, LABA and montelukast: lowest-dose oral steroid under specialist care; consider biologics.

items.stem: A 23-year-old man with known asthma is brought to the emergency department with shortness of breath. He has widespread wheeze, is too breathless to talk, and has a heart rate of 115 beats/min and a respiratory rate of 36/min.
items.explanation: Too breathless to talk, HR 115, RR 36 is acute severe asthma: oxygen to 94–98%, nebulised salbutamol (+ ipratropium) and steroids.

items.stem: A 21-year-old woman with known asthma is brought to the emergency department with shortness of breath. She can barely talk, has a silent chest and a respiratory rate of 36/min. Despite some improvement with oxygen, nebulised salbutamol and steroids, her peak flow is still 30% of her best.
items.explanation: Silent chest with PEF 30% despite initial treatment is life-threatening: IV magnesium 1.2–2 g and early ICU referral.

options: Oxygen via facemask and inhaled short-acting B2-agonist
Oxygen via facemask, inhaled short-acting B2-agonist and steroids
Oxygen via facemask and nebulized short-acting B2-agonist
Oxygen via facemask, nebulized short-acting B2-agonist and steroids
orig.answers_raw: 24. 1. C – Inhaled short-acting B2-agonist 2. H – Oral leukotriene receptor antagonist 3. I – Oral steroids 4. M – Oxygen via facemask, nebulized short-acting B2-agonist and steroids 5. D – Intravenous magnesium sulphate

notes: source key: 25. 1. I – Pertussis 2. H – Inhalation of foreign body 3. D – Croup 4. F – Epiglottitis 5. C – Bronchiolitis

items.stem: A 5-year-old unimmunized boy presents to the GP with a chronic cough. His mother reports that he has had this cough for 3 months. It started with a normal ‘cold and cough’, but he has not managed to shake it off. For the first 4 weeks, the cough would occur in bursts and he would get very distressed, occasionally going blue and vomiting.
items.explanation: Paroxysmal coughing with cyanosis and post-tussive vomiting for months in an unimmunised child is pertussis; macrolide and notify.

items.stem: A 2-year-old boy presents with a non-productive cough that started suddenly yesterday afternoon. He is otherwise well and has a temperature of 36.5°C. On examination, there are reduced breath sounds on the right side.
items.explanation: Sudden cough in a well afebrile toddler with unilateral reduced breath sounds is an inhaled foreign body; rigid bronchoscopy.

items.stem: An 18-month-old girl presents with a non-productive cough and stridor. The cough is described as ‘barking’ in nature. She has a temperature of 38°C and is restless. She does not appear systemically unwell and is not cyanotic, but there is a moderate stridor on exertion.
items.explanation: Barking cough and stridor with mild fever in a toddler is croup (parainfluenza); oral dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg.

items.stem: A 7-year-old boy presents to the emergency department. His mother says that he has become very unwell very quickly. It started with a high fever and a sore throat. He is now very quiet, and is drooling while sitting upright on the edge of the bed. You examine him briefly, and he appears shocked and tachypnoeic and has a very faint stridor. He has a past medical history of asthma and has never been immunized.
items.explanation: Rapid high fever, drooling, upright posture and soft stridor in an unimmunised child is epiglottitis (Hib): secure the airway, don't examine the throat.

items.stem: A 6-month-old baby presents with a cough. The illness began 4 days ago with a runny nose and a mild fever. Over the last 24 hours, he has developed a high-pitched cough associated with a wheeze. On examination, crepitations are heard throughout the lung fields.
items.explanation: Coryza progressing to cough, wheeze and widespread crackles in an infant is bronchiolitis (RSV); supportive care.

orig.answers_raw: 25. 1. I – Pertussis 2. H – Inhalation of foreign body 3. D – Croup 4. F – Epiglottitis 5. C – Bronchiolitis

notes: source key: 26. 1. A – CURB 0 pneumonia 2. F – CURB 5 pneumonia 3. G – Not a pneumonia 4. D – CURB 3 pneumonia 5. B – CURB 1 pneumonia

items.stem: A 55-year-old man presents with a cough productive of purulent sputum. A chest X-ray shows left basal consolidation. His blood pressure is 118/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 18/min and urea 5.4 mmol/L. He scores 10/10 on the Abbreviated Mental Test Score (AMTS).
items.explanation: Under 65, alert, urea ≤ 7, RR < 30 and normal BP: CURB-65 = 0, home treatment with amoxicillin.

items.stem: A 69-year-old man presents with a cough productive of purulent sputum. A chest X-ray shows left basal consolidation. His blood pressure is 86/62 mmHg, respiratory rate 34/min and urea 9.6 mmol/L. He scores 6/10 on the AMTS.
items.explanation: Confusion, urea > 7, RR ≥ 30, SBP < 90 and age ≥ 65: CURB-65 = 5, high severity.

items.stem: A 71-year-old man presents with a cough productive of purulent sputum. A chest X-ray shows no consolidation. His blood pressure is 96/68 mmHg, respiratory rate 28/min and urea 6.6 mmol/L. He scores 9/10 on the AMTS.
items.explanation: Pneumonia needs new radiological shadowing; with a clear CXR this is a lower respiratory tract infection, not pneumonia.

items.stem: A 71-year-old man presents with a cough productive of purulent sputum. A chest X-ray shows left basal consolidation. His blood pressure is 96/68 mmHg, respiratory rate 32/min and urea 8.3 mmol/L. He scores 9/10 on the AMTS.
items.explanation: Urea > 7, RR ≥ 30 and age ≥ 65 score (BP and AMTS 9 do not): CURB-65 = 3, high severity.

items.stem: A 42-year-old man presents with a cough productive of purulent sputum. A chest X-ray shows left basal consolidation. His blood pressure is 106/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 24/min and urea 7.3 mmol/L. He scores 10/10 on the AMTS.
items.explanation: Only urea > 7 scores: CURB-65 = 1, low severity, usually home treatment.

orig.answers_raw: 26. 1. A – CURB 0 pneumonia 2. F – CURB 5 pneumonia 3. G – Not a pneumonia 4. D – CURB 3 pneumonia 5. B – CURB 1 pneumonia

notes: source key: 27. G,E,B,C,D

items.stem: A 32-year-old man with known cystic fibrosis presents with shortness of breath and feels generally unwell.
items.explanation: Adults with CF are chronically colonised by Pseudomonas aeruginosa; exacerbations need two IV antipseudomonal agents.

items.stem: A Gram-negative coccobacillus that is a common cause of infective exacerbations and pneumonia in patients with COPD.
items.explanation: Haemophilus influenzae, a Gram-negative coccobacillus, is the commonest bacterium in COPD exacerbations.

items.stem: A middle-aged man presents with a cough and generalised muscle pains. He is a keen collector of rare birds.
items.explanation: Atypical pneumonia with myalgia in a bird keeper suggests psittacosis caused by Chlamydia psittaci. Serology confirms it and doxycycline is the treatment.

items.stem: A man who injects drugs presents with shortness of breath and fever.
items.explanation: Drug injectors with fever and breathlessness have S. aureus (tricuspid IE, septic emboli); blood cultures and echo.

items.stem: A middle-aged woman who has recently returned from a hotel stay in Las Vegas presents with a non-productive cough, fever and diarrhoea.
items.explanation: Dry cough, fever and diarrhoea after a hotel stay is Legionella; check sodium, LFTs and urinary antigen.

notes: source key: 28. D,A,H,B,E

items.stem: A drug associated with induction of hepatic enzymes.
items.explanation: Rifampicin is a potent hepatic enzyme inducer (reduces warfarin, pill, steroids) and turns secretions orange.

items.stem: A drug associated with blurred vision and red–green colour blindness.
items.explanation: Ethambutol causes optic neuritis with red–green colour blindness; check vision before and during treatment.

items.stem: A man who injects drugs is diagnosed with pneumonia with patchy consolidation on his chest X-ray; blood cultures grow meticillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus.
items.explanation: MSSA pneumonia in a drug injector: high-dose IV flucloxacillin (vancomycin if MRSA).

items.stem: A first-line antituberculous drug that causes hepatitis and can precipitate gout.
items.explanation: Pyrazinamide is hepatotoxic and reduces renal urate excretion, causing hyperuricaemia and gout. Isoniazid is also hepatotoxic but causes peripheral neuropathy rather than gout.

items.stem: A middle-aged woman with a recent stroke and an unsafe swallow aspirates and develops pneumonia with foul-smelling sputum. A drug with anaerobic cover is to be added to amoxicillin.
items.explanation: Metronidazole adds anaerobic cover to amoxicillin in aspiration pneumonia with foul sputum.

notes: source key: 29. E,G,D,F,A

items.stem: A 75-year-old man recently diagnosed with lung cancer complains of painful, swollen wrists and ankles.
items.explanation: Painful swollen wrists and ankles in lung cancer is hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy (periostitis, usually with clubbing).

items.stem: A middle-aged man presents with haemoptysis and pain in the shoulder radiating down the inner arm.
items.explanation: Shoulder pain down the inner arm with haemoptysis is a Pancoast tumour invading the brachial plexus (C8–T1).

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman presents with breathlessness, haemoptysis and velvety, pigmented thickening of the skin in her axillae.
items.explanation: Sudden flexural velvety pigmentation in an older adult is acanthosis nigricans, a paraneoplastic marker.

items.stem: A middle-aged woman with known lung cancer presents with drooping of the right upper eyelid, a constricted right pupil and apparent sinking of the right eye.
items.explanation: Ptosis, miosis and apparent enophthalmos is Horner syndrome from an apical tumour.

items.stem: A patient recently diagnosed with small cell lung cancer has proximal lower-limb weakness and difficulty climbing stairs. Tendon reflexes are absent but reappear after sustained muscle contraction; there is no rash.
items.explanation: Proximal weakness with reflexes returning after contraction in small cell cancer is Lambert–Eaton syndrome (anti-VGCC).

notes: source key: 30. G,F,E,A,H

items.stem: Permanent enlargement of the airspaces distal to the terminal bronchioles, with destruction of their walls.
items.explanation: Permanent enlargement of airspaces distal to the terminal bronchioles with wall destruction defines emphysema.

items.stem: A 23-year-old man presents in winter with sudden-onset fever, dry cough and muscle aches.
items.explanation: Abrupt winter fever, myalgia and dry cough is influenza; oseltamivir for at-risk patients within 48 h.

items.stem: A condition associated with a hoarse voice, barking cough and stridor.
items.explanation: Hoarseness, barking cough and stridor is laryngotracheobronchitis (croup); oral dexamethasone.

items.stem: An 18-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis has a persistent cough productive of yellow–green sputum.
items.explanation: Chronic purulent sputum in cystic fibrosis reflects bronchiectasis; physiotherapy and culture-guided antibiotics.

items.stem: A previously well middle-aged man develops a cough productive of sputum, mild chest tightness and wheeze a few days after a cold. He is afebrile, his symptoms resolve over 2–3 weeks and his chest X-ray is normal.
items.explanation: Self-limiting productive cough with transient wheeze after a cold and a normal CXR is acute bronchitis; no antibiotics.

notes: source key: 31. I,G,A,J,D

items.stem: A 68-year-old woman has progressive breathlessness, finger clubbing and fine bibasal inspiratory crackles. HRCT shows subpleural, basal reticulation with honeycombing.
items.explanation: Basal subpleural reticulation with honeycombing is a UIP pattern, diagnostic of IPF in the right setting.

items.stem: A 55-year-old farmer presenting with a cough and SOB. His CXR demonstrates fluffy nodular shadowing.
items.explanation: Cough and breathlessness with fluffy nodular shadowing in a farmer is extrinsic allergic alveolitis (farmer's lung).

items.stem: A lifelong smoker has an FEV1/FVC ratio of 62%, with an increase in FEV1 of only 60 mL (4%) after salbutamol.
items.explanation: FEV1/FVC 62% with only 60 mL (4%) reversibility in a smoker indicates COPD.

items.stem: A 23-year-old woman presents with fever, cough and shortness of breath. Her white cell count is 23 × 10^9/L and a chest X-ray shows patchy consolidation.
items.explanation: Acute fever, cough and a marked neutrophil leucocytosis with new consolidation indicate bacterial pneumonia. CURB-65 guides severity and management.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with haemoptysis. His chest X-ray shows cavitating lesions and blood tests show a positive c-ANCA (anti-PR3) antibody.
items.explanation: Cavitating nodules with haemoptysis and PR3-ANCA are granulomatosis with polyangiitis; steroids plus rituximab or cyclophosphamide.

notes: source key: 32. D,J,F,I,E

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman has tar-stained fingers, central cyanosis and widespread wheeze.
items.explanation: Heavy smoking with central cyanosis and diffuse wheeze indicates COPD (the chronic bronchitic 'blue bloater' pattern with hypoxaemia). Spirometry with FEV1/FVC below 0.7 confirms it.

items.stem: A 30-year-old man involved in a road traffic accident has bruising over the left chest and is short of breath. The left side is hyper-resonant to percussion with reduced breath sounds; the trachea is central and he is haemodynamically stable.
items.explanation: Hyper-resonance and reduced breath sounds after blunt trauma with a central trachea and stable BP is a simple pneumothorax; chest drain.

items.stem: A 55-year-old smoker with weight loss and a cough has stony dullness to percussion, reduced vocal resonance and absent breath sounds at the right base. The underlying cause is thought to be a bronchial carcinoma.
items.explanation: Stony dullness with absent breath sounds in a smoker with weight loss is a (likely malignant) pleural effusion; aspirate for cytology.

items.stem: A 24-year-old male master's student is admitted acutely short of breath for the past day. He had a similar episode during his first year at university. He returned from a summer tour of Australasia 1 week ago. His oxygen saturation is 93% on air and he is haemodynamically stable. There are reduced breath sounds on the left, with asymmetrical chest expansion and hyper-resonance. A medical student tells you that 'the lungs look different' on the chest X-ray.
items.explanation: A recurrent episode with unilateral reduced breath sounds and an asymmetric CXR is recurrent primary pneumothorax; refer for surgery.

items.stem: A 73-year-old woman who worked for many years in an asbestos textile mill is admitted breathless with mild haemoptysis. She has had three similar admissions in the last 5 months. She is thin, with finger clubbing, an increased anteroposterior chest diameter, scattered wheeze and fine bibasal crackles (right more than left). Arterial blood gas on 28% oxygen: PaO2 13.6 kPa, PaCO2 5.6 kPa. Chest X-ray: borderline cardiomegaly, blunted right costophrenic angle, chronic changes throughout and a bulky left hilum.
items.explanation: Clubbing, basal crackles and pleural disease after asbestos textile work is asbestosis; the bulky hilum needs CT for cancer.

notes: source key: 33. B,I,F

items.stem: A 55-year-old baker is admitted with increasing shortness of breath over the past 6 weeks, with exertional chest tightness and two episodes of syncope while at work. He had asthma as a child and has smoked 20 pack-years. He has a slow-rising pulse. Admission blood tests, including D-dimer, are unremarkable. Chest X-ray: no active disease. Peak expiratory flow rate 450 L/min.
items.explanation: Exertional dyspnoea, angina and syncope with a slow-rising pulse is severe aortic stenosis; normal PEF and D-dimer argue against asthma and PE.

items.stem: A 32-year-old woman has recently returned from a 2-month sabbatical in Thailand. She has been short of breath for the past week. There is reduced air entry in the right middle and lower zones and no calf swelling. Oxygen saturation 92%, D-dimer 0.45 mg/L (normal <0.5), white cell count 13.6 × 10^9/L. Chest X-ray: indistinct right heart border.
items.explanation: Loss of the right heart border with neutrophilia is right middle lobe pneumonia; a normal D-dimer makes PE unlikely.

items.stem: A 61-year-old retired plumber is admitted with increasing shortness of breath over the past 2 months, associated with mild pleuritic chest pain. He smokes 20 cigarettes a day. There is stony dullness, reduced breath sounds and reduced vocal resonance at the left base. Chest X-ray: a homogeneous opacity with a meniscus obscuring the left hemidiaphragm.
items.explanation: Stony dullness with a meniscus obscuring the hemidiaphragm is a pleural effusion; tap for cytology (cancer or mesothelioma).

notes: source key: 34. C,B,E,D,F

items.stem: A patient has been ventilated on the intensive care unit for a week after a complicated laparotomy and now has new lung infiltrates and mucopurulent secretions from the endotracheal tube.
items.explanation: Late ventilator-associated pneumonia (> 5 days) is commonly Pseudomonas; antipseudomonal therapy per local policy.

items.stem: A young, previously fit man presents acutely unwell with pneumonia and his chest radiograph shows numerous small abscesses.
items.explanation: Pneumonia with multiple small abscesses in a fit young man is S. aureus (possibly PVL); antistaphylococcal plus anti-toxin agents.

items.stem: A middle-aged man is admitted to intensive care with severe acute pneumonia. He is the second intensive care admission and the third case of pneumonia among workers at the same factory in town.
items.explanation: A cluster of severe pneumonia among workers at one site suggests Legionella from contaminated water; notify.

items.stem: A 71-year-old woman develops a chest infection 3 days after an uncomplicated resection of a Dukes A colonic carcinoma. Blood cultures and a catheter urine specimen both grow the same lactose-fermenting Gram-negative bacillus.
items.explanation: A lactose-fermenting Gram-negative bacillus in blood and urine after bowel surgery is E. coli.

items.stem: A 36-year-old woman has a 3-day history of fever, cough and pleuritic pain. She has coughed up a bit of blood in some purulent sputum. She has a pleural rub and her chest radiograph shows segmental consolidation in the left upper lobe.
items.explanation: Fever, pleuritic pain, rusty sputum and segmental consolidation in a healthy adult is pneumococcal pneumonia.

stem: A 51-year-old man with mitral valve prolapse and type 2 diabetes has had intermittent fever, night sweats and fatigue for 10 days, with mild exertional breathlessness and occasional palpitations. He recently had a dental extraction. T 38.9 °C, pulse 122/min, BP 105/65 mmHg, RR 22/min. There is a pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla and tender erythematous nodules on his fingertips. What is the most likely causative organism?
explanation: Subacute endocarditis on a prolapsing mitral valve after dental extraction is caused by oral viridans streptococci. S. aureus is acute and fulminant; S. epidermidis infects prosthetic valves.

stem: A 51-year-old man with mitral valve prolapse and type 2 diabetes has had intermittent fever, night sweats and fatigue for 10 days, with mild exertional breathlessness and occasional palpitations. He recently had a dental extraction. T 38.9 °C, pulse 122/min, BP 105/65 mmHg, RR 22/min. There is a pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla and tender erythematous nodules on his fingertips. Which of the following findings is most specific to this disease?
explanation: Only the vascular signs (splinter haemorrhages, like his Osler nodes) point specifically to endocarditis; fever, dyspnoea, tachycardia and splenomegaly are non-specific.

stem: A 51-year-old man with mitral valve prolapse and type 2 diabetes has had intermittent fever, night sweats and fatigue for 10 days, with mild exertional breathlessness and occasional palpitations. He recently had a dental extraction. T 38.9 °C, pulse 122/min, BP 105/65 mmHg, RR 22/min. There is a pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla and tender erythematous nodules on his fingertips. The initial step of management should include:
explanation: Take three sets of blood cultures, then start empirical IV antibiotics and tailor to the organism. Surgery is for heart failure, uncontrolled infection or large emboli.

stem: A 51-year-old man with mitral valve prolapse and type 2 diabetes has had intermittent fever, night sweats and fatigue for 10 days, with mild exertional breathlessness and occasional palpitations. He recently had a dental extraction. T 38.9 °C, pulse 122/min, BP 105/65 mmHg, RR 22/min. There is a pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla and tender erythematous nodules on his fingertips. Which of the following is the most serious potential complication of this disease?
explanation: Leaflet or chordal destruction causes acute regurgitation and heart failure, the commonest cause of death in IE and the main reason for urgent surgery. Pulmonary emboli come from tricuspid IE.

stem: A 71-year-old male smoker with hypertension and type 2 diabetes has noticed a pulsating abdominal mass and has had dull abdominal pain radiating to the back for 2 months. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: An expansile (pulsatile) mass with back pain in an older male smoker is an abdominal aortic aneurysm; new or persistent pain suggests expansion and needs urgent imaging.

stem: A 71-year-old male smoker with hypertension and type 2 diabetes has noticed a pulsating abdominal mass and has had dull abdominal pain radiating to the back for 2 months. What is the gold-standard diagnostic test?
explanation: Ultrasound is for screening and surveillance; CT angiography is the reference test, measuring the aneurysm, its extent and any leak, and planning EVAR or open repair.

stem: A 71-year-old male smoker with hypertension and type 2 diabetes has noticed a pulsating abdominal mass and has had dull abdominal pain radiating to the back for 2 months. He suddenly develops pain in his right leg, and the dorsalis pedis pulse is absent. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Sudden pain with a lost pulse is acute limb ischaemia, here from an embolus of mural thrombus in the aneurysm. Look for the 6 Ps (pain, pallor, pulselessness, perishing cold, paraesthesia, paralysis).

stem: A 71-year-old male smoker with hypertension and type 2 diabetes has noticed a pulsating abdominal mass and has had dull abdominal pain radiating to the back for 2 months. What is the first-line management for this complication?
explanation: Give IV unfractionated heparin at once to stop clot propagation, then revascularise (embolectomy or thrombolysis). Elevation worsens ischaemia.

stem: A 25-year-old man has exertional chest pain. His father died of a myocardial infarction at the age of 44. Fasting lipids: total cholesterol 550 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol 280 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol 35 mg/dL, triglycerides 120 mg/dL. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Very high LDL, normal triglycerides and premature coronary disease in a first-degree relative is familial hypercholesterolaemia (LDL-receptor defect).

stem: A 25-year-old man has exertional chest pain. His father died of a myocardial infarction at the age of 44. Fasting lipids: total cholesterol 550 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol 280 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol 35 mg/dL, triglycerides 120 mg/dL. If untreated, what is the most likely complication?
options: Premature coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction
explanation: Lifelong high LDL causes premature atherosclerosis and MI decades early. Pancreatitis complicates severe hypertriglyceridaemia, not high LDL.

stem: A 25-year-old man has exertional chest pain. His father died of a myocardial infarction at the age of 44. Fasting lipids: total cholesterol 550 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol 280 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol 35 mg/dL, triglycerides 120 mg/dL. What is the best initial treatment?
explanation: Start a high-intensity statin (atorvastatin 40–80 mg) with lifestyle advice; diet alone cannot correct a genetic LDL excess. Fibrates target triglycerides.

stem: A 25-year-old man has exertional chest pain. His father died of a myocardial infarction at the age of 44. Fasting lipids: total cholesterol 550 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol 280 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol 35 mg/dL, triglycerides 120 mg/dL. Despite adherence to a high-intensity statin for 3 months, his LDL cholesterol remains above target. What is the next step?
explanation: Add ezetimibe (blocks intestinal cholesterol absorption) to the statin; if LDL is still above target, add a PCSK9 inhibitor. Niacin and fish oil do not reduce events here.

stem: A 25-year-old man has exertional chest pain. His father died of a myocardial infarction at the age of 44. Fasting lipids: total cholesterol 550 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol 280 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol 35 mg/dL, triglycerides 120 mg/dL. What is the mode of inheritance of this disorder?
explanation: FH is autosomal dominant (LDLR, APOB or PCSK9 variants), so half of first-degree relatives are affected and cascade testing of the family is recommended.

stem: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a car accident. There is bruising over the right chest with paradoxical movement of a segment of the right chest wall, reduced expansion and diminished breath sounds on the right. He is conscious but in respiratory distress; BP 95/60 mmHg, SpO2 86% on air. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A segment moving paradoxically (in on inspiration) means two or more ribs broken in two or more places: a flail chest. Tension pneumothorax would shift the trachea and cause severe shock.

stem: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a car accident. There is bruising over the right chest with paradoxical movement of a segment of the right chest wall, reduced expansion and diminished breath sounds on the right. He is conscious but in respiratory distress; BP 95/60 mmHg, SpO2 86% on air. Which of the following is the main reason his lung function is compromised?
explanation: Hypoxaemia in flail chest comes mainly from the contused lung beneath the segment (alveolar haemorrhage and oedema), worsened by pain-limited breathing.

stem: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a car accident. There is bruising over the right chest with paradoxical movement of a segment of the right chest wall, reduced expansion and diminished breath sounds on the right. He is conscious but in respiratory distress; BP 95/60 mmHg, SpO2 86% on air. Chest X-ray and CT show a massive haemothorax. What is the next immediate step?
options: Needle decompression in the second intercostal space
Observation and repeat chest X-ray in 6 hours
explanation: Resuscitate and insert a large-bore chest drain. Thoracotomy is needed if >1500 mL drains at once or >200 mL/h continues for 2–4 hours; needle decompression is for tension pneumothorax.

stem: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a car accident. There is bruising over the right chest with paradoxical movement of a segment of the right chest wall, reduced expansion and diminished breath sounds on the right. He is conscious but in respiratory distress; BP 95/60 mmHg, SpO2 86% on air. His condition improves, but he remains hypoxic with persistent paradoxical chest movement despite oxygen and analgesia. What is the next definitive step?
options: External strapping of the chest wall
explanation: Respiratory failure despite oxygen and analgesia needs intubation and positive-pressure ventilation, which splints the segment internally; rib fixation suits selected patients.

stem: A 62-year-old man has had progressive breathlessness and a productive cough for 8 years, with thick whitish sputum that is worst in the morning; his symptoms have recently worsened. He has a 40 pack-year smoking history. He is cyanosed with a raised JVP and bilateral pitting ankle oedema, and coarse crackles and rhonchi are heard over both lungs. RR 22/min, BP 145/85 mmHg; PaO2 55 mmHg, PaCO2 66 mmHg, haemoglobin 18 g/dL. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Chronic bronchitis in a heavy smoker with hypoxaemia, hypercapnia, cyanosis, raised JVP and oedema is COPD complicated by cor pulmonale (right heart failure from hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction).

stem: A 62-year-old man has had progressive breathlessness and a productive cough for 8 years, with thick whitish sputum that is worst in the morning; his symptoms have recently worsened. He has a 40 pack-year smoking history. He is cyanosed with a raised JVP and bilateral pitting ankle oedema, and coarse crackles and rhonchi are heard over both lungs. RR 22/min, BP 145/85 mmHg; PaO2 55 mmHg, PaCO2 66 mmHg, haemoglobin 18 g/dL. What is the most important risk factor for this condition?
explanation: Tobacco smoking causes most COPD and stopping is the single intervention that slows FEV1 decline. Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency explains early, basal emphysema in a minority.

stem: A 62-year-old man has had progressive breathlessness and a productive cough for 8 years, with thick whitish sputum that is worst in the morning; his symptoms have recently worsened. He has a 40 pack-year smoking history. He is cyanosed with a raised JVP and bilateral pitting ankle oedema, and coarse crackles and rhonchi are heard over both lungs. RR 22/min, BP 145/85 mmHg; PaO2 55 mmHg, PaCO2 66 mmHg, haemoglobin 18 g/dL. The raised haemoglobin is most likely due to:
options: Secondary polycythaemia due to chronic hypoxia
explanation: Chronic hypoxaemia drives renal erythropoietin release, giving secondary polycythaemia; it raises viscosity and is reduced by long-term oxygen. Polycythaemia vera would have a low EPO.

stem: A 62-year-old man has had progressive breathlessness and a productive cough for 8 years, with thick whitish sputum that is worst in the morning; his symptoms have recently worsened. He has a 40 pack-year smoking history. He is cyanosed with a raised JVP and bilateral pitting ankle oedema, and coarse crackles and rhonchi are heard over both lungs. RR 22/min, BP 145/85 mmHg; PaO2 55 mmHg, PaCO2 66 mmHg, haemoglobin 18 g/dL. The raised JVP is most likely caused by:
explanation: Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction causes pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular failure (cor pulmonale), seen as a raised JVP, hepatomegaly and peripheral oedema.

stem: A 62-year-old man has had progressive breathlessness and a productive cough for 8 years, with thick whitish sputum that is worst in the morning; his symptoms have recently worsened. He has a 40 pack-year smoking history. He is cyanosed with a raised JVP and bilateral pitting ankle oedema, and coarse crackles and rhonchi are heard over both lungs. RR 22/min, BP 145/85 mmHg; PaO2 55 mmHg, PaCO2 66 mmHg, haemoglobin 18 g/dL. What is the most appropriate long-term management for this patient?
explanation: LTOT for ≥15 h/day prolongs survival when PaO2 is <7.3 kPa (55 mmHg), or <8 kPa with oedema, polycythaemia or pulmonary hypertension, once he has stopped smoking.

stem: A 24-year-old man has fever and cough productive of sputum after a recent influenza-like illness. He is unwell but alert and orientated; BP 80/60 mmHg, RR 35/min, urea 55 mg/dL (9.2 mmol/L). Chest X-ray shows multilobar consolidation with several thin-walled pneumatoceles. What is the most likely causative organism?
explanation: Necrotising pneumonia with pneumatoceles after influenza is typical of S. aureus (including PVL strains). Pneumococcus is commoner overall but rarely cavitates.

stem: A 24-year-old man has fever and cough productive of sputum after a recent influenza-like illness. He is unwell but alert and orientated; BP 80/60 mmHg, RR 35/min, urea 55 mg/dL (9.2 mmol/L). Chest X-ray shows multilobar consolidation with several thin-walled pneumatoceles. What is his CURB-65 score?
explanation: Urea >7 mmol/L (1), RR ≥30 (1) and SBP <90 mmHg (1) score; he is not confused and is under 65. CURB-65 = 3, high severity: admit and consider critical care.

notes: Recalled stem: chest X-ray with pneumatoceles was given "in one version" of the paper.
stem: A 24-year-old man has fever and cough productive of sputum after a recent influenza-like illness. He is unwell but alert and orientated; BP 80/60 mmHg, RR 35/min, urea 55 mg/dL (9.2 mmol/L). Chest X-ray shows multilobar consolidation with several thin-walled pneumatoceles. What is the best initial treatment?
explanation: Severe CAP needs a beta-lactam plus macrolide, but pneumatoceles after influenza suggest S. aureus, so add anti-MRSA cover (vancomycin or linezolid) until cultures return.

stem: An elderly man who is a heavy smoker has weight loss, haemoptysis, fatigue, constipation and thirst; he has diabetes mellitus. Chest X-ray shows a right hilar mass, and PET-CT shows no distant metastasis. What is the most likely type of lung cancer?
explanation: A central (hilar) tumour in a smoker with hypercalcaemia (thirst, constipation) is squamous cell carcinoma, which secretes PTH-related peptide. Small cell causes SIADH and ectopic ACTH instead.

stem: An elderly man who is a heavy smoker has weight loss, haemoptysis, fatigue, constipation and thirst; he has diabetes mellitus. Chest X-ray shows a right hilar mass, and PET-CT shows no distant metastasis. What is the most likely cause of his hypercalcaemia?
explanation: With no metastases on PET, hypercalcaemia is humoral: PTHrP from the squamous tumour, with a suppressed PTH. Treat with IV saline then a bisphosphonate.

stem: An elderly man who is a heavy smoker has weight loss, haemoptysis, fatigue, constipation and thirst; he has diabetes mellitus. Chest X-ray shows a right hilar mass, and PET-CT shows no distant metastasis. Lung function tests show good pulmonary reserve. What is the most appropriate management?
explanation: Non-metastatic non-small cell cancer in a patient fit for surgery (adequate FEV1/TLCO) is resected, usually by lobectomy with nodal sampling.

stem: An elderly man who is a heavy smoker has weight loss, haemoptysis, fatigue, constipation and thirst; he has diabetes mellitus. Chest X-ray shows a right hilar mass, and PET-CT shows no distant metastasis. Lung function tests show good pulmonary reserve. One year later he develops contralateral chest pain; a pleural effusion is found and aspiration confirms malignant cells. What is the best treatment to prevent recurrence of the effusion?
explanation: A symptomatic recurrent malignant effusion is drained and then controlled by talc pleurodesis (or an indwelling pleural catheter if the lung is trapped). Repeated aspiration only buys days.

stem: A patient is suspected of having pulmonary tuberculosis. How is the diagnosis confirmed?
options: Sputum acid-fast bacilli smear, culture and GeneXpert (NAAT)
explanation: Sputum for AFB smear, culture and a rapid NAAT (GeneXpert, which also detects rifampicin resistance) confirms active TB. Skin tests and IGRAs show infection only.

stem: Which antituberculous drug causes peripheral neuropathy and requires pyridoxine (vitamin B6) supplementation?
explanation: Isoniazid depletes pyridoxine and causes peripheral neuropathy, so pyridoxine is co-prescribed. Ethambutol causes optic neuritis; pyrazinamide causes gout.

stem: A man with an exacerbation of COPD has shallow breathing at 10 breaths/min. Arterial blood gases: pH 7.31, PaCO2 70 mmHg (9.3 kPa), HCO3− 33 mmol/L (reference 22–26). What is the acid–base disturbance?
explanation: Low pH with high PaCO2 is respiratory acidosis from hypoventilation (type 2 failure). The raised bicarbonate matches chronic compensation, so it is not a separate metabolic disorder.

stem: A man with an exacerbation of COPD has shallow breathing at 10 breaths/min. Arterial blood gases: pH 7.31, PaCO2 70 mmHg (9.3 kPa), HCO3− 33 mmol/L (reference 22–26). What does the raised bicarbonate indicate?
explanation: Over days the kidneys retain bicarbonate (about 3.5 mmol/L per 10 mmHg rise in PaCO2), so the high HCO3− shows chronic CO2 retention with renal compensation.

notes: The paper listed both "nicotinic acid" and "niacin" (the same drug); the second was replaced by a PCSK9 inhibitor.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man with coronary artery disease still has a high LDL cholesterol despite taking a statin. What is the next treatment?
items.explanation: With LDL above target on a maximally tolerated statin, add ezetimibe first; a PCSK9 inhibitor follows if LDL remains high.

items.stem: A 30-year-old man has isolated hypertriglyceridaemia. Which drug acts by stimulating lipoprotein lipase?
items.explanation: Fibrates activate PPAR-α, increasing lipoprotein lipase activity and lowering triglycerides by up to 50%.

items.stem: A patient with hyperlipidaemia is started on a drug that inhibits HMG-CoA reductase and can lower LDL cholesterol by up to 60%.
items.explanation: High-intensity statins (atorvastatin 40–80 mg) inhibit HMG-CoA reductase and cut LDL by about 50–60%.

notes: Recalled theme: the "snowman" scenario had no matching option in the recall, so total anomalous pulmonary venous return was added (L).

items.stem: A 4-month-old infant has cyanosis and breathlessness. The chest X-ray shows a "boot-shaped" heart.
items.explanation: A boot-shaped heart (upturned RV apex, concave pulmonary bay) with cyanosis in infancy is tetralogy of Fallot.

items.stem: A 44-year-old patient has progressive breathlessness and central cyanosis. The ECG shows right ventricular hypertrophy and the chest X-ray shows enlarged pulmonary arteries.
items.explanation: Progressive dyspnoea with RV hypertrophy and enlarged central pulmonary arteries is pulmonary hypertension; echo then right heart catheter.

items.stem: A 60-year-old smoker has chronic cough, wheeze and cyanosis. The chest X-ray shows hyperinflated lungs.
items.explanation: Chronic cough and wheeze in a smoker with hyperinflation is COPD; confirm with post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.7.

items.stem: A 30-year-old patient has a sudden fever, productive cough and cyanosis. The chest X-ray shows bilateral patchy infiltrates.
items.explanation: Acute fever and cough with bilateral patchy shadowing is bronchopneumonia; ARDS needs a precipitant and refractory hypoxaemia.

items.stem: A 6-year-old child has cyanosis. The chest X-ray shows a "snowman" (figure-of-eight) heart.
items.explanation: The snowman heart is supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous return; TGA gives an "egg on a string".

items.stem: A 65-year-old man with a mechanical mitral valve, receiving IV antibiotics for infective endocarditis, suddenly develops severe pain in his right leg while watching television. The leg is cold, pale and pulseless with loss of sensation below the knee; motor function is intact.
items.explanation: Sudden cold, pale, pulseless leg from an embolus (vegetation or valve thrombus) is acute limb ischaemia; heparin and urgent embolectomy.

items.stem: A man has bilateral buttock and thigh claudication, absent femoral pulses and erectile dysfunction.
items.explanation: Aorto-iliac occlusion gives the Leriche triad: claudication, absent femoral pulses and impotence.

items.stem: After an emergency embolectomy the patient develops increasing pain, swelling and a tense calf.
items.explanation: Reperfusion causes oedema and compartment syndrome; measure compartment pressure and perform fasciotomy.

items.stem: A 30-year-old male smoker develops ischaemia of the distal digits. He has previously had superficial thrombophlebitis.
items.explanation: Distal ischaemia with migratory thrombophlebitis in a young male smoker is thromboangiitis obliterans; stop smoking completely.

notes: Recalled stem for item 4 read "irregular pulse, unstable, HR 46"; with these options (no atropine or pacing) the intended rate is taken as 146/min.

items.stem: A patient with an acute STEMI in a rural area can be taken for PCI within 90 minutes.
items.explanation: Primary PCI is the reperfusion of choice when it can be delivered within 120 min of diagnosis (ideally <90 min).

items.stem: A patient with an acute STEMI presents to you; the nearest hospital with PCI is 3 hours away. What is the best treatment?
items.explanation: When PCI cannot be achieved within 120 min, give fibrinolysis (e.g. tenecteplase) within 10 min, then transfer for angiography.

items.stem: A patient has palpitations; the ECG shows a regular narrow-complex tachycardia (SVT) and he is haemodynamically stable.
items.explanation: Stable SVT: vagal manoeuvres first, then IV adenosine 6 mg, then 12 mg, as a rapid bolus.

items.stem: A patient has an irregular tachycardia at 146/min with hypotension and chest pain.
items.explanation: An unstable tachyarrhythmia (shock, ischaemia, syncope, heart failure) needs synchronised DC cardioversion under sedation.

notes: Option A (STEMI) was missing from the extracted list and was restored from the source page.

items.stem: A patient has typical central chest pain at rest radiating to the left arm.
items.explanation: Ischaemic pain at rest radiating to the arm is an acute coronary syndrome; of these options it is STEMI, so get an ECG within 10 min.

items.stem: A patient on long-term steroids has chest pain after meals and on lying down that is partly relieved by a proton-pump inhibitor.
items.explanation: Postprandial, positional burning pain relieved by a PPI is gastro-oesophageal reflux, aggravated by steroids.

items.stem: A patient has chest pain relieved by sitting forward; the ECG shows ST elevation with PR depression.
items.explanation: Pleuritic pain eased by leaning forward with saddle ST elevation and PR depression is acute pericarditis: NSAID plus colchicine.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman has central chest pain at rest with ST elevation on the ECG that resolves spontaneously.
items.explanation: Transient ST elevation with rest pain resolving spontaneously is coronary vasospasm (Prinzmetal); calcium-channel blockers and nitrates.

items.stem: A patient has tearing chest pain radiating to the back.
items.explanation: Tearing pain radiating to the back is aortic dissection; check both arms' BP and arrange urgent CT aortography.

items.stem: A 68-year-old diabetic smoker has chronic productive cough and progressive breathlessness; spirometry shows persistent airflow limitation. He takes empagliflozin and metformin.
items.explanation: COPD: stop smoking, then a long-acting bronchodilator (LABA, with a LAMA); his diabetes drugs do not cause cough.

items.stem: A 22-year-old woman has a chronic dry cough that is worse at night with occasional wheeze; the chest X-ray is normal and spirometry shows reversible obstruction.
items.explanation: Nocturnal cough with reversible obstruction is asthma; treatment is based on inhaled corticosteroid (ICS–formoterol per GINA).

items.stem: A 45-year-old man taking steroids for glomerulonephritis has a chronic cough that is worse after meals and on lying flat; chest examination is normal.
items.explanation: Cough after meals and when lying flat suggests reflux, made worse by steroids: give a trial of a proton-pump inhibitor.

items.stem: A 52-year-old has a chronic cough with a sensation of postnasal drip and frequent throat clearing, especially at night.
items.explanation: Upper-airway cough syndrome (postnasal drip) is treated with an antihistamine–decongestant or intranasal steroid.

items.stem: A 60-year-old hypertensive man taking ramipril has had a dry cough for 4 weeks.
items.explanation: ACE-inhibitor cough (bradykinin) settles after stopping ramipril; switch to an ARB.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman has a chronic cough with night sweats, weight loss and haemoptysis.
items.explanation: Night sweats, weight loss and haemoptysis suggest pulmonary TB: confirm on sputum, then 6 months of RIPE therapy.

items.stem: A 65-year-old man has a dry cough and exertional breathlessness with fine inspiratory crackles and finger clubbing.
items.explanation: Dry cough, Velcro crackles and clubbing suggest IPF; after HRCT confirmation, give an antifibrotic (pirfenidone or nintedanib).

items.stem: A 58-year-old man who works in a cement factory has a chronic cough; the chest X-ray shows diffuse nodular opacities.
items.explanation: Dust-related pneumoconiosis (e.g. silicosis) has no specific drug treatment; remove him from exposure.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman has acute fever, cough with purulent sputum, pleuritic chest pain and bronchial breathing.
items.explanation: Lobar pneumonia: assess CURB-65 and start antibiotics (amoxicillin for low severity).

items.stem: A 72-year-old woman coughs when lying flat and has frothy sputum, bilateral basal crackles and ankle swelling.
items.explanation: Orthopnoea, frothy sputum, basal crackles and oedema mean heart failure: give a loop diuretic.
